pages.text: More machines are requiring bigger structures to run, and constantly placing them manually is getting tiring, so I have created a simple assembly program to inject into the multiblock controller. Set the multiblock controller down, use the $(item)Structure Assembler$() on it, and it builds every missing block, bottom-up, with Inferface port (if available) in my inventory (free in creative).

Lesson learned: $(thing)sneak-use$() first for a dry run. Sparks mark the gaps, and I get a shopping list that counts what I already carry.$(br2)The assembler never breaks blocks - anything in the way is marked, for me to clear myself.

$(thing)Taking a structure apart$(): sneak-use the assembler in the air to switch it to disassemble mode (it glints while it is in it). Use it on a controller, then again within five seconds to confirm: every block of the structure's pattern - casings, ports, coils, glass, the controller last - comes back to your inventory, and anything that does not fit lands at your feet. Blocks that are not part of the pattern are never touched. Sneak-use on a controller in this mode lists what you would get back.
On a $(thing)tower of variable height$() (the Gas Centrifuge Cascade), using the assembler on a finished structure builds one more stage on top.
Use on a multiblock controller to build every missing block from your inventory. Sneak-use to preview what is missing.$(br2)Made in the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

An Extreme Assembly Table that fully runs by itself. Push the ingredients of one craft in from any side - an AE2 $(thing)Pattern Provider$() with a processing pattern, pipes, hoppers - and it finds the Extreme recipe they make, lays them out itself and crafts. The result waits in its output; pull it out from any side.

Every Extreme recipe works, including the ones that follow the game (the Omniscience Catalyst, singularity clusters, specimen bundles, the Compendium and the Harvest). Those are matched by exactly what was delivered, so give their patterns blocking mode. Use the block to see what it is doing.
The big machines are not single blocks but assemblies of $(thing)functional components$(), each with its own crafting chain. Everything is required for the machine to run, none can be left behind.

The parts list reads like a CERN inventory: magnets, RF cavities, beam pipes, cryogenics, vacuum pumps, detectors, injectors, lenses, anchors, stabilisers and more. In reality, dipole magnets bend a beam, RF cavities kick it faster, and cryogenics keep superconductors below their critical temperature.

$(thing)Coils$() come in five tiers: Superconducting, Chronosteel, Spacetime Alloy, Cosmic Neutronium and Transfinite. Like a chain and its weakest link, a structure counts only its $(thing)lowest$() coil. Each tier above the first adds 25% speed, and some recipes need a minimum tier (JEI shows it).

$(thing)Field Emitters$() come in three tiers. The lowest emitter tier multiplies how many parallels the tuning panel allows.$(br2)The $(item)Structure Assembler$() places the best tier I carry; in creative, hold the tier you want in your off-hand. Mixing tiers works, but only the lowest counts.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Use on a multiblock controller to build every missing block from your inventory. Sneak-use to preview what is missing.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Spacetime Alloy Coil Block$(): Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block$(li)$(item)Graviton Field Emitter$(): Axiomatic Field Emitter, Chronal Field Projector, Dimensional Lift Projector, Empirical Notes I, Graviton Field Projector and more$(li)$(item)Dipole Bending Magnet$(): Antiproton Decelerator, Hyperion Synchrotron, Particle Spectrometer

A bucket is a cup with a handle. It cannot hold a plasma at a hundred million kelvin, a superfluid near absolute zero, or a liquid that is really a law of physics. It is still normal iron after all, and has its limits.

An $(item)Empty Containment Cell$(), which is specifically designed for this purpose, can. Right-click a source block of any Theoretical Sciences fluid to fill it, or click a machine tank with it. Pour it out, feed it to a tank, or use it in a recipe, and you get the empty cell back.$(br2)Ordinary water and lava still go in ordinary buckets. Some fluids are resistant to placement, likely bounded by some unknown law that I do not understand.

What keeps a bucket out keeps you out too. $(thing)Hot$() liquids (500 K and up) burn like lava, harder the hotter they are, and destroy anything dropped in them - past 2,000 K not even fire resistance or netherite helps. $(thing)Cold$() ones (200 K and below) freeze like powder snow, faster the colder they are; leather keeps out all but the coldest. $(thing)Exotic$() ones - a false vacuum, liquid spacetime, the broths and reagents - twist whoever wades in with harmful effects.
A magnetically sealed flask for fluids too hot, too cold or too strange for a bucket. Scoop a source block or fill it from a tank.$(br2)Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Empty Containment Cell$(): Anomaly Containment Ward, Antihydrogen, Empty Containment Cell

A multiblock whose containment reaches zero does not simply stop. What it was holding gets out - and what gets out depends on the machine. I have catalogued five kinds after multiple containment failures for records.

$(li)$(thing)Reality Destabilisation$() (colliders, reactors, forges, crucibles): a blast, and the surrounding world starts to come apart. Blocks become $(thing)Fractured Reality$(): they fade in and out and split into smaller copies of themselves, spreading slowly before reality heals.

Anything alive suffers too. Creatures caught in Fractured Reality glitch and splinter like the shadows of higher-dimensional bodies, hit harder and move faster. Villagers and zombies become $(thing)Destabilised Husks$(). Keep anyone far, far away from such machines.

$(li)$(thing)Spatial$() (singularities, wormholes, universe forging): a $(thing)rupture$() grows for ten seconds, drags everything in, eats the terrain and detonates. $(thing)Void Wraiths$() - tiny living black and white holes - crawl out, and burst like a creeper when they collapse. Definitely make sure these machines never fail or there will be more bills for  expensive repair.

$(li)$(thing)Infectious$() (Matrioshka Brain, Reality Compiler, Assembly Line): flying $(thing)Nanite Swarms$() escape. They split when destroyed, down to single units, and any creature that dies infected bursts into a new swarm. Grey goo, in other words - the old nanotech nightmare, given wings. Never have any living be nearby or these can get out of hand.

$(li)$(thing)Temporal$() (Causality Loop Engine): $(thing)Paradox Echoes$() - walking clockwork, one for every player nearby - that rewind themselves when hurt. The least dangerous type of containment failure, yet by no means harmless.$(li)$(thing)Dimensional$() (Rift, Tesseract, Breach, Omnilex): a rupture plus $(thing)Law Wraiths$(), broken laws of nature shaped like tesseracts. Higher Dimension objects are very hard to handle, so it is best to study well on how to spot them in our 3D space.

Note to self: overclocked machines fail harder. Keep containment up with a $(item)Field Calibrator$(), or install an $(item)Autonomous Calibrator$().$(br2)For server owners: the consequences or the block damage can be disabled in the config, and block damage also respects the $(thing)mobGriefing$() game rule.

A splinter of reality that broke away from a destabilised creature. It is in several places at once.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chronon Field Inverter$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Destabilised Husk.
What is left of a Void Wraith: a little pocket of nothing that refuses to be filled.$(br2)Made in $(item)Dark Matter Halo Collector$().
Use on a multiblock controller to restore its containment, clear a fault and read out the ideal tuning value.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

Can be installed on a multiblock: it follows the drifting tuning and repairs containment by itself, for a 25% power tax.$(br2)Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$(). There are better versions of this as I expand my knowledge more.

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Fractured Essence$(): Contained Anomaly Specimen, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Integer Ring, Strange Matter Pellet, Warm Helium and more$(li)$(item)Void Essence$(): Contained Anomaly Specimen, Dark Matter Lens, Empty Set$(li)$(item)Field Calibrator$(): Autonomous Calibrator, Phase-Locked Stabiliser$(li)$(item)Autonomous Calibrator$(): Predictive Lattice Governor, Theoretical Notes I
$(thing)Destabilised Husk$(). Only appears in a Containment Failure event involving Reality Distortion.$(br)Drops: Fractured Essence, Rotten Flesh, Strange Matter Pellet.
$(thing)Void Wraith$(). Only appears in a Containment Failure event involving Spatial Distruption.$(br)Drops: Void Essence, Void Lattice Shard, Exotic Matter Crystal.
$(thing)Nanite Swarm$(). Only appears in a Containment Failure involving nanobots and computerised machinery.$(br)Drops: Nanite Swarm, Quantum Dot.
$(thing)Law Wraith$(). Only appears in a Containment Failure involving Higher Dimensions.$(br)Drops: Crystallised Law, Axiom Fragment.

Machines now hold at least twenty seconds of whatever their recipe draws, and take power as fast as it is delivered. $(item)Energy Cells$() store it: every face takes energy in, the marked face sends it out.
$(li)Casimir: 4 billion FE, 16 M FE/t$(li)Vacuum: 256 billion, 512 M FE/t$(li)Singularity: 16 trillion, 2.1 billion FE/t$(li)Omnium: effectively bottomless$(br2)Cells keep their charge when broken.

$(item)Entangled Relays$() and $(item)Transceivers$() sit on a block's face. Tune several to one channel with an $(item)Entanglement Tuner$(): senders pull items, fluids and energy out of what they sit on and receivers push it in - instantly, at any distance, even between dimensions.
Relay: 256 items, 64,000 mB and 64 M FE per tick. Transceiver: 8,192 items, 4,096,000 mB and 2.1 billion FE per tick. Sneak-use with the tuner to switch sending/receiving.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Links Entangled Transceivers to one channel. Sneak-use a transceiver to switch it between sending and receiving.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Casimir Energy Cell$(): Vacuum Energy Cell$(li)$(item)Entangled Relay$(): Entangled Transceiver

The first thing to make: a $(item)crafting table$() ringed with iron and copper. The $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() is a 9x9 crafting grid - and a crafting table too: anything laid out within three by three that it has no recipe for is crafted as at an ordinary table.

Every one of this mod's own recipes that would be made at a crafting table is made here instead - and fills the whole 9x9 grid: what used to be one ingredient in a 3x3 recipe is now a block of nine. Storage blocks are not packed from ingots: each is woven from its ingots and many of the mod's other resources of the same stage, and none can be taken apart again. Decorative blocks keep their small recipes. JEI shows every pattern.

Collections: the $(item)Biosphere Compendium$() and the $(item)Primordial Harvest$() want one of every meat and drop, or every crop, seed, fruit and flower, of every mod installed. Gather each mod's into its $(item)Specimen Bundle$() here first (with an egg, or bone meal); if there are too many bundles, nine at a time are bound into an $(item)Archive$().
Some recipes only run in the right conditions around the controller - heavy gravity, extra dimensions, slowed or hastened time, an altered vacuum. JEI marks them with a diamond.

Some dimensions supply conditions by nature: the Bulk has 5 dimensions, the Transfinite Hierarchy 7, Hyperdimensional Reality 11; inside a black hole gravity is 1000 g and time runs at 1%; the Foam's vacuum is false. Anywhere else, $(item)Field Projectors$() can create such conditions within 16 blocks of placement.

Right-click a projector to step its setting up, sneak to step down; it needs power to hold the field. $(item)Graviton$(): 0.01 to 1000 g. $(item)Dimensional Lift$(): 4 to 11 dimensions. $(item)Chronal$(): time x0.01 to x100. $(item)Vacuum State$(): Casimir, false, true vacuum.

Fields act on you too. High gravity crushes ($(item)Graviton Harness$()), extra dimensions bleed you ($(item)Brane Tether$()), altered time slows or ages you ($(item)Chronal Anchor$()) and an altered vacuum decays you ($(item)Coherence Stabiliser$()). Prepare before you walk into your own factory.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Spreads crushing gravity evenly through you. Carry it into high-gravity fields.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Holds your own clock steady. Carry it into fields where time runs fast or slow.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Ties your mass to our brane. Carry it in the Bulk - or in any field of extra dimensions.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Keeps your wavefunction in one piece. Carry it in the Quantum Foam - or in an altered vacuum.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

$(l)Welcome$(). This Codex is your guide to Theoretical Sciences. The gold-marked nodes in this column are the $(thing)Getting Started$() steps: read them from the top down. Later steps open by themselves as you reach them (a padlock says what opens it), and every chapter of the map to the right opens with the step that explains it.

$(l)Using the Codex$()$(li)$(thing)Drag$() the map (or arrow keys) to move it, $(thing)mouse wheel$() to zoom, $(thing)Fit$() (F) shows the whole map, $(thing)Centre$() (C) comes back here.$(li)$(thing)Hover$() a node: everything it links to lights up.$(li)$(thing)Click$() a node to read it; highlighted names in the text are links. $(li)$(thing)Search$() (bottom right, or Ctrl+F) looks through every page you have unlocked.$(li)The tabs along the top sort the same entries by branch: Physics, Materials, Machines...

$(l)Two shortcuts$()$(li)$(thing)Sneak + use$() the Codex opens the $(thing)Research Tree$() (so does the $(thing)Research$() button at the bottom left).$(li)In any inventory, hover an item of this mod and press $(thing)K$() (changeable in Controls): the Codex opens at its page, with every way to make it.$(br2)The $(thing)Next steps$() button lists the research you can start right now and the guide steps you have not read yet.
Lost your Codex? It is crafted in an ordinary crafting table: $(item)Book$(), $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$().

Everything in this mod begins with $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(). It grows as $(item)Deepslate Cherenkov Quartz Ore$() deep underground, Y -64 to 0 in the deepslate layer, in long thin veins; the ore glows faintly blue, so look along cave walls. Mine it with an $(thing)iron pickaxe$() or better.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Deepslate Cherenkov Quartz Ore in the Overworld.

Also found: 2-8 at a time in the supply caches of $(l:world/ruins)Observatory Ruins$(/l) - crashed research domes on the Overworld surface, which also hold Neutronium, a Spectral Analyzer or a spare Codex. Be wary as these ruins may hold some unpleasant surprise, explaining why it is the state it is now.$(br2)Holding $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() once teaches the research symbol $(thing)ħ$() (reduced Planck constant) - the derivation of $(thing)Quantum Foundations$() and $(thing)The Casimir Effect$() needs it. Collect a few dozen: the first machines use it by the nine.

Your first block, made in an ordinary crafting table: 4 $(item)Iron Ingots$(), 4 $(item)Copper Ingots$(), $(item)Crafting Table$().$(br2)The $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() is a $(thing)9x9$() crafting grid, and a normal crafting table as well.

$(l)The 9x9 rule$(): almost every recipe of this mod is made here, filling the whole 9x9 grid - what would be one ingredient in a 3x3 recipe is a $(thing)3x3 block of nine$() of it. So "a furnace in the middle" means nine furnaces in the middle block. Only the Codex itself and this table are made in a normal 3x3 crafting grid (and decorative blocks in a stonecutter).$(br2)The recipe pages of every entry draw the full 9x9 pattern; JEI or EMI show it too.

Machines run on $(thing)FE (Future Energy)$(). The first generator needs nothing exotic: the $(item)Thermoelectric Generator$(), on the Extreme Assembly Table from 36 $(item)Iron Ingot$(), 9 $(item)Copper Block$(), 18 $(item)Redstone$(), 9 $(item)Furnace$(), 9 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(). No research needed.

It burns ordinary fuel:$(li)$(item)Charcoal$(): 48 FE/t for 80 s$(li)$(item)Coal$(): 48 FE/t for 80 s$(li)$(item)Dried Kelp Block$(): 24 FE/t for 200 s$(li)$(item)Blaze Rod$(): 96 FE/t for 120 s$(li)$(item)Coal Block$(): 432 FE/t for 80 s$(li)$(item)Nuclear Waste Glass$(): 32 FE/t for 1200 s$(li)$(item)Polonium-210 Source$(): 96 FE/t for 600 s$(li)$(item)Protostellar Ember$(): 128 FE/t for 800 s$(br2)It pushes its power into the blocks touching it, so set your first machine right beside it (or use any cable mod: every machine takes and gives FE on every side). Feed it with a hopper or pipe to keep it going.

Nearly every machine is built from $(item)Neutronium Ingot$() - and a lot of it (the first few machines take well over a hundred). Where it comes from:$(li)$(thing)The End$(): $(item)Degenerate Matter Ore$() in End stone (Y 10 to 80), needs a $(thing)diamond pickaxe$(). Smelt the $(item)Degenerate Matter Chunk$() it drops in a furnace (20 s; 10 s in a blast furnace) - one chunk, one ingot. This is the main source early on.$(li)$(thing)Observatory Ruins$() on the Overworld surface: 1-4 ingots in a cache.$(li)$(thing)Anomaly Vaults$(): half-sunk containment vaults, 2-8 ingots per chest - but the anomaly engine inside keeps spawning creatures.

Later, once you have the Casimir Vacuum Press (step 9), you can make Degenerate Matter at home: 128 $(item)Cobbled Deepslate$() + 16 $(item)Obsidian$() → 1 $(item)Degenerate Matter Chunk$() (2,048 FE/t, 30 s).$(br2)Holding $(item)Degenerate Matter Chunk$() once teaches the research symbol $(thing)∫ f dx$() (integral) - the derivation of $(thing)The Casimir Effect$() and $(thing)Precision Lithography$() needs it.

$(item)Dilithium Ore$() grows in the Nether's netherrack, Y 10 to 110; an $(thing)iron pickaxe$() mines it into $(item)Dilithium Crystal$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilithium Ore in the Nether.

You need it early:$(li)Holding $(item)Dilithium Crystal$() once teaches the research symbols $(thing)∂²f/∂x²$() (second partial derivative) and $(thing)∂f/∂x$() (partial derivative) - the derivation of $(thing)Quantum Foundations$() needs them. $(li)It goes into $(item)Neutronium Plates$() (step 9), which most later parts are made of.$(br2)While you are in the Nether: blazes and ghasts are worth observing with the Spectral Analyzer (next step), and the Nether sky is worth Insight too.

Research is paid for in $(thing)Insight$(), and Insight comes from observing things with the $(item)Spectral Analyzer$(): on the Extreme Assembly Table from 9 $(item)Amethyst Shard$(), 27 $(item)Neutronium Ingot$(), 9 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() (or found in Observatory Ruins).

Every $(thing)new$() observation counts once:$(li)$(thing)Sneak + use$() it in the air: the sky of the dimension you are in - 8 Insight each for the Overworld, the Nether, the End and every other world.$(li)Use it on unusual blocks - amethyst clusters, budding amethyst, obsidian, crying obsidian, magma, glowstone, spawners, enchanting tables, beacons, sculk... - 3 each.$(li)On creatures - endermen, blazes, ghasts, phantoms, shulkers, wardens... - 6 each.$(li)On a $(thing)running$() machine of this mod: 4, or 12 for a multiblock.
The first research, $(thing)Quantum Foundations$(), costs only 5 Insight: observing the Overworld sky is enough. Later, machines running $(thing)thought experiments$() make Insight without end.

$(thing)Sneak + use the Codex$() to open the Research Tree (or press the Research button here, or use a Research Terminal block - you do not need one).$(br2)Machines refuse recipes you have not researched, and many entries of this Codex have research pre-requisites too.

Each research shows what it builds on, its $(thing)Insight$() price and sometimes items it uses up. Most end in a $(thing)derivation$(): the situation is described, and you lay out the real equation from symbol tiles, then use it to compute a number from the given values (each world has its own numbers). Hints can be bought with Insight. The $(thing)Book of Symbols$() in the tree explains every tile and how to learn it.

$(l)Your first: Quantum Foundations$() - 5 Insight, no items. The derivation is the time-dependent Schrödinger equation. Its derivation uses symbols you learn by $(thing)holding an item$() once: $(thing)ħ$() (reduced Planck constant) from $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(); $(thing)∂²f/∂x²$() (second partial derivative) from $(item)Dilithium Crystal$(); $(thing)∂f/∂x$() (partial derivative) from $(item)Dilithium Crystal$(). With the tiles learned, build the equation, then compute the electron's de Broglie wavelength from the given numbers.

With Quantum Foundations done, research $(thing)The Casimir Effect$() next: 5 Insight and 4 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(). Its derivation uses symbols you learn by $(thing)holding an item$() once: $(thing)ħ$() (reduced Planck constant) from $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(); $(thing)∫ f dx$() (integral) from $(item)Degenerate Matter Chunk$(). It unlocks the recipes of the Casimir Vacuum Press and the Zero-Point Energy Extractor.

Meanwhile, make $(item)Spacetime Casings$() - the frame of most machines - on the Extreme Assembly Table: 36 $(item)Neutronium Ingot$(), 36 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(), 9 $(item)Ender Pearl$() (makes 4). The rings of Observatory Ruins are made of them too: a pickaxe takes them.

Your first real machine. On the Extreme Assembly Table: 45 $(item)Neutronium Ingot$(), 9 $(item)Piston$(), 18 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(), 9 $(item)Spacetime Casing$(). Place it next to the Thermoelectric Generator.

What it makes first:$(li)4 $(item)Neutronium Ingot$() + 8 $(item)Raw Pitchblende$() → 1 $(item)Neutronium Plate$() (64 FE/t, 5 s)$(li)128 $(item)Cobbled Deepslate$() + 16 $(item)Obsidian$() → 1 $(item)Degenerate Matter Chunk$() (2,048 FE/t, 30 s) - renewable Neutronium.$(li)8 $(item)Neutronium Plate$() + 4 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() + 4 $(item)Theodolite Lens$() → 1 $(item)Casimir Plate$() (128 FE/t, 10 s)$(li)4 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() + 4 $(item)Glowstone Dust$() + 4 $(item)Magnetite$() → 4 $(item)Quantum Dot$() (96 FE/t, 8 s)$(br2)Place the ingredients in its slots (or pipe them in); its screen shows progress and what is missing. Its own entry lists everything else it makes.

More power: the $(item)Zero-Point Energy Extractor$(), on the Extreme Assembly Table from 36 $(item)Casimir Plate$(), 9 $(item)Neutronium Plate$(), 9 $(item)Spacetime Casing$(), 27 $(item)Neutronium Ingot$().

It draws power from the vacuum itself, using up a catalyst:$(li)$(item)Casimir Plate$(): 64 FE/t for 120 s$(li)$(item)Metamaterial Sheet$(): 256 FE/t for 120 s$(li)$(item)Exotic Matter Crystal$(): 2,048 FE/t for 300 s$(li)$(item)Spin Foam Lattice$(): 8,192 FE/t for 300 s$(br2)Like every generator it pushes power into the blocks it touches. Keep the Thermoelectric Generator for the small jobs.

From here the research tree branches. The next research open to you:$(li)$(thing)Magnetostatics$() (8 Insight, 4 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$()): A steady current makes a magnetic field that circles the wire and weakens with distance from it. The first study of electromagnetism. Unlocks the Gauss Meter.$(li)$(thing)Number Systems$() (10 Insight, 8 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$()): Zero, and "the next one". From two rules, all of arithmetic. Unlocks the Peano Arithmetic Engine.$(li)$(thing)Observational Astronomy$() (8 Insight, 4 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$()): Everything known about the sky came through a lens. A bigger mirror gathers more light and splits finer detail - up to the limit that the wave nature of light itself sets. Unlocks the Telescope Mirror Blank.$(li)$(thing)Quantum Entanglement$() (5 Insight, 4 $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$()): Spooky action at a distance, put to work. Unlocks qubits and the Quantum Entangler.$(li)$(thing)Radioactivity$() (10 Insight, 4 $(item)Raw Pitchblende$()): Some nuclei are unstable and fall apart on their own, at random, but at a rate fixed for each kind. Half of any sample is gone after its half-life, whatever you do to it. Unlocks Radium Salt, the Geiger Tube and Counter, and the Prussian Blue Tablet. $(item)It is recommended to be careful with this branch as it can contaminate your world$()!$(li)$(thing)Cryogenics$() (10 Insight, 2 $(item)Neutronium Plate$()): Near absolute zero, most properties become meaningless. Unlocks Superfluids and Bose-Einstein condensates.

$(thing)Precision Lithography$() matters early: its Lattice Growth Vat grows Cherenkov Quartz from ordinary quartz and amethyst, so you stop depending on ore. $(thing)Quantum Entanglement$() gives the Quantum Entangler, whose $(thing)thought experiment$() turns materials into Insight - the renewable way to pay for research.$(br2)Every machine's entry on the map says what it makes; machines need their own research before they run.
The big machines are $(thing)multiblocks$(): a controller block plus casings and glass around it. One of your first will be the $(item)Tesla Coil$() ($(thing)Resonant Circuits$()).

How to build one:$(li)Open the machine's entry: its $(thing)Structure$() page shows the build layer by layer, with the blocks needed.$(li)Place the controller, then use a $(item)Structure Assembler$() on it - it places every missing block from your inventory. $(thing)Sneak + use$() first for a dry run and a shopping list. $(li)If you have $(item)Interface Port$() in your inventory, it will be added to the multiblock automatically.$(li)Multiblocks works differently from single block machines; They have special parameters that needs to be fulfil to run, you can see them under the Readout section in the GUI screen. Use the Controls and feed Coolant to ensure all parameters are met.$(li)Some multiblocks require specific conditions for the machine to run, for those you can use $(item)Projected Fields $()to create an altered localised bubble to allow the machines to run. All these are written in JEI/EMI.$(li)Running multiblocks drift and wear: their tuning panel and stabilisers keep them safe - a containment failure is dangerous.

Structure Assembler: 18 $(item)Block of Cherenkov Quartz$(), 9 $(item)Ender Pearl$(), 18 $(item)Neutronium Ingot$().$(br2)Interface Port: 36 $(item)Neutronium Ingot$(), 9 $(item)Hopper$(), 18 $(item)Bucket$(), 9 $(item)Spacetime Casing$(), 9 $(item)Redstone$() (makes 2).

That is the beginning. The rest of the $(thing)Discovery$() map runs left to right in the order things are met, each chapter linked to what it builds on; locked chapters show as $(thing)$()??? until their research is done. The other tabs sort the same pages by branch (Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics), by world (Dimensions) and by kind (Materials, Creatures, Machines).

Habits that help:$(li)Press $(thing)K$() over any item in an inventory to see how it is made.$(li)Check $(thing)Next steps$() whenever you have new Insight.$(li)Every tier has a thought experiment for Insight: build each tier's thinking machine.$(li)Storage blocks are woven, not packed: they cannot be taken apart again, so don't craft them unless absolutely necessary.

Science starts with observation of the world around. I used a $(item)Spectral Analyzer$() on unusual blocks (beacons, end portal frames, amethyst, sculk, Cherenkov ore...), on Endermen and Wardens, and on $(thing)running$() Theoretical Sciences machines to gather understanding of this world.

Every $(thing)new$() observation grants $(thing)Insight$(). Sneak-use the analyzer to observe the sky of the dimension you are in - splitting starlight into a spectrum is how astronomers first learned what stars are made of.$(br2)Multiblocks are worth the most; A running machine that puts theories into practice, allows one to learn more.
Right-click on phenomena, blocks or creatures to gain Insight.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Spectral Analyzer$(): Resonance Probe

With Applied Energistics 2 installed, an $(item)Interface Port$() of a formed multiblock connects to ME cables (it needs a channel). The multiblock then takes recipe ingredients - items and fluids - straight from the network, after whatever is in its own slots, and puts everything it makes into the network.
Every machine slot and tank holds as much as the game can count (2,147,483,647).

pages.title: Akashic Record
pages.text: Everything that has ever been known, written once. Creative mode only.
$(thing)Creative mode only$(). Every research entry and every symbol of the Book of Symbols, learned at once. It cannot be crafted and the Core refuse to make it.

pages.title: Casimir Plate
pages.text: Two conducting plates held nanometres apart. Between them only short vacuum modes fit, so the empty space outside pushes harder than the empty space inside, and the plates are drawn together by nothing at all. Holding the pair, I can feel them straining toward each other.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)To test the Casimir effect properly I needed plates flatter than atoms. Neutronium plate, spaced with slivers of Cherenkov Quartz, made it in the press, and the attraction matched the prediction to the last digit.

Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Observatory Ruin chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Casimir Effect.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bose-Einstein Condenser, Casimir Energy Cell, Chemical Reactor, Cryocooler Unit, Empirical Notes III, False Vacuum Membrane, Femtoscale Capacitor, Foam Substrate and more.

pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block
pages.text: A coil of cosmic neutronium over spacetime alloy, cooled cryogenically and threaded with pentaquark shards. It runs hotter than anything below it and seems to pull faintly on the room. The windings are so dense that they barely look like separate turns.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Transcendent Plasma Forge demanded hotter coils still. I wound cosmic neutronium over a spacetime alloy coil, with a hyperdimensional processor to handle the load and pentaquark shards to stabilise it.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Component Tiers.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Transcendent Plasma Forge, Transfinite Coil Block.

pages.title: Degenerate Matter Chunk
pages.text: Matter so compressed that its electrons are packed into every available quantum state, held up only by the Pauli exclusion principle. It is the remains of white dwarf cores, and a lump the size of a walnut weighs more than I could ever carry. It is faintly warm, utterly rigid, and refuses to be scratched by anything I own.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Degenerate Matter Ore in the End.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Letting a Pocket Universe run overly long in the Universe Forge, I found its first stars had already lived and died. Sifting the remains, I pulled out the cinders of their cores: electron-degenerate, still dense enough to dent the forge tray.

Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Degenerate Matter Ore$(), in veins through the End.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Casimir Effect.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Block of Neutronium, Bounce Core, Liquid Metallic Hydrogen, Neutrino Flux, Protostar Core, Sterile Neutrino, Strange Matter, Strange Matter Pellet and more.

pages.title: Destabilised Husk
pages.text: $(thing)Destabilised Husk$(). Only appears in a Containtment Failure event involving Reality Distortion.$(br)Drops: Fractured Essence, Rotten Flesh, Strange Matter Pellet.

pages.title: Empirical Dossier
pages.text: A thick binder of my earliest discoveries - every measurement, every failed run, every note in the margin - bound and sealed in superfluid-cooled pages. Read by a machine, it is a curriculum. Read by me, it is mostly embarrassment and nostalgia in roughly equal parts.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Teaching a machine to study meant giving it something to study. I gathered the three volumes of my empirical notes and preserved them in superfluid helium, so the Research Nexus could read them as I once did - only faster. I have found copies in anomaly vaults too.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Research Synthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Theoretical Dossier.

pages.title: Empirical Notes I
pages.text: A sheaf of first-hand observations from the hardest experiments of my early work: time's arrow, a kugelblitz forming, gravitons, a stellar core, a monopole. The handwriting gets worse as the experiments get stranger. Every page smells faintly of ozone.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)When I first tried to teach a machine to study, I realised my raw notes were scattered across every lab. Pressing an arrow of time shard, a kugelblitz seed, a magnetic monopole and their kin into the Femtoscale line made them into a record a machine could read.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Research Synthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Dossier.

pages.title: Empirical Notes II
pages.text: The second third of my empirical record: psionic crystals, attosecond capacitors, strange and charm quarks, quaternions and the complex plane, tachyon klystrons. It is the most chaotic volume, the one where physics and mathematics start to bleed into each other on the page.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Assembling the second volume showed me how much of my early work was really mathematics in disguise. A quaternion crystal and the complex plane sat beside quarks and a tachyon klystron, and the Femtoscale line wove them into one coherent set of notes.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Research Synthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Dossier.

pages.title: Empirical Notes III
pages.text: The final third of the early record: gravitational lensing, all six quark flavours, spacetime lattices, fractals, neurons built of light. It ends abruptly, mid-thought, where I stopped measuring and started theorising. The last page is mostly arrows.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Bottom and top quarks next to up and down, a Minkowski lattice beside a fractal set, a gravitic lens element and a photonic neuron - closing the empirical record meant gathering the pieces that bridged particles, geometry and minds.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Research Synthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Dossier.

pages.title: Entanglement Tuner
pages.text: A slim instrument with a dial that sets which entangled channel a transceiver listens on. Entanglement cannot carry a message by itself, but it can share a key and a correlation; the tuner makes two devices agree on which pair of photons they share. It clicks softly between settings.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)My transceivers kept pairing with whichever partner was nearest. I mounted an entangled photon pair and a quantum dot on a neutronium plate as a reference, so every device I tune shares the same correlated source and stays on one channel.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Casimir Effect.

pages.title: Equilibrium Lattice
pages.text: Forged with Omnipotence: An eternal law that says this machine does not change, and thus the machine resists all other attempts to change.
The fourth and perfect stabiliser: a multiblock holding it never drifts, never wears, never quenches and never faults.
Forged at the reborn Core's $(item)Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnipotence Core.

pages.title: Gene Sampler
pages.text: A slim needle on a neutronium handle, tipped with a quantum dot that reads base pairs as it draws them. One quick touch takes a genome sample. Touch a creature from another dimension and the dot reads something that is not DNA at all.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed a way to copy a creature's blueprint without harming it. A quantum dot on a stick, backed by neutronium so it would not flex, was enough to read a genome on contact. The first creature I sampled barely noticed.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Casimir Effect.

pages.title: Graviton Field Emitter
pages.text: A field emitter upgraded with a graviton crystal and a gravitic lens element, so it projects gravity as well as fields. It weighs more on one side than the other, thus that side changes. Dust drifts toward its face and settles in slow rings.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Better emitters let a multiblock run more parallels. I added a graviton crystal and a gravitic lens to a field emitter, with a hyperdimensional processor and hyperon crystal to shape the field. It projected gravity cleanly.

Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Component Tiers.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiomatic Field Emitter, Chronal Field Projector, Dimensional Lift Projector, Empirical Notes I, Graviton Field Projector, Vacuum State Projector.

pages.title: Laplace's Demon
pages.text: An intellect that knows every force and every position. Shown a machine, it knows exactly how the machine must be run.

$(thing)Creative mode only$(). Use it on a multiblock controller: it tunes the machine for the recipe its inputs match (or hold a recipe's product in your off hand to choose one) - every control, the coolant, containment and drift. For pack makers and testers.

pages.title: Law Wraith
pages.text: $(thing)Law Wraith$(). Only appears in a Containtment Failure involving Higher Dimensions.$(br)Drops: Crystallised Law, Axiom Fragment, Blaze Rod.

pages.title: Nanite Swarm
pages.text: $(thing)Nanite Swarm$(). Only appears in a Containtment Failure involving nanobots and computerised machinery.$(br)Drops: Nanite Swarm, Quantum Dot.

pages.title: Paradox Echo
pages.text: A figure forever meeting its own past. It acts out the grandfather paradox, flickering whenever its history stops adding up.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Paradox Residue, Chronon Capacitor, Closed Timelike Curve.

pages.title: Phase-Locked Stabiliser
pages.text: Locks a multiblock's fields to a reference oscillator. Drift comes slower and smaller.
Made in $(item)Nanite Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Field Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Adaptive Feedback Core.

pages.title: Quantum Dot
pages.text: A nanocrystal small enough that its electrons are confined like those of a single atom, so it behaves as an artificial atom with tunable energy levels. Smaller dots glow blue, larger ones red: the colour is written by the size alone. A pinch of them looks like coloured sand that shines under any light.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Nanite Swarm.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pressing Glowstone Dust against Cherenkov Quartz in the Casimir Vacuum Press shattered the dust into grains only nanometres across. Their glow had shifted colour by size, which told me the electrons were now trapped as in an atom.

Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Nanite Swarm.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Crashed Satellite, Observatory, Observatory Ruin chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Casimir Effect.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bose-Einstein Condensate, Chiral Crystal, Dilaton Crystal, Entangled Relay, Entanglement Tuner, Femto Fabricator, Femtoscale Transistor, Field Emitter and more.

pages.title: Geodesy
pages.text: $(thing)Geodesy$()$(br2)Measure one baseline and two angles and every other distance follows - that is how countries were mapped, triangle by triangle. Geodesy measures the planet itself. Unlocks the Theodolite Lens, the Geoid Model and the Geodetic Surveyor.

$(thing)Insight$(): 10$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Cartography, Number Systems.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Surveyors measure one side c of a triangle and the angles at both its ends; the third angle γ follows. Write the length a of the side opposite the angle α.

pages.title: Vacuum Energy Storage
pages.text: $(thing)Vacuum Energy Storage$()$(br2)Store energy in the difference between two vacua. Unlocks the Energy Cells.

$(thing)Insight$(): 15$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): The Casimir Effect, Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Casimir Plate.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the energy released when a volume V of false vacuum relaxes to the true vacuum.

pages.title: Specimen Bundle
pages.text: One of everything a mod's world grows or leaves behind, sealed in glass.

One for each mod: one of every meat and drop (with an egg) or every crop, seed, fruit and flower (with bone meal) that mod has, gathered on the Extreme Assembly Table. Too many bundles are bound nine at a time into an Archive. The Biosphere Compendium and the Primordial Harvest want them all.

pages.title: Void Wraith
pages.text: $(thing)Void Wraith$(). Lives in: nowhere natural.$(br)Drops: Void Essence, Void Lattice Shard, Exotic Matter Crystal.

Housekeeping. All my machines use standard $(thing)FE$() and expose items, fluids and energy on every side, so any pipe, cable or storage mod works. Inputs can be inserted; outputs can be extracted. Universally it works the same as RF for all other known systems.

Fluids move the same way: pipes, AE2 import/export buses, storage buses and pattern providers can all fill input tanks and drain output tanks.$(br2)Multiblocks talk to the outside world through $(item)Interface Ports$() placed in the marked positions - and one port is enough for items, fluids and energy alike.

Working by hand: right-click a machine with a bucket or a $(item)Containment Cell$(), or click a tank in its screen while holding one. Containment Cells are proper fluid containers, so tanks, pipes and AE2 can fill and empty them too. A good thing to have - some of what I bottle should never touch a bucket.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

Every multiblock (except generators) takes $(thing)16$() kinds of item and $(thing)16$() fluids at once, and gives up to 4 of each; the smaller machines take a few more than they used to. Recipes are built to fill them: each needs many materials from all over the mod, in quantities that grow steeply with the machine's tier.

The $(item)Engineering Components$() - from the Coherent Wiring Harness (tier 1) to the Omnilex Seal (tier 8) - are the standard parts: each tier's recipes use its own and the one before. Each is made in a machine of its tier from that tier's plate and processor.

Some recipes also ask for materials from other mods in your pack (Mekanism, AE2, GregTech, Draconic Evolution, Botania, Malum, Astral Sorcery...). These appear only if that mod is installed. JEI always shows exactly what is needed.
Pack makers: the common config $(thing)recipeIngredientMultiplier$() scales every machine recipe's inputs (then /reload); KubeJS or a datapack can edit or replace any recipe.
I set up a $(item)Research Terminal$() to keep my thinking in order: it opens the research tree. Each node costs Insight and sometimes materials, and needs its prerequisites.

Machines refuse to run recipes I have not researched - a machine checks the research of whoever placed it.$(br2)For pack makers: this can be turned off in the config, entries can be edited in $(thing)data/*/ts_research$(), and research can be granted with $(thing)/theoreticalsciences research grant$().
Handy trick: sneak-use this Codex to open the research tree from anywhere. I no longer need to walk back to the terminal every time an idea strikes.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Research Terminal$(): Research Nexus

Later research is not bought - it is studied. Once paid for, an entry takes real time: minutes at first, hours near the end. You can study one thing at a time; the Research Terminal shows how long is left.
A $(item)Research Nexus$() studies in your place. Feed it $(item)Research Dossiers$() while you study and each one cuts the wait: Empirical 2 min, Theoretical 5, Unified 10, Absolute 20.

A dossier must be at least as advanced as the entry: $(thing)Empirical$() up to 150 Insight, $(thing)Theoretical$() up to 400, $(thing)Unified$() up to 1000, $(thing)Absolute$() beyond. Each is assembled from three sets of Notes, and those from a broad sample of everything you have researched before - a test of your whole production line.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Every early discovery, written up. A Research Nexus can study it in your place.$(br2)Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Empirical Dossier$(): Theoretical Dossier

Every multiblock drifts: its ideal setting (or, for the physics machines, the disturbance it fights) wanders while it runs, and its containment wears. A $(item)Stabiliser$() used on the controller reduces the frequency of drifting.

$(li)$(item)Phase-Locked Stabiliser$(): 40% less drift, 1.5x longer between drift steps, 30% less wear and damage.$(li)$(item)Adaptive Feedback Core$(): 65% less drift, 2.5x longer between steps, 55% less wear.$(li)$(item)Predictive Lattice Governor$(): 88% less drift, 4x longer between steps, 80% less wear.

Only one perfect stabiliser exists: the $(item)Equilibrium Lattice$(), forged at the rebuilt Omnipotence Core. A machine holding it never drifts, never wears, never quenches and never faults - set it once and leave it. A better stabiliser replaces a lesser one, and the old one is handed back.

Every research ends in a derivation: the situation is described, and the full relation is laid out in real notation with a box for every symbol. Fill them all from your tiles; the order inside a sum or product does not matter.
The law is never named until you have derived it. Then its name appears, and you must use it - to compute a number from given values.

Tiles are $(thing)symbols$(), and you only have the ones you have learned. Each is learned by holding a particular item, or by finishing a particular research. The $(thing)Book of Symbols$() (in the research tree and in every derivation) explains what each one means and how to learn it.

pages.title: Thermoelectric Generator
pages.text: A furnace wrapped in thermocouples: the heat of ordinary fuel, turned straight into current by the Seebeck effect. Humble - and the first power any laboratory has.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Burns $(item)coal$(), $(item)charcoal$(), $(item)coal blocks$(), $(item)blaze rods$() and $(item)dried kelp blocks$() for power - no research needed. Enough to run the Casimir Vacuum Press and build the Zero-Point Energy Extractor.
$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (1 item and 0 fluid inputs, 0 and 0 outputs).
Made in a crafting grid.
Research costs $(thing)Insight$(). Observing new machines, blocks, creatures and skies with the Spectral Analyzer gives some, once each - not nearly enough for everything.

Every tier has a $(item)thought experiment$(): a recipe in one of its machines that uses up materials and gives the machine's owner Insight each time it finishes - 10 in the Quantum Entangler, 25 in the Neural Synthesizer, 60 in the Holographic Encoder, 120 in the Graviton Condenser, 300 in the Matrioshka Brain, 500 in the Cantor Diagonalizer and 800 in the Axiom Distiller. The owner gets it even when away. JEI shows the Insight beside the recipe.

Multiblocks are not set-and-forget. Each has a $(thing)tuning panel$() beside its screen with its own control: the Collider's $(thing)Beam Focus$(), the Crucible's $(thing)Plasma Temperature$(), the Omnilex's $(thing)Law Coherence$().

The ideal setting $(thing)drifts$() while the machine runs, each machine its own way: some wander, some swing back and forth, some steadily fall, some sit still then suddenly jump. Match it to keep $(thing)efficiency$() high.

$(thing)Overclock$() doubles speed but quadruples power draw - a square law, like resistive heating. $(thing)Parallel$() runs several recipes per cycle. Generators cannot overclock; tuning sets their output instead.

$(thing)Containment$() wears down while running - faster when overclocked or out of tune. At zero the machine $(thing)faults$(): work in progress is lost and it stops. A $(item)Field Calibrator$() used on the controller restores it. It also reveals the ideal setting, marked in gold on the panel.

Much later: an $(item)Autonomous Calibrator$() can be installed into a controller. From then on the machine follows its own drift and repairs itself, for a 25% power tax and 10% less generator output. Worth every joule.$(br2)Pack makers can slow or disable drift and wear in the config.
Use on a multiblock controller to restore its containment, clear a fault and read out the ideal tuning value.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Installs into a multiblock controller for good: it follows the drifting tuning and repairs containment by itself, for a 25% power tax.$(br2)Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Field Calibrator$(): Autonomous Calibrator, Phase-Locked Stabiliser$(li)$(item)Autonomous Calibrator$(): Predictive Lattice Governor, Theoretical Notes I

Every research question gives its values up front, with the question. They are not the same in every world: each world draws its own (from its seed), so the answers cannot be shared or looked up - only worked out.
Constants of nature - the speed of light, Planck's constant, the gravitational constant and the rest - are the same everywhere. Server owners can turn this off (puzzleValuesPerWorld).

pages.title: Zero-Point Energy Extractor
pages.text: Even empty space jitters. This machine $(thing)generates power$() from vacuum fluctuations, burning Casimir plates and exotic matter as catalysts.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

Textbook physics says the vacuum's ground state cannot be mined - there is nothing lower to fall to. But the Casimir effect is real: plates set close together feel a measurable push. The $(item)Zero-Point Energy Extractor$() leans on that, with Casimir plates and exotic matter as catalysts. And it does generate power.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.
$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (1 item and 0 fluid inputs, 0 and 0 outputs).
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

A tumour is not one enemy but a population of competing clones, each with its own mutations and its own fitness f_i. A clone gains share only when it beats the average: dx_i/dt = x_i(f_i − Σx_j f_j). Every treatment changes the fitness - and so it selects whichever clones it happens not to kill.

That is how $(thing)drug resistance$() arises: a resistant cell one in a thousand, with an advantage of s = 0.5 per day under treatment, is 96% of the tumour twenty days later. It was there before the drug - the drug chose it due to the natural selection process. Hence combination therapy: a clone resistant to two independent drugs at once is rarer by the product of their odds.
In the $(item)Evolution Engine$(), metastatic spores, an immortal line and an enzyme under selection leave a $(item)Resistant Clone Colony$().
The cells that survived the last treatment - and so the ones that make the next tumour. Selection, not malice.$(br2)Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Resistant Clone Colony$(): Apoptosis Trigger, Contagion Network Map, Renormalised Essence, Stem Cell Culture$(li)$(item)Evolution Engine$(): Abiogenesis Crucible

Containment is not destruction: you must keep the anomaly alive to study it. A unit that makes new ones at rate β, and is cleared naturally (γ) or by quarantine (q), makes R_e = ∫β e^{−(γ+q)τ}dτ = β/(γ + q) in its life. Quarantine works by pushing R_e below 1 - every outbreak then dies out - and the minimum field is q = β − γ.

The protocols, from the clinic and the high-containment lab: $(li)isolate - one specimen, one cell, sealed$(li)reduce contact (q) without starving the sample$(li)watch R, not the count$(li)never study what you cannot destroy. The Containment Ward's console is exactly this: hold R below 1, close to it for the fastest work.
In the Ward: stabiliser matrices, causal shielding, a defect core and a contagion map become $(item)Quarantine Field Matrices$().
A field that clears an anomaly faster than it can copy itself. It does not destroy anything - it only keeps R below one.$(br2)Made in $(item)Anomaly Containment Ward$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Quarantine Field Matrix$(): Reality Anchor, Resolved Anomaly

pages.title: Anomaly Containment Ward
pages.text: A quarantine cell of chronoplastic walls, causal shielding and windows of containment glass, with dimensional stabilisers at every corner. It lets what it holds grow - just slower than its field can clear it.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 5$() machine.
This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

Turns what containment failures leave behind - $(item)Fractured Essence$(), $(item)Void Essence$(), $(item)Paradox Residue$(), $(item)Nanite Swarms$(), $(item)Law Crystals$() - into $(item)Contained Anomaly Specimens$(), and later grows $(item)Local Law Violations$(), $(item)Symbiont Cultures$(), the $(item)Anomaly Catalogue$() and $(item)Quarantine Field Matrices$(). Keep R = β/(γ + q) below 1.

pages.title: Anomaly Containment Ward
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Anomaly Catalogue, Contained Anomaly Specimen, Local Law Violation, Quarantine Field Matrix, Symbiont Culture.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

A splinter of reality that broke away from a destabilised creature. It is in several places at once.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chronon Field Inverter$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Destabilised Husk.
What is left of a Void Wraith: a little pocket of nothing that refuses to be filled.$(br2)Made in $(item)Dark Matter Halo Collector$().
What is left after a contradiction resolves itself.$(br2)Made in $(item)Causality Loop Engine$().
A billion machines the size of viruses. Hungry.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nanite Assembler$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Fractured Essence$(): Contained Anomaly Specimen, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Integer Ring, Strange Matter Pellet, Warm Helium and more.$(li)$(item)Void Essence$(): Contained Anomaly Specimen, Dark Matter Lens, Empty Set$(li)$(item)Paradox Residue$(): Absolute Notes I, Axiom Fragment, Bootstrap Artifact, Closed Timelike Curve, Contained Anomaly Specimen and more.$(li)$(item)Nanite Swarm: $()Contained Anomaly Specimen, Xenobot Swarm, Nanite Slurry and more.

Between hosts, an infection is a bookkeeping process. Split a population into susceptible S, infected I and recovered: dI/dt = βSI/N − (γ + μ)I. At the start everyone is susceptible, and the infection grows only if each case makes more than one more: $(thing)R₀ = β/(γ + μ) > 1$(). Once a fraction 1 − 1/R₀ is immune, it can no longer spread.

That threshold is a $(thing)phase transition$(). Let each link of a network pass the infection with probability T: below a critical T, outbreaks stay small; above it a giant connected cluster appears and the infection $(thing)percolates$() through the whole population - like water through ground coffee, or a magnet ordering below its Curie point. On networks with hubs the critical T can be very small.
In the $(item)Holographic Encoder$(), a replicator, a resistant clone and a holographic matrix write the $(item)Contagion Network Map$(): every path an anomaly can take, and where R crosses 1.
Every contact, every transmission, every node an infection passed through. Somewhere in it is the threshold where R crosses 1.$(br2)Made in $(item)Holographic Encoder$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Contagion Network Map$(): Anomaly Catalogue, CAR-T Cell Culture, Quarantine Field Matrix

The body destroys anomalous cells all the time. A tumour exists because it escaped detection. $(thing)Immune evasion$(): it sheds the markers T cells look for, shows PD-L1 to switch them off, and recruits cells that suppress inflammation. $(thing)Immortality$(): every division shortens the telomeres at the chromosome ends until a cell must stop - unless it switches $(thing)telomerase$() back on.

$(thing)Angiogenesis$(): beyond a millimetre it starves of oxygen, so it calls in new blood vessels (VEGF). Even then it slows: a tumour grows as N = K·exp(ln(N₀/K)e^{−αt}), fast when small and levelling off at the capacity of its supply. $(thing)Metastasis$(): cancer cells loosen their grip (the epithelial-mesenchymal transition), enter the bloodstream, survive the journey and grow again elsewhere. Most die; but it only takes one to recreate another tumour.

In the $(item)Bioreactor$(): a strain culture with a telomerase complex becomes an $(item)Immortal Cell Line$() - and an immortal line in broth is passaged into twelve, forever. In the $(item)Evolution Engine$(): an immortal line and a silicon spore in xenoplasm make $(item)Metastatic Spores$().
Telomerase switched back on: the chromosome ends rebuild themselves, and the cells forget how to grow old. They have outlived their donor.$(br2)Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().

A cluster of cells that has learned to leave the original tumour: to slip through its tissue, ride through bloodstreams and grow again somewhere it was never meant to be.$(br2)Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Immortal Cell Line$(): Anomaly Catalogue, Immortal Cell Line, Metastatic Spore, Resistant Clone Colony$(li)$(item)Metastatic Spore$(): Resistant Clone Colony, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid$(li)$(item)Bioreactor$(): Gene Sequencer$(li)$(item)Evolution Engine$(): Abiogenesis Crucible

What can an anomaly do? The catalogue so far:$(li)break a symmetry and stay broken (defects)$(li)make itself from its surroundings (autocatalysis, prions)$(li)override the rules of its host (oncogenesis)$(li)defy prediction (chaos, undecidability)$(li)copy itself and escape (replicators, metastasis)$(li)evolve resistance$(li)spread through a population$(li)break a conservation law locally

How big do they get? Sizes of tumours, outbreaks, earthquakes, forest fires and ruptures follow $(thing)power laws$(), p(s) ∝ s^{−τ}: most are tiny, a few are enormous, and nothing sets a typical size. The mean is s₀(τ − 1)/(τ − 2) - and for τ ≤ 2 it is infinite: the largest anomaly you will ever meet outweighs all the others together. Systems tuned to the edge of a phase transition do this by themselves (self-organised criticality).

Every science keeps a drawer of things that should not happen. Physics has defects and law violations through Black Holes, chemistry has molecules that self-propagates in the form of prions, biology has cancer, mathematics has indivisible numbers. $(thing)Abnormality & Infection$() studies them together, because they behave alike: they $(thing)arise$() from a broken rule, $(thing)replicate$(), $(thing)escape$() what should destroy them, and $(thing)change$() the normal world they live in.

You have met them already. A failing multiblock leaks them: $(thing)Fractured Reality$() spreads block to block like an infection of a higher-dimensional shadow, Nanite Swarms turn their hosts into new swarms, Husks, Void Wraiths, Paradox Echoes and Law Wraiths crawl out. What they leave - $(item)Fractured Essence$(), $(item)Void Essence$(), $(item)Paradox Residue$(), $(item)Nanite Swarms$(), $(item)Law Crystals$() - is the field sample.

Build the $(item)Anomaly Containment Ward$(). It turns each of those drops, with a stabiliser matrix or causal shielding, into sixteen $(item)Contained Anomaly Specimens$() - the raw material of the whole branch. Its Operation console is an epidemic: the specimen grows at β, the ward clears it at γ + q, and R = β/(γ + q) must stay below 1. The faster it grows (just below 1), the more there is to study.

Is it anomalous at all? Normal noise scatters as a Gaussian. A deviation of kσ happens by chance with probability ≈ √(2/π)e^{−k²/2}/k: one in 1.7 million at five sigma - the threshold at which physics believes a discovery. The branch runs in six stages: $(li)Origin$(li)Replication & escape$(li)The systems behind it$(li)Interaction with normality$(li)Extent$(li)Containment, study, isolation - and resolution.

In quantum field theory an $(thing)anomaly$() is a technical word: a symmetry that holds in the classical theory and fails in the quantum one. The chiral charge of massless fermions should be conserved; in parallel electric and magnetic fields it is created from the vacuum at the rate e²E·B/2π² per unit volume. This $(thing)anomaly$() is real - it makes the neutral pion decay into two photons, and it is measured in crystals today.

So normality can be broken locally, by exactly calculable amounts, without the rest of physics falling apart: the theory stays consistent because the anomalies of different particles cancel; Whereas defect core touches ordinary space, such violations leak out.

pages.text: In chemistry an anomaly begins as $(thing)autocatalysis$(): a product that speeds up its own making. Its concentration does not rise steadily but explodes, and with feedback it can oscillate - a chemical clock - or spread as a wave through a still dish. The classic model feeds A and B into dX/dt = A − (B + 1)X + X²Y; past B = 1 + A² the steady state breaks and the colours start to pulse.

A $(thing)prion$() is autocatalytic by shape. A protein folded wrongly, and the wrong variant is the stable version: it touches a healthy copy and refolds it, and the misfolded stack grows into an amyloid fibre that breaks into more seeds. Nothing is alive, and yet it spreads, resists heat and protease, and kills healthy cells in the process.

In the $(item)Chemical Reactor$(): a zeolite catalyst and a specimen in ionic liquid and water make $(fluid)Autocatalytic Broth$() - and broth with water and a zeolite catalyst (kept) makes more broth than went in. Folded protein crystals in broth misfold into a $(item)Prion Lattice$(); one lattice templates two crystals into twelve.

How does an anomaly begin in physics? With a choice. A field whose potential has two equal valleys must fall into one as the universe cools - and regions too far apart to agree fall into different ones. Where they meet, the field is stuck on the hill between: a $(thing)domain wall$(). With more dimensions of choice you get strings, monopoles and textures - $(thing)topological defects$(), which no smooth change can remove.

The wall's energy is E = ∫[½φ'² + λ(φ² − v²)²/4]dx = (2√2/3)√λ v³: finite, localised and permanent. A $(thing)pocket of false vacuum$() is the same idea in reverse: a region left in the higher valley, held by its own wall, waiting.

The $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() quenches a $(item)Metastable Vacuum Lattice$() around a specimen in false vacuum and catches the seams as $(item)Topological Defect Cores$(). They are where the branch's physics leaks into everything else.
A knot in a broken symmetry: the field could not agree which vacuum to fall into, so it kept both - and the seam between them cannot untie.$(br2)Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$().

Cancer is the model anomaly: a part of the body that stops obeying the body; It is not one mistake but several layers of mistakes. An $(thing)oncogene$() gets stuck on (RAS, MYC) and the cell is told to divide; a $(thing)tumour suppressor gene$() is lost - $(thing)p53$(), the guardian of the genome, which initiates cell apoptosis; and nothing tells it to stop. Each mutation gives one clone an edge over its neighbours.

That cancer needs several hits shows in the numbers: the incidence of most cancers rises as the fifth or sixth power of age, I(t) = Πk_j·t^{n−1}/(n − 1)!, as if n ≈ 6 independent steps were needed. What a cell has gained by the end are the $(thing)hallmarks of cancer$(): sustained growth signals, deaf to growth suppressors, no apoptosis, endless replication, its own blood supply, invasion - and later, an unstable genome, reprogrammed metabolism, hiding from immunity.

Mathematics breeds anomalies from perfectly good rules. In 1872 a sum of cosines, W(x) = Σaⁿcos(bⁿπx), turned out to be continuous everywhere and differentiable nowhere: a $(thing)monster$(), as Poincaré called such things. Its graph is a fractal of dimension 2 + ln a/ln b. Then came sets with no measure, space-filling curves, a sphere cut into a few pieces that reassemble into two.

$(thing)Chaos$(): a deterministic system such as the logistic map xₙ₊₁ = rxₙ(1 − xₙ) can amplify every error exponentially - a positive Lyapunov exponent - and settle onto a $(thing)strange attractor$(), a fractal it never leaves and never repeats. Predicted exactly, it cannot be predicted at all.

$(thing)Undecidability$(): some questions have answers no algorithm can find - whether a program halts, whether a statement follows from the axioms. Gödel and Turing showed the anomaly is built in. The $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$() compiles a Gödel sentence, a fractal set and a specimen into $(item)Undecidable Kernels$(): programs no other program can predict.
A program no other program can predict: whether it halts is true or false, and provably unprovable. It runs on anyway.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().

The end of an anomaly is understanding it. Physics has done this before: infinities in quantum field theory looked like a disaster until $(thing)renormalisation$() showed they only meant the constants depend on the scale you measure at. A measured quantity G then obeys [μ∂/∂μ + β(g)∂/∂g + nγ]G = 0, and at a fixed point it scales as μ^{−nγ}: the anomaly is just an $(thing)anomalous dimension$(), a number in a deeper law.

Every stage of this branch was a piece of that: where it came from, how it copies, what system carries it, where it breaks the rules and by how much, how large it gets, how to hold it and how to cure it. With all of it, the $(item)Anomaly Resolution Engine$() resolves a catalogued, quarantined anomaly: $(item)Resolved Anomalies$(). A Local Law Violation with an Undecidable Kernel, renormalised, is resolved too: the broken law explained.

A $(thing)quine$() is a program that prints its own source code. It needs two parts: a description of itself, and instructions to copy the description and build from it. Von Neumann found the same two parts in any machine that can build itself - years before DNA showed life does it that way. A computer virus, a gene and a $(thing)meme$() (an idea that spreads because it is good at spreading) are the same trick.

Does a replicator's lineage survive? If each copy makes k copies with probability p_k, the chance q that it ever dies out is the smallest root of q = Σp_k q^k. If the mean number of copies is at most 1, it always dies out; above 1 it escapes destruction with probability 1 − q - for two-or-nothing copies at p = 0.6, one time in three.

In the $(item)Nanite Assembler$(), an Undecidable Kernel with a nanite swarm in Autocatalytic Broth becomes four $(item)Quine Replicators$(). Two replicators, catoms and a processor in nanite slurry are another way to a $(item)Von Neumann Probe$().

An anomaly that lives inside a normal system is in a relationship with it. Write both as populations: dN₁/dt = r₁N₁(1 − (N₁ + αN₂)/K₁), and the mirror equation for N₂ with β. With α and β positive they compete; they coexist at N₁* = (K₁ − αK₂)/(1 − αβ) only if neither crowds the other out. Flip the sign of α and the invader helps its host instead.

Nature has done it before: mitochondria and chloroplasts were bacteria that invaded other cells two billion years ago and became their power plants. Gut bacteria, lichens, the viral genes in our own DNA that now build the placenta - the line between infection and partnership is one coefficient.

Signalling networks - growth factors, cytokines, feedback loops - decide which cells divide, move or die, and a mutation in one hub rewires them all.

Seen from far away, it invades as a $(thing)front$(): cells of density u diffuse (D) and grow (r) until crowded, ∂u/∂t = D∇²u + ru(1 − u/K), and any small seed becomes a front moving at c = 2√(Dr). And dose: n fractions of D let each cell survive with probability e^{−αD−βD²}. The anomaly is resolved only if not one of its N₀ clonogens survives: TCP = exp(−N₀e^{−n(αD+βD²)}). Normal tissue repairs between fractions; its damage grows as BED = nD(1 + D/3) - so many small fractions beat a few large ones.

Notebook, antimatter. Swap every particle for its antiparticle (C), reflect the world in a mirror (P), and run the film backwards (T). Do all three at once and the laws of physics come out the same: CPT symmetry, as solid as anything we know.

So a universe of antimatter would be a universe like ours. The $(item)CPT Mirror$() opens onto one - the $(thing)Antiverse$(): continents of antistone under a copper sky, seas of antiwater, anti-ores in the rock.

pages.text: $(thing)Annihilator$(). Lives in: The Antiverse.$(br)Drops: Antiquark Shard, Antihelium Nucleus.

pages.title: Anticarbon Crystal
pages.text: Antidiamond: the hardest thing in the Antiverse, glowing faintly where stray matter atoms meet its surface.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Anticarbon Ore in the Antiverse.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Picked out of anticarbon veins deep in the antistone.

Made in $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Anticarbon Ore$(), in veins through the Antiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Antiverse Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): CPT Symmetry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Mirror Processor.

pages.title: Anti-Gold Ingot
pages.text: Soft, dense, incorruptible - and the most dangerous jewellery imaginable.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cast in the Foundry from raw anti-gold. The mirror symmetry is perfect: same melting point, same density.
Made in $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mirror Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Baryogenesis Seed.

pages.title: Antihydrogen
pages.text: A positron bound to an antiproton. CERN first made a few atoms of it in 1995; it can only be held in magnetic traps, since touching any wall annihilates it.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Antiatoms.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Baryogenesis Seed, Liquid Antihelium.

pages.title: Antihydrogen Crystal
pages.text: The simplest anti-atom, frozen into a crystal. It shines with the same spectral lines as hydrogen, exactly - which is the point.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Antihydrogen Ice in the Antiverse; dropped by the Antihydrogen Wisp (the Antiverse).
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Found as ice in the Antiverse. Comparing its spectrum with hydrogen to twelve decimal places was the first test of CPT I ever did.

Made in $(item)Antiproton Decelerator$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Antihydrogen Ice$(), in veins through the Antiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Antihydrogen Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Antiverse Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): CPT Symmetry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antihydrogen.

pages.title: Antihydrogen Wisp
pages.text: $(thing)Antihydrogen Wisp$(). Lives in: The Antiverse.$(br)Drops: Antihydrogen Crystal.

pages.title: Anti-Iron Ingot
pages.text: A bar of anti-iron, refined in levitation and cooled in vacuum. It rings like iron when the field taps it.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Mirror Matter Foundry melts the ore without a crucible - the metal floats in a Penning field the whole time.
Made in $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mirror Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Mirror Alloy Ingot.

pages.title: Antiproton Bundle
pages.text: A magnetic bottle the size of a thumb with a pale pink knot of light at its centre: billions of antiprotons circling, never touching the glass.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Decelerator catches them from collisions at nearly light speed and brakes them lap after lap until a trap can hold them.

Made in $(item)Antiproton Decelerator$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Antiverse Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Antiatoms.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antihelium Nucleus, Antihydrogen, Antihydrogen Crystal, Liquid Antihelium, Mirror Matter Foundry.

pages.title: Antiquark Shard
pages.text: Anti-colour charge cannot be isolated, so this is a shard of something larger that refuses to come apart further.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Positronium Skitterer (the Antiverse); dropped by the Annihilator (the Antiverse).
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Torn from the shells of Antiverse creatures.
Made in $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Annihilator, Positronium Skitterer.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): CPT Symmetry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Mirror Processor.

pages.title: Antisilicon Shard
pages.text: Its band gap is the same as silicon. Its holes are positrons. It would make perfectly good chips for an anti-engineer.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Antisilicon Ore in the Antiverse; dropped by the Positronium Skitterer (the Antiverse).
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)From antisilicon veins - and from the Positronium Skitterers that eat it.

Made in $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Antisilicon Ore$(), in veins through the Antiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Positronium Skitterer.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Antiverse Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): CPT Symmetry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Mirror Processor.

pages.title: Antistone

Made in $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): CPT Symmetry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antistone Bricks, Antiverse Cache.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): CPT Symmetry.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): CPT Symmetry.

pages.title: Antiwater

Made in $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): CPT Symmetry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antihydrogen, Empty Containment Cell.

pages.title: Liquid Antihelium

pages.title: Mirror Alloy Ingot
pages.text: Matter and antimatter grains alternate in it like a chessboard, each pair held apart by its own Penning field. It hums, and it is warm.

pages.title: Mirror Processor
pages.text: A chip of antisilicon on an anticarbon die. It runs any program at all - with positrons instead of electrons, and current flowing the other way.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Etched in the Foundry. It is the first circuit I have made that would work equally well on either side of the mirror.
Made in $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mirror Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Baryogenesis Seed, Dimensional Residue, Omega Point.

pages.title: Omniscience Catalyst
pages.text: Physics, mathematics, the stars, time, mind and exotic matter, every singularity of knowledge fused into one catalyst. Holding it, for an instant you understand everything that is the case. Then the knowledge fades, leaving a sense of having forgotten something enormous.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)On the Extreme Assembly Table, I combined the Theory of Everything with every other conceptual singularity I had compressed. They fused into a catalyst that let me glimpse everything for a moment.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Baryon Asymmetry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnium Ingot, Pleroma Confluence.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Found in veins in the antistone, shining blue-white under the copper sky.

pages.title: Accretion Disk Reactor
pages.text: Feeds matter onto a captive black hole: falling in, it gives up to a third of its rest energy as light. Too much at once, and its own light blows the disk away.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Set the hole's mass, how fast it is fed, and its spin. A spinning hole lets matter orbit closer before it falls, so more of its rest energy comes out (6% at no spin, a third near the maximum). The light pushes back on the infalling gas: past the Eddington luminosity, L = 1.26×10³¹ (M/M☉) W, it blows the disk apart.

Made in $(item)Spectrograph$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Galactic Dynamics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Web Filament.

pages.title: The Cosmic Web
pages.text: $(thing)The Cosmic Web$()$(br2)On the largest scales the galaxies are not scattered evenly: they lie along filaments and sheets round enormous voids, the shape gravity has pulled the dark matter into since the Big Bang. Unlocks the cosmic web simulation.
$(thing)Insight$(): 220$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Galactic Dynamics, The Hot Big Bang, Interstellar Medium.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Galactic Filament, 2 Redshift Lens.

pages.title: Exoplanetology

$(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Spectroscopy.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Star Field Plate, 2 Stellar Spectrum Plate.

pages.title: Galactic Dynamics
pages.text: $(thing)Galactic Dynamics$()$(br2)Map how fast the Galaxy's hydrogen turns at each distance from its centre and the stars alone cannot hold it together: something unseen outweighs them several times over. Unlocks the long galactic survey.
$(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Radio Astronomy.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Hydrogen Line Map, 2 Pulsar Timing Record, 2 Deep Sky Plate.
