pages.title: Transit Light Curve
pages.text: A star's brightness, dipping for a few hours as a planet crosses in front of it. The depth gives the planet's size.
Made in $(item)Reflecting Telescope$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Exoplanetology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Posterior Tablet.

Split light into its colours and it tells you what made it. A hot body glows brightest at a wavelength set by its temperature alone: $(thing)λ = b/T$(), with b = 2.898 mm·K. The Sun, at 5,778 K, peaks in green light.

Atoms leave their own marks: dark lines where cool gas in front absorbs, bright lines where hot gas emits, each element at its own wavelengths. That is how helium was found on the Sun before anyone found it on Earth.

The $(item)Spectrograph$() turns glass and amethyst into $(item)Spectral Plates$(). Fed $(item)Raw Pitchblende$() and a plate, it finds the radium hidden in the ore by its lines and separates it as $(item)Radium Salt$(), with a little magnetite left over.

Astronomy begins with gathering light. A $(item)Telescope Mirror Blank$() - glass, ground and silvered - collects a star's light over its whole face and brings it to one point. The wider the mirror, the fainter the stars it shows.

But no mirror focuses light on a true point. Light is a wave, and a round opening of diameter D spreads it into a disc about 1.22λ/D wide. Two stars closer than that blur into one: $(thing)the diffraction limit$(). Bigger mirrors are sharper as well as brighter.

Everything falls the same way: a feather and a hammer land together on the Moon. That is the $(thing)equivalence principle$(), and a $(item)Proof Mass$() - shielded so that nothing but gravity touches it - follows free fall exactly.
Clocks lower in a gravity well run slower: τ = t·√(1 − 2GM/rc²). On the Earth's surface the effect is a few parts in 10¹⁰; on a neutron star a clock loses twelve minutes an hour.

The $(item)Atomic Clock$() shows it, scaled up so you can see it: it runs at full speed at the top of the world and at about three quarters at its floor. Carry one in your off hand and your own time stays in step - it clears Time Dilation.

Measure the Doppler shift of the hydrogen line along the Galaxy, and you have how fast its gas circles at each distance from the centre. If the stars were all its mass, the speed would fall off far out, as the planets' does: v = √(GM/r).

It does not. Far beyond the visible disc the gas still turns at over 200 km/s. Something unseen holds it: $(thing)dark matter$(), several times the mass of every star. The long galactic survey maps it - and gives a great deal of Insight.
A $(item)Dark Matter Collector$() told where the halo is gathers twice as much: give it two $(item)Hydrogen Line Maps$() with its usual inputs.

Sometimes a $(thing)crater$() lies in open country: a bowl of $(item)Impact Breccia$() with a raised rim, and in the middle, half buried, what made it. An $(item)Iron Meteorite$() is the core of a small planet that shattered billions of years ago; a $(item)Chondrite$() is stone that has not melted since the planets formed.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Iron Meteorite in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.

$(item)Meteoric Iron$() smelts to iron. Assayed in the Spectrograph, four pieces give two blocks of the $(item)Iron-Nickel$() a planet's core is made of. Chondrites hold $(item)Presolar Grains$(): silicon carbide that condensed around stars that died before the Sun was born. Henri Moissan found it in the Canyon Diablo meteorite: eight grains make a $(item)Moissanite$() crystal.

One iron meteorite in four is a $(thing)pallasite$(): green olivine crystals set in the metal, the boundary between a small planet's core and mantle. Its assay gives a $(item)Peridot$() - an olivine refractory that lines a Refractory Firebox as well as corundum does.

The $(item)Radio Telescope$() is a dish on an alt-azimuth mount with a $(item)Feed Horn$() at its focus. Radio passes through cloud and daylight: it works at any hour, rain or shine - but it needs a view of the sky, and every machine running within 24 blocks is $(thing)noise$() in its receiver.

A source raises the antenna temperature by T = S·A/2k; the receiver hears it over the system temperature, T_sys. Taking in a band B for a time τ beats the noise down: $(thing)SNR = T·√(Bτ)/T_sys$(). The Galaxy itself roars at low frequencies, so T_sys climbs steeply below a few hundred MHz.

$(thing)Hydrogen$() glows in a narrow line at 1420.4 MHz. Tune to it and keep the band narrow: a line half a megahertz wide is diluted in a wider one. $(thing)Pulsars$() are faint and broadband - take a wide band for the SNR, but not so wide that dispersion in the interstellar plasma, 8.3 µs·DM·B/ν³, smears the pulse beyond a millisecond. Higher frequencies smear less, but the pulsar is fainter there.

Every map and timing record gives $(thing)Insight$(). Once you have mapped how fast the Galaxy turns, the long galactic survey gives a great deal more - and a $(thing)binary pulsar$() can be timed: its orbit shrinks exactly as general relativity predicts, measured against a $(item)Time-Dilated Sample$() as the reference clock.

After the furnace at Odeillo in the Pyrenees: $(item)Heliostats$() turn with the Sun and throw its light onto a parabolic wall of $(item)Concentrator Mirrors$(), which brings it to a point on the $(item)Solar Receiver$(). It works only by day, under open sky and without rain.

Sunlight brings about 1,000 W/m² when the Sun is high - less as it sinks. Concentrated C times and let through the shutter, it heats the target until it radiates away what it takes in: αgCG = εσT⁴. At ten thousand suns that is well over 3,000 K - hotter than any flame. Too hot and the crucible itself melts (3,200 K); too cool and nothing does.

Quartz or sand melts at 1,986 K into $(item)Fused Silica$(): a glass that barely expands with heat. Corundum - or, more slowly, the alumina in clay - melts at 2,323 K and freezes into a $(item)Sapphire Boule$(), for the Optical Workshop to cut into windows. Both go into the Radio Telescope's cold receiver.

The $(item)Reflecting Telescope$() is a mirror under a dome. It works only at $(thing)night$(), with $(thing)open sky$() above its slit and no rain - and every plate it exposes teaches you something: each run gives $(thing)Insight$().

Two settings decide what it records. The $(thing)aperture$() D gathers light in proportion to D², and the $(thing)exposure$() t adds up what arrives: the faintest star on the plate, the limiting magnitude, rises by 5·log D and 1.25·log t. Each magnitude is 2.5 times fainter. A full Moon brightens the sky by three magnitudes and drowns the faintest stars.

The air smears every star into a $(thing)seeing$() disc of about 2.5″ at sea level - better the higher you build. The mirror cannot beat its own $(thing)diffraction limit$(), 1.22λ/D. But in exposures shorter than about 50 ms the turbulence stands still: take very short ones and keep the sharpest - $(thing)lucky imaging$() - for a $(item)Planetary Plate$().

What it makes: $(item)Star Field Plates$() (magnitude 9), $(item)Stellar Spectrum Plates$() through a Spectral Plate (12), $(item)Planetary Plates$() (sharper than 1.1″), and, once you know stellar astrophysics, $(item)Deep Sky Plates$() of galaxies (16.5 - a big mirror, long exposures and a dark sky).

The plates are evidence, too: the $(item)Bayesian Analyzer$() turns a Prior Tablet and a Stellar Spectrum Plate (or two Star Field Plates) into Posterior Tablets. And star positions against the plumb line are how the geoid was first mapped - a Star Field Plate and two Survey Maps make two $(item)Geoid Models$(). Mirror blanks ground with $(item)Garnet$() grit come out twice as many.
Optics from the workshop make the Reflecting Telescope a better instrument. Each sits in it as a catalyst and is never used up.

A $(item)Schmidt Corrector Plate$() turns it into a survey camera: four plates at once give two Star Field Plates and a Deep Sky Plate (magnitude 15). An $(item)Echelle Grating$() spreads each star's light so finely that one exposure gives three Stellar Spectrum Plates. An $(item)Apochromatic Objective$() brings every colour to one focus: two Planetary Plates at a time.
Matter falling onto a black hole gives up energy as it spirals in - η of its rest energy, from 6% for a hole that does not spin to a third for one spinning at the limit. Fusion manages 0.7%.

The $(item)Accretion Disk Reactor$() holds a black hole in a sphere of horizon containment, its disk turning in the confinement ring. Set the hole's mass, the feed rate and the spin. Power follows the luminosity $(thing)L = η·ṁc²$() - but the light pushes back on the gas, and past the $(thing)Eddington luminosity$(), L = 1.26×10³¹ (M/M☉) W, the disk is blown away and the reactor stops.

It burns Interstellar Dust with Molecular Cloud gas, Accretion Disk Fragments, or a whole Brown Dwarf Core, leaving $(fluid)Accretion Disk Plasma$() - and now and then a $(item)Quasar Jet Filament$() from the jets out of its poles.

Cepheid variables pulse with a period that gives their true brightness: the first rung of the distance ladder. A Spectrograph sets a $(item)Cepheid Standard Candle$() against a spectral plate: a $(item)Redshift Lens$() - every galaxy is receding, faster the farther.

A long survey of the hydrogen line maps a $(item)Galactic Filament$(). Four of them and a Redshift Lens, run through the Monte Carlo Engine, trace the $(item)Cosmic Web$(): the filaments and voids gravity has drawn the dark matter into since the Big Bang.
For the Universe to be flat, it must hold the $(thing)critical density$() ρ = 3H²/8πG - about five protons in every cubic metre.

A planet crossing its star blocks a fraction $(thing)δ = (r/R)²$() of its light: a Jupiter dims the Sun by one per cent, an Earth by one part in twelve thousand. The Reflecting Telescope records a $(item)Transit Light Curve$().

In the Accretion Frontier's Asteroid Belt lie the cores of shattered planets that formed round other stars. The Spectrograph assays an $(item)Exoplanet Core Sample$() into iron-nickel and ringwoodite, and a $(item)Brown Dwarf Core$() - a failed star - into rare earths and dust.

The $(item)Interstellar Scoop$() gathers what lies between the stars - but only where the air will not swamp it: at y 200 or above in the Overworld, or anywhere in the Accretion Frontier or the End. It gathers $(fluid)Molecular Cloud$() gas, $(fluid)Interstellar Medium$() (into glass bottles) and $(item)Interstellar Dust$() (onto paper).

A hot star ionises the gas round it out to a sphere where recombination keeps up: $(thing)Q = (4/3)πR³n²α$(). Photograph a dying star's shell with dust and a plate: a $(item)Planetary Nebula Shell$(). Four dust and a bucket of water make clay again - every rocky planet began as dust.

A neutron-star merger heard by the Laser Interferometer can be found in the sky: point the telescope with its record and photograph the $(thing)kilonova$() - the glow of freshly made gold and platinum, peaking after days: $(item)Kilonova Ash$().

The same mergers, and the collapse of the heaviest stars, launch jets at Γ ≈ 300, beamed into a cone of 1/Γ: $(thing)gamma-ray bursts$(). The $(item)Burst Observatory$() watches the whole sky with twelve scintillators. A low threshold sees more bursts but more noise. Watch until you are 90% sure of a catch, with few false triggers: a $(item)Burst Afterglow Crystal$().

pages.title: Radio Telescope
pages.text: A dish that listens to the sky: To cold hydrogen, pulsars and more. It works by day and in rain, but every machine running nearby is noise in its receiver.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Works day and night, rain or shine, but needs a view of the sky - and every other machine running within 24 blocks raises the system temperature. Tune to the line, narrow the band to it, and integrate long enough: SNR = T·√(Bτ)/T_sys. For pulsars, too wide a band smears the pulse. Every map and record gives Insight.

The engines found in ruins pull creatures out of nothing at random. One you build yourself (on the $(item)Convergence Altar$()) grows the creature you choose - once you have studied $(thing)Synthetic Biology$(); before that it will not open for you.
Its template is a $(item)Genome Sample$() from the Gene Sampler: every sample now remembers whose it is. Each creature costs one $(item)Morphogenic Serum$() and 16 million FE.

And it must be tuned: four controls - morphogen, membrane, tide and coherence - and four readings of how close the breach is to the creature's form. Every creature has its own settings; bring all four readings to the middle and it starts to grow them. It stops when eight are around it. It will not grow bosses (tag theoreticalsciences:not_spawnable).

pages.title: Breached Anomaly Engine
pages.text: Ruins of a machine that broke more than itself. Its frame is torn, and from the tears leak fragments of rules that no longer apply anywhere. It hums irregularly, and the space around it is not quite consistent.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I came upon it in the wreckage of a breach, still sputtering. Someone, maybe some earlier version of me, built an engine to break the axioms, and it is clear such an effect had consequences.
$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.

pages.title: Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor
pages.text: A protein from a robin's eye that senses Earth's magnetic field through a pair of entangled electron spins. Light makes the pair; the field tips their dance. The crystal turns slowly in the hand to point north.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Migratory birds see magnetic fields, probably via radical pairs in cryptochrome. I folded the protein from feather genetics, entangled its radical pair with a photon pair and grew it in nutrient broth. It aligned with the field.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Psionic Crystal.

pages.title: Engineered Enzyme
pages.text: A protein designed rather than evolved, folded around a pocket shaped for exactly one reaction. It speeds that reaction a millionfold and ignores everything else. It looks like a pale, slightly sticky crystal.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Natural enzymes are evolved to fit their substrates. I started from a genome, used a chiral crystal to fix the handedness and a zeolite to shape the pocket, then let the Bioreactor optimise the rest in nutrient broth.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Genomics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Apoptosis Trigger, Morphogenic Serum, Recombinant DNA, Resistant Clone Colony, Stem Cell Culture, Tardigrade Culture, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid.

pages.title: Folded Protein Crystal
pages.text: A long chain of amino acids that has found its one native shape out of more possible shapes than there are atoms in the universe - and frozen in that shape as a crystal. Levinthal's paradox says it should take forever. It took milliseconds.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Proteins fold quickly because the energy landscape funnels them. I mapped that funnel with a molecular orbital lattice, let a quantum processor search it, and grew the folded chain from recombinant DNA in nutrient broth.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Protein Folding.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor, Morphogenic Serum, Prion Lattice, Quantum Chlorophyll.

pages.title: Genome Sample
pages.text: A vial of clear fluid with every instruction for building one creature written in four chemical letters. It looks like water. It is the most information-dense thing I have ever casually put in my pocket.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Gene Sampler's first touch filled a vial with a creature's complete genome. Sequencing it showed the same alphabet as my own, which was both expected and moving.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Genomics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Engineered Enzyme, Recombinant DNA, Stem Cell Culture, Tardigrade Culture, Xenogenome Sample.

pages.title: Morphogenic Serum
pages.text: Every signal an embryo listens to, in one vial. A Breached Anomaly Engine spends one on every creature it grows.
Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity.

pages.title: Neural Organoid
pages.text: A pea-sized brain grown in a dish: real neurons, folded and connected, with no body around them. Its electrical activity has started to look like the patterns of a sleeping brain. I try not to think about what it might be dreaming about.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Brain organoids are a real technology. I grew stem cells around a thought matrix with a room-temperature superconductor for wiring and fed them synaptic fluid. Within days the electrodes recorded coordinated waves.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Neurobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Boltzmann Brain, Cognitive Singularity, Omnicellular Genome, Silicon Life Spore, Superintelligence Core, Xenobot Swarm.

pages.title: Nutrient Broth
pages.text: A warm, rich medium for growing cells. Sugar provides energy, bone meal provides minerals, and a zeolite catalyst keeps the chemistry steady. It smells faintly sweet. Left uncovered for even a moment, it clouds with whatever life drifts into it.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Life needs food. In the Bioreactor, I combined sugar, bone meal and water with a zeolite catalyst, and the broth supported growth.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Molecular Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomalous Strain Culture, CAR-T Cell Culture, Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor, Engineered Enzyme, Folded Protein Crystal, Immortal Cell Line, Minimal Synthetic Cell, Morphogenic Serum and more.

pages.title: Omnicellular Genome
pages.text: One genome that can build any creature in any dimension - carbon or silicon, DNA or not. It is a coiled, shifting helix that seems to shift as I watch. Every living thing I have met is a sentence it can write.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I fed the Evolution Engine a panspermia seed, a silicon life spore, a neural organoid, recombinant DNA and Xenoplasm and let it evolve a single code that could express all of them. It took less time than I thought.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Panspermia.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Arbor Simulacrum, Bubble Universe, Omnilex Seal, Pocket Universe, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

pages.title: Panspermia Seed
pages.text: A seed packed with life designed to survive the trip between universes. Tardigrade toughness, a spark of life and unbihexium shielding, all sealed in a capsule that seems to hold a small universe of its own. It is light and very still.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Panspermia supposes life travels between worlds. I wanted it to travel between universes. The Abiogenesis Crucible sealed a spark of life with tardigrades, Xenoplasm and primordial soup inside a bubble universe shielded by unbihexium.
Made in $(item)Abiogenesis Crucible$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Panspermia.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnicellular Genome, Omnilex Seal, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

pages.title: Primordial Soup
pages.text: The chemical mixture from which life arose. Morphogens, chiral crystals and superacids give it the ingredients for self-replication. It is warm and bubbles slowly. Miller and Urey made amino acids in a flask of sparks; this goes much further.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Abiogenesis needs the right chemistry. In the Chemical Reactor, I combined a Turing Morphogen with chiral crystal, clathrate and superacid, and the soup began to organise itself.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Abiogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Panspermia Seed, Spark of Life.

pages.title: Recombinant DNA
pages.text: A double helix spliced together from more than one creature, its pieces joined by enzymes that cut and paste at precise sequences. It looks no different from any other DNA, yet does things no single creature's DNA could.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Restriction enzymes cut genomes at precise points; ligases stitch them back. I let engineered enzymes splice two samples together in a nutrient broth, and the Gene Sequencer read back a genome that had never existed before.

Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Genomics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Apoptosis Trigger, CAR-T Cell Culture, Chronoplastic Gasket, Folded Protein Crystal, Minimal Synthetic Cell, Morphogenic Serum, Omnicellular Genome, Stem Cell Culture.

pages.title: Extremophiles
pages.text: $(thing)Extremophiles$()$(br2)Life at the edges: boiling vents, frozen vacuum, radiation. Unlocks tardigrade cultures.

$(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Genomics, Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 8 Genome Sample.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the rate constant of an enzyme-catalysed reaction in a hyperthermophile living at 121 °C, using the Arrhenius law.

pages.title: Morphogenesis
pages.text: $(thing)Morphogenesis$()$(br2)How a blob of identical cells paints itself into a body: reaction and diffusion. Unlocks Turing morphogens.

$(thing)Insight$(): 120$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Minimal Synthetic Cell.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the relative morphogen concentration C/C0 at x = 50 µm from the source, with D = 10 µm^2/s and degradation rate k = 0.001 /s.

pages.title: Neurobiology
pages.text: $(thing)Neurobiology$()$(br2)Grow a brain in a dish and ask it what it thinks. Unlocks neural organoids.

$(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Artificial General Intelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Stem Cell Culture.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the potassium equilibrium potential (V) of a neuron at 310 K with 5 mM K+ outside and 140 mM inside.

pages.title: Panspermia
pages.text: $(thing)Panspermia$()$(br2)Life carried between worlds - and between universes. Unlocks panspermia seeds and the omnicellular genome.

$(thing)Insight$(): 450$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Abiogenesis, The Multiverse, The Island of Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Spark of Life.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find how many spores in a meteorite survive an interplanetary journey of time t under cosmic radiation.

pages.title: Protein Folding
pages.text: $(thing)Protein Folding$()$(br2)A chain finds its one shape among astronomically many. Unlocks folded protein crystals.

$(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Genomics, Quantum Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Recombinant DNA.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the time (s) a 30-residue chain would need to try every conformation if each residue has 3 states and each try takes 1e-13 s (Levinthal's paradox).

pages.title: Xenobiology
pages.text: $(thing)Xenobiology$()$(br2)Life in other dimensions does not use DNA. Unlocks xenogenome work, Xenoplasm and silicon life.

$(thing)Insight$(): 130$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 16 Genome Sample.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find how many bits a 100-letter genome stores in an 8-letter (hachimoji-like) genetic alphabet.

pages.title: Silicon Life Spore
pages.text: A spore built on silicon instead of carbon - a speculative chemistry that only works in the strange physics of the Bulk. It is glassy, faceted and very slightly warm, and it ticks quietly, as though growing at the pace of crystal.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Silicon life has always been a thought experiment. In the Bulk, where chemistry runs differently, I seeded a minimal cell with a xenogenome and Xenoplasm on a bulk crystal. The spore that grew was neither carbon nor stone.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metastatic Spore, Omnicellular Genome, Silicon Life Spore, Xenobot Swarm.

pages.title: Spark of Life
pages.text: A small bright point that is the moment chemistry crossed into biology - self-replication, metabolism and a boundary, all arriving at once. It flickers unsteadily. Holding it feels like holding a match that might become a forest.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Abiogenesis is the unsolved step. I put primordial soup, stellar plasma and the omega point in the Abiogenesis Crucible with telomerase, a minimal cell and quantum chlorophyll, and caught the instant it all started to copy itself.

Made in $(item)Abiogenesis Crucible$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Abiogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnilex Seal, Omniscience Catalyst, Ontological Junction, Panspermia Seed, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

pages.title: Stem Cell Culture
pages.text: A flask of cells that have yet to differentiate. Any of them could be a neuron, a muscle, a bone. The broth is warm and cloudy and seems to be thinking about its options. Under the microscope they look identical, and that sameness is exactly the point: every possibility is still open.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Synthetic biology lets me write life rather than read it. I took a genome sample, spliced in recombinant DNA to undo specialisation and used an engineered enzyme to hold the cells in their undecided state.

Made in $(item)Anomaly Resolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomalous Strain Culture, CAR-T Cell Culture, Neural Organoid, Telomerase Complex, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid, Xenobot Swarm.

pages.title: Tardigrade Culture
pages.text: A culture of water bears, tiny eight-legged animals that survive vacuum, radiation and freezing by drying out and simply pausing being alive. In the jar they wander slowly through moss. Dried, they will wait for centuries.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Extremophiles taught me that life could survive almost anything. I used engineered enzymes to boost a tardigrade genome's repair genes, gave them moss to live in and froze a culture in superfluid helium. It woke up.
Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Extremophiles.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronoplastic Gasket, Panspermia Seed, Telomerase Complex.

pages.title: Telomerase Complex
pages.text: An enzyme that rebuilds telomeres - the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes that shorten every time a cell divides. Cells that have it do not age. The complex is small, pale and oddly cold, as if keeping time for itself.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Telomerase is real; most adult cells have switched it off. The Evolution Engine ran a million generations of stem cells and tardigrades with Turing morphogens and Xenoplasm, while an arrow of time shard kept the clock running fast.

Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Directed Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Immortal Cell Line, Omnilex Seal, Ontological Junction, Spark of Life, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

pages.title: Turing Morphogen
pages.text: A pair of chemicals, one that activates and diffuses slowly and one that inhibits and diffuses fast. Mixed on a dish they paint stripes and spots by themselves, exactly the reaction-diffusion patterns Turing predicted in 1952.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Turing proposed that patterns in animals arise from reaction and diffusion. I extracted the morphogens from a minimal cell, set their handedness with a chiral crystal and tuned their rates using the complex plane. Spots appeared on the dish.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Morphogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Primordial Soup, Telomerase Complex.

pages.title: Xenobot Swarm
pages.text: Living machines a millimetre across, built from cells arranged in shapes no animal ever had. They walk, push, heal and even assemble copies of themselves from loose cells. They twitch in the jar, busy.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Xenobots were real: frog cells arranged by an evolutionary algorithm. I gave a general AI core stem cells and nanites to design with, and the Bioreactor built whatever shape it picked. Some of them built more of themselves.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Silicon Life Spore, Symbiont Culture, Xenobot Swarm.

pages.title: Xenogenome Sample
pages.text: A vial of something that is clearly a genome but is not DNA. The molecule folds the wrong way, uses letters I do not recognise and carries information more densely than any terrestrial code. It glows faintly in the dark.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I sampled a creature from another dimension expecting DNA and found something else. Life evolved under different physics, with a different chemistry of inheritance - and it was still readable.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Silicon Life Spore, Xenobot Swarm, Xenoplasm.

pages.title: Xenoplasm
pages.text: Life fluid from another dimension. It does not use DNA, and its chemistry is foreign. It is warm, iridescent and moves on its own. Its molecules are built on a backbone no terrestrial cell would recognise, and their handedness alternates in ways that should be unstable. Somehow it thrives on that instability.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Xenobiology studies life without DNA. In the Bioreactor, I combined a Xenogenome Sample with foam substrate and nutrient broth, and the culture grew as no Earth life could.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metastatic Spore, Omnicellular Genome, Panspermia Seed, Silicon Life Spore, Telomerase Complex, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid.

Photosynthesis moves energy through its antenna with near-perfect efficiency by trying every path at once, coherently. A robin feels north through a pair of electrons entangled in a protein in its eye.

From these: $(item)Quantum Chlorophyll$() and the $(item)Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor$() - which Psionic Crystals now need. $(item)Tardigrade Cultures$() come from the extremophiles: animals that survive vacuum by pausing life itself.

Chemistry. A bond is not a stick between balls. Two atoms share an electron because the shared $(thing)wavefunction$() spread over both has lower energy than either alone - the same quantum mechanics as everything else in this book.
The $(item)Chemical Reactor$() is where it starts: $(fluid)Supercritical Solvent$() (gas-dense, liquid-thin) and $(item)Zeolite Catalysts$(), whose pores let only the right molecules meet.
Next: $(item)Molecular Orbital Lattices$() - the bond itself, frozen - and $(item)Chiral Crystals$(), molecules that come in a left hand and a right hand. Life, I will find, only ever uses one.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

Electron wavefunctions shared between atoms, frozen into a grid. This is what a chemical bond is.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().

pages.title: Essence Distillery
pages.text: A tower of fractionation trays wound with chronosteel coils. Pour in every fluid one mod has and it boils them together, tray after tray, until what is left is a single fluid that stands for all of them: that mod's Essence.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 5$() machine.
This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.
Distils every fluid of one mod into that mod's $(fluid)Essence$(), which the $(item)Pleroma Confluence$() wants. JEI lists, mod by mod, which fluids go in.

pages.title: Essence Distillery
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).

Pleroma is everything at once - and that now includes every fluid of every mod installed. They do not each go into the $(item)Pleroma Confluence$(): first, every mod's fluids are distilled together in the $(item)Essence Distillery$() into that mod's $(fluid)Essence$() - one fluid that stands for all of them.

Each distillation takes up to twelve of one mod's fluids (16,000 mB of each) and gives 1,000 mB of Essence. A mod with more fluids is distilled in parts, and the parts (4,000 mB of each) into the whole Essence. JEI lists every mod's distillations; new mods' fluids join in by themselves. Only fluids that fit in a bucket count, and a server can leave fluids or mods out (essenceBlacklist).

The Confluence then wants 64,000 mB of every mod's Essence beside its million of each of this mod's fluids. Essences live in tanks and pipes only: a containment cell cannot remember whose Essence it held.

Replace the electron and chemistry changes. A $(thing)positron$() makes positronium - an atom of matter and antimatter - and $(item)Positronium Hydride$() is a molecule of it. A $(thing)muon$() is 200 times heavier than an electron, so a $(item)Muonic Catalyst$() squeezes atoms close enough to fuse cold.
A $(item)Room-Temperature Superconductor$() - hydrogen packed into a framework - carries current with zero resistance and no cryogenics.
A molecule made of a hydrogen atom and an atom of matter bound to antimatter. It lasts a nanosecond - unless you trap it.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Swap an electron for a muon and atoms shrink 200 times - close enough to fuse cold.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Zero resistance without cryogenics. Physicists have chased this for a century.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Positronium Hydride$(): Unbihexium Ingot$(li)$(item)Muonic Catalyst$(): Flerovium Ingot, Stellar Singularity$(li)$(item)Room-Temperature Superconductor$(): Neural Organoid, Transfinite Coil Block
Past uranium, elements get heavier and shorter-lived - until, theory says, an island: nuclei with $(thing)magic numbers$() of protons and neutrons, closed shells that hold them together.

The $(item)Nuclide Forge$() fires heavy ions from the r-process into a target. $(item)Flerovium$() (element 114) first, then $(item)Unbihexium$() (126), the heart of the island. Hypernova Alloy and Transcendent Metal now need them.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Element 114, held together by magic numbers of protons and neutrons.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nuclide Forge$().
Element 126, the heart of the island of stability. Nothing should be this heavy and last this long.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nuclide Forge$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Flerovium Ingot$(): Dimensional Residue, Transcendent Metal Ingot, Transcendent Plasma, Unbihexium Ingot$(li)$(item)Unbihexium Ingot$(): Dimensional Residue, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Panspermia Seed

pages.title: Buckyball Cage
pages.text: Sixty carbon atoms bonded into the shape of a football - twelve pentagons and twenty hexagons - with a hollow centre big enough to trap one more atom. It is round, slippery and perfectly symmetrical, and the hollow seems to be waiting for something.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Heating graphene with blaze powder, I expected soot. Instead the sheets curled into closed spheres, and cooled in superfluid helium they stayed that way - the same cages Kroto and Smalley found in vaporised graphite.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nanochemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Minimal Synthetic Cell, Noble Gas Clathrate, Positronium Hydride.

pages.title: Carbon Nanotube Bundle
pages.text: Graphene sheets rolled seamlessly into tubes a few nanometres across, then twisted together into a rope. Each tube is far stronger than steel; the bundle feels like silk and refuses to snap. Pulled taut, it sings faintly.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Graphene curled on its own along the edges of an orbital lattice, so I gave it more lattice and an ionic liquid to roll in. The tubes came out closed and clean, and twisted into rope as they dried.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nanochemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metal-Organic Framework, Self-Healing Polymer.

pages.title: Carborane Superacid
pages.text: The strongest acid that can be bottled. It protonates almost anything yet is gentle on glass, because its conjugate base is so stable it does not attack. It is clear and calm in the flask. It is one of the few acids that is strong and polite at the same time.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Carborane acids are a million times stronger than sulfuric. Electrolysing an Electride Crystal with chiral crystal and ionic liquid, I made one strong enough to protonate anything.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superacids.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Positronium Hydride, Primordial Soup.

pages.title: Chiral Crystal
pages.text: A crystal that comes in only one hand. Like my left and right palms, its mirror image cannot be rotated to match it. Living things use left-handed amino acids and right-handed sugars, and nobody fully knows why. This one twists light passing through it, always the same way.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Molecular orbitals let me predict which hand a molecule would take. Seeding an orbital lattice with amethyst and a quantum dot in supercritical solvent, I found the crystals all came out with the same handedness. I stopped calling it an accident after the tenth batch.

Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Carborane Superacid, Coherent Wiring Harness, Engineered Enzyme, Metal-Organic Framework, Primordial Soup, Turing Morphogen.

pages.title: Electride Crystal
pages.text: A salt in which the negative ions are not atoms at all but bare electrons, sitting in cavities of the lattice like eggs in a carton. It is dark, glossy and conducts strangely, and seems to give up electrons at the slightest provocation.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing electrons into Cherenkov quartz with redstone current, while superfluid helium held the lattice cold and still, I found that some electrons stayed behind in empty sites with no atom to belong to. The Electrolytic Cell had made an electride.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Electrochemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Carborane Superacid, Room-Temperature Superconductor.

pages.title: Flerovium Ingot
pages.text: Element 114, a superheavy metal held together by a near-magic number of protons. Real flerovium lasts seconds; this ingot lasts indefinitely because its neutron count sits right on the island. It is improbably dense and faintly warm.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The island of stability predicts superheavy nuclei that live long. I fed r-process clusters and neutronium into the Nuclide Forge with muons to tighten the nuclei and quark-gluon plasma to supply neutrons, and something came out that did not immediately decay.
Made in $(item)Nuclide Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Island of Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Transcendent Metal Ingot, Transcendent Plasma, Unbihexium Ingot.

pages.title: Inflaton Field
pages.text: The field that drove cosmic inflation, stretching the universe exponentially in a fraction of a second. Bottled, it trembles with stored expansion, as if wanting to make everything around it larger. It is hot, restless and very light.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Guth's inflation needs a field to drive it. Distilling dimensional residue at the very top of the spire, I captured a fraction that kept trying to expand its container. The inflaton, caught before it could decay.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Fractional Distillation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, Inflaton Condensate, Pocket Universe, Universe Seed.

pages.title: Ionic Liquid
pages.text: A salt that is liquid at room temperature. It conducts electricity, does not evaporate, and dissolves almost anything. It is clear, slightly viscous and faintly warm. Chemists call such salts designer solvents, because they can be tuned for almost any task.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Electrolysing quartz with supercritical solvent in the Electrolytic Cell, I got a salt that stayed liquid. An ionic liquid, perfect for further chemistry.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity, Autocatalytic Broth, Carbon Nanotube Bundle, Carborane Superacid, Metal-Organic Framework, Self-Healing Polymer.

pages.title: Liquid Sodium
pages.text: Sodium melted at 98 °C. It carries heat far better than water and boils only at 883 °C, which is why fast reactors use it as coolant, though it burns in air.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Electrochemistry.

pages.title: Lithium Ingot
pages.text: The lightest metal, won from brine. Soft enough to cut with a knife; it floats on oil and burns crimson.
Made in $(item)Electrolytic Cell$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Electrochemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Lithium-6 Ingot.

pages.title: Metal-Organic Framework
pages.text: A scaffold of copper nodes and organic struts so open that a single gram of it hides more inner surface than a football pitch. Gas soaks into it like water into a sponge. It is feather-light and full of rooms.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Supramolecular chemistry lets molecules assemble themselves. Copper ions met nanotube struts and chiral linkers in an ionic liquid, and each found its place without my help. The framework grew the way frost grows on glass.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Supramolecular Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Morphogenic Serum, Room-Temperature Superconductor.

pages.title: Mod Essence
pages.text: Every fluid of one mod distilled together into a single liquid. It tastes, reportedly, of everything its authors ever put in a tank.

One fluid for each mod installed: every fluid of that mod distilled together in the $(item)Essence Distillery$(). The Pleroma Confluence wants 64,000 mB of each mod's Essence. Essences live in tanks and pipes only.

pages.title: Molecular Orbital Lattice
pages.text: Electron clouds shared across a whole grid of atoms, frozen in place so I can finally see what a bond is: not a stick between balls but a wavefunction spread over both, lower in energy than either alone. The lattice shimmers faintly where the orbitals overlap.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Solving the Schrodinger equation for a molecule taught me where the electrons sit. I used a qubit to encode that solution and grew the crystal around it on a zeolite template in supercritical solvent, so the orbitals set exactly where the mathematics put them.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Carbon Nanotube Bundle, Chiral Crystal, Folded Protein Crystal, Gene Sequencer.

pages.title: Muonic Catalyst
pages.text: A capsule of molecules in which electrons are replaced by muons, two hundred times heavier. The orbitals shrink accordingly, and two nuclei that would never fuse at room temperature are pulled close enough to tunnel into one. It feels oddly heavy for its size.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Muon-catalysed fusion was known in the 1950s; its problem is that muons are short-lived and get stuck. Using a noble gas clathrate to hold the fuel, quark-gluon plasma to make muons and a monopole to free them, I got the catalyst to work cycle after cycle.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Exotic Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Flerovium Ingot, Stellar Singularity.

pages.title: Noble Gas Clathrate
pages.text: A cage of ice with a xenon atom trapped in every cell, held not by bonds but by the plain fact that it cannot get out. The noble gases are supposed to be aloof; caged like this they are merely patient. It fizzes slightly as it warms.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ice frozen around buckyball templates in superfluid helium formed cages of a very particular size. Noble gas filled them before I could seal the reactor, and stayed. Clathrates were not a goal - they were a pleasant accident.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Supramolecular Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Muonic Catalyst, Primordial Soup.

pages.title: Quantum Chemistry
pages.text: $(thing)Quantum Chemistry$()$(br2)Solve the Schrödinger equation for a molecule and you have its chemistry. Unlocks orbital lattices and chiral crystals.

$(thing)Insight$(): 35$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Chemical Bonding, Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Qubit.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the energy of the n = 2 level of the hydrogen atom from the Schrödinger equation.

pages.title: Superacids
pages.text: $(thing)Superacids$()$(br2)Acids a million million times stronger than sulfuric - strong enough to protonate almost anything.

$(thing)Insight$(): 50$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Electrochemistry, High-Energy Particle Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Electride Crystal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the Hammett acidity H0 of an acid in which the indicator (pK of BH+ = -10.1) is 100 times more protonated than not.

pages.title: Room-Temperature Superconductivity
pages.text: $(thing)Room-Temperature Superconductivity$()$(br2)Cooper pairs that hold together at room temperature, inside a hydrogen-rich framework.

$(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Supramolecular Chemistry, Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Metal-Organic Framework.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the BCS critical temperature of a hydride superconductor from its Debye temperature and electron-phonon coupling.

pages.title: Supramolecular Chemistry
pages.text: $(thing)Supramolecular Chemistry$()$(br2)Molecules that build themselves into cages, frameworks and machines. Unlocks MOFs, clathrates and self-healing polymers.

$(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Nanochemistry, Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Graphene Sheet.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the Gibbs energy of binding (kJ/mol) of a host-guest complex with association constant K = 1e6 at 298 K.

pages.title: Self-Healing Polymer
pages.text: A rubbery strip that, cut cleanly in two, slowly finds itself again. Its chains carry reversible bonds that break and reform, so pressing the halves together lets them rebond across the seam. It is warm and a little sticky at the cut.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted a material that repaired itself the way skin does. Nanotube rope gave it strength, slime gave it reversible bonds, and a topological circuit board gave the bonds a pattern to restore. The first sample healed overnight.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Supramolecular Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Minimal Synthetic Cell.

pages.title: Supercritical Solvent
pages.text: A fluid past its critical point, neither liquid nor gas. It diffuses like a gas and dissolves like a liquid, getting into every pore. It is warm and almost invisible. Industry uses supercritical water and carbon dioxide to dissolve what nothing else will.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Heating charcoal and water past their critical point in the Chemical Reactor, the water became supercritical, dissolving things it never could before.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chiral Crystal, Graphene Sheet, Ionic Liquid, Molecular Orbital Lattice, Zeolite Catalyst.

pages.title: Unbihexium Ingot
pages.text: Element 126, the heart of the island of stability, where magic numbers for both protons and neutrons line up. Nothing this heavy should last; this does. Its surface is a dull silver that seems to swallow light.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Flerovium on its own is only the shore of the island. Pushing further meant adding supernova debris, positronium hydride to supply energy and quark-gluon plasma for neutrons. The Nuclide Forge produced element 126 and it stayed.
Made in $(item)Nuclide Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Island of Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Panspermia Seed.

pages.title: Zeolite Catalyst
pages.text: An aluminosilicate crystal riddled with channels the width of a single molecule. Anything that fits inside is held in exactly the right pose to react, so reactions that would idle in open air happen in a blink. It is light, chalky and faintly gritty, like pumice that remembers being a mineral.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Clay and quartz dissolved in supercritical solvent recrystallised into a sponge of perfect pores. With a pinch of Cherenkov quartz as a template the channels came out uniform, and molecules small enough to enter came out changed.

Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Chemical Bonding.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Autocatalytic Broth, Bioreactor, Engineered Enzyme, Graphene Sheet, Molecular Orbital Lattice, Nutrient Broth.

pages.title: Nuclide Forge
pages.text: A heavy-ion accelerator firing into a spinning target: fuses nuclei into elements beyond the periodic table, aiming for the island of stability.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 4$() machine.
This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.
Fuses superheavy elements - Flerovium and Unbihexium - from the r-process.

pages.title: Nuclide Forge
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Flerovium Ingot, Unbihexium Ingot.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

pages.title: Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor
pages.text: Converts mass entirely into energy, E = mc^2, regulated by dilithium crystals. Nothing more efficient exists.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

When a particle meets its antiparticle, both vanish and all of their rest mass becomes energy - mostly gamma rays, via E = mc^2. Fission releases under 0.1% of the mass; annihilation releases 100%. One gram of antimatter matches dozens of kilotons of TNT.

Fuel log: it burns $(item)Antimatter Pellets$() (with a $(item)Dilithium Crystal$() as regulator) at 131,072 FE/t, or a full $(item)Annihilation Core$() at 524,288 FE/t.$(br2)It needs superfluid helium cooling. Do not skip this.

pages.title: Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (2 item and 1 fluid inputs, 0 and 1 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Neutrino Flux.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Held in a Penning trap. Do not let it touch anything.$(br2)Made in $(item)Antimatter Penning Trap$().
Porous to antimatter. It regulates annihilation reactions.$(br2)Made in $(item)Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilithium Ore in the Nether.
A controlled matter-antimatter reaction in a box.$(br2)Made in $(item)Antimatter Penning Trap$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor$(): Mirror Matter Foundry$(li)$(item)Antimatter Pellet$(): Annihilation Core, Anticarbon Crystal, Antihelium Nucleus, Antihydrogen, Antihydrogen Crystal and more$(li)$(item)Dilithium Crystal$(): Annihilation Core, Block of Dilithium, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dilithium Crystal, Magnetar Shard and more$(li)$(item)Annihilation Core$(): Neutrino Flux

pages.title: Neutrino Condenser
pages.text: Traps the ghost particles that pass through planets without noticing. Trillions cross my hand each second, and now I can keep some.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Neutrinos are near-massless leptons that feel only the weak force (and gravity). A light-year of lead would stop only about half of them. Real detectors use kilotons of water or ice and catch a handful a day. The $(item)Neutrino Condenser$() is, frankly, cheating.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.
$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (4 item and 1 fluid inputs, 1 and 1 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Neutrino Flux, Proton Decay Residue, Sterile Neutrino.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

pages.title: Neutron Star Forge
pages.text: Recreates the crushing interior of a collapsed star: neutronium, metallic hydrogen and quark matter. Each one a state of matter no lab on Earth has held.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 4$() machine.
Note to self: this controller is too complex for a crafting grid. It has to be built on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts before ordering anything.

Why it matters: a neutron star packs more than a Sun's mass into a city-sized sphere. Gravity crushes electrons into protons, leaving neutrons held up only by degeneracy pressure. Deeper in, neutrons may dissolve into free quarks. A teaspoon would weigh about a billion tonnes.

pages.title: Neutron Star Forge
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Block of Neutronium, Bounce Core, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Frozen Photon, Liquid Metallic Hydrogen, Magnetar Shard, Pulsar Timing Crystal, Quark Star Core, Supernova Remnant.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

pages.title: Annihilation Core
pages.text: A controlled matter-antimatter reaction inside a box. Matter and antimatter meet and convert entirely into energy, the most efficient fuel possible. Dilithium slows the reaction so it releases steadily rather than all at once. It glows white-hot, but the box stays cool.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Antimatter Penning Trap I let antimatter seep through Dilithium Crystal into a superfluid helium bath. Instead of a crater, it gave me a steady glow I could tap for power.
Made in $(item)Antimatter Penning Trap$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Annihilation Power.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Neutrino Flux.

pages.title: Baryon Asymmetry Crystal
pages.text: One extra quark in every billion pairs. Everything that was not annihilated grew out of that one part in a billion.
Made in $(item)Quark-Gluon Collider$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Leptogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Baryogenesis Seed, Pocket Universe, Universe Seed.

pages.title: Bounce Core
pages.text: A universe crushed to the Planck density, where the quantum geometry of space turned the collapse around.
Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Big Crunch & the Big Bounce.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Universe Seed.

pages.title: Degenerate Armour Plate
pages.text: A slab of neutronium that should, by rights, explode back into a cloud of free neutrons the moment it leaves a star. The spacetime-alloy frame keeps the pressure on, so the plate stays degenerate: neutrons packed shoulder to shoulder, refusing by the Pauli principle to be squeezed any further.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Neutronium decompresses violently outside a star, so I tried caging a block in spacetime alloy and letting the Casimir Vacuum Press hold the vacuum around it. The neutrons stayed locked. Anything that can survive a compact star's interior can survive me.
Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Stellar Containment Plate, Theoretical Notes II.

pages.title: Horizon Containment
pages.text: Walls built to hold a region where escape velocity reaches light speed. Nothing leaves through a horizon; the walls are for what has not fallen in yet.
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Accretion Disk Reactor, Horizon Cage.

pages.title: Kilonova Ash
pages.text: Gold, platinum and lanthanides made in a second by the rapid neutron capture of a neutron-star merger, and thrown out at a fifth of the speed of light.
Made in $(item)Reflecting Telescope$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Kilonovae.

pages.title: Magnetar Shard
pages.text: A fragment of a magnetar, a neutron star with a magnetic field a thousand trillion times stronger than Earth's. Near it, atoms are stretched into needles and empty space becomes birefringent. It would wipe a credit card from the Moon, and it pulls iron from across the room.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Through the Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector I reached toward a magnetar and caught a shard. Dilithium Crystal and Sterile Neutrino kept the field from tearing it apart on the way back.

Made in $(item)Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Miniature Pulsar, Pulsar Timing Crystal, Residual Starlight, Stellar Singularity.

pages.title: Liquid Metallic Hydrogen
pages.text: Hydrogen compressed until it becomes a metal. At pressures found in the cores of gas giants, the electrons break free and conduct like copper. It flows silvery and heavy, and may be a room-temperature superconductor.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Wigner and Huntington predicted metallic hydrogen in 1935. Crushing degenerate matter with superfluid helium in the Neutron Star Forge, I found hydrogen that conducted like a metal.
Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metallic Hydrogen Ingot.

pages.title: Metallic Hydrogen Ingot
pages.text: Hydrogen compressed until its electrons are shared freely, like a metal. In the cores of Jupiter and Saturn it is the dominant form. It is probably metastable at ordinary pressure, and conducts electricity and heat beautifully. The ingot is mirror-bright and surprisingly light.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I pressed Liquid Metallic Hydrogen between Casimir Plates and cooled it. When the pressure was released, it held its metallic state. Probably. I have kept an eye on it.
Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Room-Temperature Superconductor, Theoretical Notes III.

pages.title: Neutrino Flux
pages.text: A stream of ghost particles, trillions of which pass through me every second. They barely interact with anything, so the flux is invisible, weightless and almost impossible to stop. Only rarely does one leave a blue flash.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pauli predicted the neutrino to save energy conservation. The Neutrino Condenser caught the rare few that interacted with its Cherenkov quartz, and slowly accumulated them into a flux.

Made in $(item)Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Neutrino Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Gold Ingot, Lepton Triplet, Magnetar Shard, Pulsar Timing Crystal, R-Process Cluster, Standard Model Singularity, Supernova Remnant.

pages.title: Block of Neutronium
pages.text: A cube of compacted neutronium, matter in which electrons and protons have been crushed together into neutrons. It is almost impossibly dense for its size, and dropping it on a floor would be a mistake. The surface is a smooth, dull grey.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Storing loose neutronium ingots wasted space, so I pressed nine together. The block holds its shape with nothing but the strong force, and it makes a convenient compact supply.

Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bounce Core, Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Degenerate Armour Plate, Dimensional Residue, Magnetar Shard, Neutron Star Forge, Neutronium Ingot, Proton Decay Residue and more.

pages.title: Pulsar Timing Crystal
pages.text: A crystal that ticks with the precision of a millisecond pulsar, the most regular natural clocks known. Its pulses are so stable that any drift reveals a passing gravitational wave. It flashes a faint blue on every beat, and I set my watches by it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Pulsar Timing Ore in the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field); dropped by the Pulsar Wisp (the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field)).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutron Star Forge I spun a Magnetar Shard up inside quartz, with a Chronon Capacitor to stabilise the rhythm. Neutrino Flux synchronised it with the stars, and the beat matched to the nanosecond.

Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Pulsar Timing Ore$(), in veins through the rock.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Pulsar Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Pulsar Beacon chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Causality Loop Engine, Chronal Accelerator, Exotic Matter Crystal, Horizon Containment, Multiverse Shard, Temporal Singularity.

pages.title: Quark Star Core
pages.text: The heart of a star too dense even for neutrons, where the neutrons have dissolved into free quarks. Strange matter may be stable here. It is the densest thing short of a singularity, and holding it makes my wrist ache even through the containment.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutron Star Forge, I compressed a Block of Neutronium with strange matter and supernova remnants, until the neutrons broke apart into quarks. Quark-Gluon Plasma bonded the result together.

Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Dimensional Residue, Hypernova Plasma, Miniature Quasar, Reality Anchor, Stellar Singularity.

pages.title: Kilonovae
pages.text: $(thing)Kilonovae$()$(br2)When two neutron stars merge, a few hundredths of a solar mass of neutron-rich matter is flung out, and in a second it captures neutrons up to gold and platinum. Its radioactive glow fades over days.
$(thing)Insight$(): 170$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Compact Stars, Nuclear Astrophysics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Neutron Star Merger Record, 2 Deep Sky Plate.

pages.title: Sterile Neutrino
pages.text: A neutrino that feels no force except gravity: no weak interaction, no electromagnetism, nothing. It passes through anything without a trace, which makes it a candidate for dark matter. Keeping hold of one is like trying to catch smoke with a sieve.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutrino Condenser, Degenerate Matter Chunks released neutrinos as their electrons merged into protons. Most were ordinary, but a few did not interact at all, and I trapped them by gravity alone.

Made in $(item)Neutrino Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Neutrino Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Baryon Asymmetry Crystal, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dilithium Crystal, Gold Ingot, Higgs Field Modulator, Hyperon Crystal, Lepton Triplet, Magnetar Shard and more.

pages.title: Cyclotron
pages.text: Protons spiralling outward between two copper dees, kicked across the gap twice a turn by a radio-frequency voltage that must keep exact step with them.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Set the field, then tune the RF to the protons' cyclotron frequency, f = qB/2πm (15.25 MHz per tesla). The beam reaches E = (qBR)²/2m at the extraction radius; as it gains energy its mass grows and it slips out of phase - keep the slip under 90°. Above 2.2 T the iron saturates. Beam power heats the target.
