pages.title: Category Lattice
pages.text: Objects connected by arrows, with the only rule being that arrows compose. Numbers, spaces, groups and programs all form categories, and theorems about one often transfer to the others. The lattice looks almost bare: dots and arrows, and nothing else.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I noticed that function graphs, power sets and axiom schemas all had the same shape: things and maps between them. The Formal Proof Assistant abstracted that shape into a lattice of objects and arrows.
Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Category Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Conceptual Containment Casing, Functor Bridge, Theoretical Notes III.

pages.title: Complex Plane
pages.text: The real line, with the imaginary unit laid at right angles across it, forming a flat sheet of numbers. On this plane every polynomial has all its roots, multiplication is rotation and scaling, and smooth functions become astonishingly rigid. It feels like a perfectly flat, perfectly thin pane of glass.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)With i in hand, the obvious step was to cross it with the real continuum. The Analytic Continuator held the two at right angles in a condensate until they fused into one field of numbers, two dimensions wide.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes II, Fourier Series, Fractal Set, Mathematics Singularity, Modular Form, Quaternion Crystal, Riemann Zeta Crystal, Turing Morphogen and more.

pages.title: Derivative Operator
pages.text: Take a function, look at it on a smaller and smaller scale until it looks straight, and record the slope. That is the derivative, and this operator does it at every point at once. It feels like a lens: everything seen through it is reduced to how fast it is changing.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dividing a function graph's rise by its run over an infinitesimal step gave exactly the instantaneous slope I wanted. Newton and Leibniz argued over credit; the Analytic Continuator just does it.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Calculus.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Christoffel Symbol, Differential Manifold, Hamiltonian Operator, Metric Tensor, Riemann Curvature Tensor.

pages.title: Differential Manifold
pages.text: A space that looks flat if you look closely enough, though it may curve in any way overall. Calculus works on each small flat patch, and the patches stitch together smoothly. Einstein wrote relativity on exactly this kind of stage. The object folds and flexes in the hand without ever creasing.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted calculus on a curved surface, so I glued derivative and integral operators onto a topological insulator patch by patch. The condensate smoothed the seams until no point could tell it was anywhere special.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Calculus.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Functor Bridge, Klein Bottle, Minkowski Lattice, Quantum Field Lattice, Tensor Calculus Engine.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Octonions and the Hopf fibration kept pointing at the same structure, so I fed both into the Tesseract Assembler with a G2 manifold and a little exotic matter. The lattice that came out was the one every symmetry I had studied was secretly a shadow of.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A Void Wraith leaves behind a kind of absence. Feeding that essence to the Formal Proof Assistant, I asked it to collect every element present. It returned a set and confirmed that it was empty.
Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Formal Logic.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Power Set.

pages.title: Formal Proof Tree
pages.text: A proof written so carefully that every step cites the rule that justifies it, branching back to axioms at the leaves. Machines check these line by line; mathematicians tend to trust them and move on. The tree is cool and heavy and it never contradicts itself.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mathematicians skip steps; I wanted a proof with none. Feeding an axiom schema and a function graph into a quantum processor, and wetting it with synaptic fluid, gave me a tree where every leaf was an axiom.

Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Formal Logic.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Aleph-Null Shard, Axiom of Choice, Chronon Gas, Conceptual Containment Casing, General AI Core, Godel Sentence, Mathematics Singularity, Novikov Crystal and more.

pages.title: Fourier Series
pages.text: Fourier claimed any periodic signal could be written as a sum of sines and cosines, and he was almost right. This series holds infinitely many harmonics in balance, each one a quiet tone. Hold it to your ear and it hums every frequency at once, so quietly that it sounds like silence.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Integrating a function graph against waves on the complex plane gave me one coefficient for each frequency. Adding the waves back together rebuilt the original curve exactly, and the Continuator stored the whole spectrum.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Modular Form, Wave Packet.

pages.title: Fractal Dust
pages.text: Grit with the same structure at every scale: each grain is made of smaller grains arranged exactly like the whole pile. Its dimension is not a whole number, somewhere between a scattering of points and a line. It sifts strangely, never quite settling, as if there is always more of it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Fractal Ore in the Platonic Realm; dropped by the Fractal Wyrm (the Platonic Realm).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The first handful came from a Fractal Wyrm I had cut down in the Platonic Realm, and from shelves in the old vaults. Later I learned to shave it from fractal lattice blocks with the Planck-Scale Cutter, helium keeping the cuts clean.

Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Fractal Ore$(), in veins through the Platonic Realm.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Fractal Wyrm.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Euclids Vault, Hilbert Archive chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Platonic Realm.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes I, Fractal Core, Fractal Set.

pages.title: Fractal Ore
pages.text: A vein that never resolves. Zoom in on any facet and it repeats itself in smaller copies, edges crinkling like a coastline whose length depends on the ruler you use. It has a fractional dimension somewhere between surface and solid, and it feels faintly rough no matter how finely it is polished.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Chipping at the axiom stone, I hit a seam whose outline kept getting longer the closer I measured it. Self-similarity that deep is not geology; it is a rule being iterated by the rock itself.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Platonic Realm (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Fractal Set
pages.text: Iterate z goes to z squared plus c, and colour each point by whether it escapes. The boundary that results is infinitely detailed: zoom in anywhere and new spirals, filaments and tiny copies of the whole appear. Holding it, the edges seem fuzzy, and they never sharpen however closely you look.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running a Koch crystal's self-similar rule through a function graph on the complex plane, I asked the Analytic Continuator which points stayed bounded. The answer was the Mandelbrot set, coastlines within coastlines.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes III, Mathematics Singularity, Undecidable Kernel.

pages.title: Function Graph
pages.text: A rule that sends each input to exactly one output, drawn as a curve of light through the plane. Some are smooth, some are jagged, and some are discontinuous everywhere. It hangs in the air as a luminous thread that never doubles back on itself vertically.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A photonic neuron fires once for each input it is given; aimed across the real continuum, it traced every input to its output. The Analytic Continuator kept the beam as a permanent curve rather than a flash.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Euclids Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Real Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Category Lattice, Chronoplastic Gasket, Derivative Operator, Formal Proof Tree, Fourier Series, Fractal Set, Integral Operator, Möbius Strip.

pages.title: Functor Bridge
pages.text: A map between categories that sends objects to objects and arrows to arrows while respecting composition. It lets you translate a hard problem in one area of mathematics into an easier one elsewhere. The bridge is narrow, sturdy and arched in a way that suggests symmetry.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed a structured way to pass from a category to a manifold to the octonions. The Formal Proof Assistant found a functor that carried every arrow over without breaking a composition.
Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Category Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Topos.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pulled from the walls of the Hilbert archive. Each brick is stamped with axioms in small, careful script, so I started stacking them for my own records. Ground down, they yield axiom schemata.

pages.text: A three-sphere unwound into circles, each circle linked with every other exactly once. Hopf found it in 1931, and it appears in physics from magnetic monopoles to quantum states. It is beautiful and endlessly twisting.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a hypersphere fragment with quaternions and compactified circles in the Tesseract Assembler, I found the three-sphere fibred into linked circles. I also found these in the Ordinal Spire.

Hilbert's Hotel has infinitely many rooms, all full, and still has space for a new guest: everyone just moves up by one. The key is warm, as if someone has only now handed it over.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Hilbert Bellhop (the Transfinite Hierarchy).

pages.title: Imaginary Unit
pages.text: A number whose square is minus one, which sounds like nonsense until you notice that it simply rotates the number line by a right angle. A tachyon's mass is imaginary, and this tiny bead was distilled from exactly that. It looks perfectly ordinary until you turn it, when it seems to point somewhere sideways.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A tachyon's rest mass squared is negative, so its mass itself must be an imaginary number. I condensed tachyon flux over a tachyon crystal and pinned the result against the real continuum, and the leftover factor was i.
Made in $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Complex Plane.

pages.title: Inaccessible Cardinal
pages.text: An infinity so large no smaller infinity can build it, by unions or power sets. Its existence cannot be proved from the usual axioms. The token is heavy and remote, as if seen from a great distance. Nothing reaches it.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Using a topos, aleph-one and Hilbert's Hotel key in the Cantor Diagonalizer, I tried to build a larger infinity from smaller ones. It refused, and the result was an inaccessible cardinal.
Made in $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Infinity, Absolute Notes III.

pages.title: Infinitesimal
pages.text: Smaller than every positive real, and yet not zero. Leibniz used them freely; Weierstrass banished them; Robinson brought them back rigorously as non-standard analysis. The grain looks like nothing at all, and the closer you look the further away it seems to be.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted the step size in a derivative to be truly smaller than anything. The Analytic Continuator pressed the real continuum against a quantum dot under superfluid helium, and squeezed out a number below every real but still above zero.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Real Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronoplastic Gasket, Derivative Operator, Integral Operator, Surreal Number.

pages.title: Integer Ring
pages.text: Every natural number paired with its mirror image below zero, closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication. The ring has a satisfying symmetry: turn it over and every number becomes its negative. Being a ring, you can add or multiply any two elements and never fall out of it.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Subtraction kept breaking the natural numbers; three minus five had nowhere to go. Feeding an antimatter pellet into the engine alongside a natural lattice gave each number an opposite, the way antimatter gives each particle one.
Made in $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Number Systems.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes III, Platonic Compass, Rational Field.

pages.title: Koch Crystal
pages.text: A pane whose rim is a Koch snowflake: a finite area enclosed by an infinitely long border. The glass is clear, but its edge glitters endlessly as each tiny triangle catches light. Set it against a lamp and the outline seems to keep growing as I stare.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)First turned up in a chest deep inside a Hilbert archive, wrapped like a specimen. Measuring its perimeter with finer and finer rulers, the number never settled. A border with no length is still a border.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Hilbert Archive chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Platonic Realm.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Christoffel Symbol, Fractal Set.

pages.title: Modular Form
pages.text: A function on the complex upper half-plane with so much symmetry that it is almost forced to be what it is. Modular forms connect primes, elliptic curves and string partition functions, and Wiles used them to prove Fermat's Last Theorem. This one is a slowly turning tiling of curved triangles.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a Fourier series with primes on the complex plane, I hoped for a function whose coefficients counted something arithmetic. The Analytic Continuator returned one invariant under the whole modular group, with prime patterns hiding in its expansion.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Number Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Riemann Zeta Crystal, Warm Helium.

pages.title: Omega-One
pages.text: The first ordinal that cannot be counted, the first uncountable infinity in the order of ordinals. Every countable ordinal comes before it. The token is heavy and solid, and seems to have no edges. It refuses to be listed.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Climbing past epsilon-naught in the Ordinal Recursor, I eventually ran out of countable ordinals. Combining aleph-null and cardinal shards with dark energy, I reached the first uncountable one.
Made in $(item)Ordinal Recursor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes I, Aleph-One, Continuum Shard.

pages.title: Omega
pages.text: The first ordinal after all the natural numbers, the first step into infinity. It comes after every finite number but is not the largest of anything. The token is smooth and plain, with no predecessor.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I counted the natural numbers in the Ordinal Recursor with ordinal shards and stone. When they ran out, the next step was omega. I also found tokens of it in the Ordinal Spire.

Made in $(item)Ordinal Recursor$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Ordinal Spire chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes II, Cardinal Shard, Epsilon-Naught.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The terrain in this dimension was stacked like the ordinals: 1, 2, 3, then omega, then omega plus one. I took a pick to it and found each layer gave way in exactly the expected order.

pages.text: A five-dimensional cube: its shadow in three dimensions is a nest of cubes connected corner to corner. Every face is a tesseract. Turning it in the hand, the faces fold through one another endlessly. It never stops turning.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Extending a tesseract core into a fifth dimension with a hypersphere fragment and Hopf fibration, the Tesseract Assembler built a penteract. Exotic matter held the extra dimension open.

pages.title: Power Set
pages.text: The set of all subsets of a set. Cantor proved it is always strictly larger than the set itself, even when the original is infinite. Turn it over and it seems to contain more than could possibly fit in it.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I asked the Formal Proof Assistant to list every subset of a natural number lattice, starting with the empty set. A proof tree confirmed what Cantor showed: no list of them could ever be complete.

Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Hilbert Hotel chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Set Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes II, Aleph-Null Shard, Cantor Key, Category Lattice, Continuum Shard, Epsilon-Naught, Hypersphere Fragment, Mathematics Singularity and more.

pages.title: Prime Number Ore
pages.text: Axiom stone threaded with veins that appear only at prime positions - never at a composite one, and never in a pattern I can predict. It feels slightly irregular, like counting with a missing beat. The ore is rarer deeper down.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I mined along a seam in axiom stone and found the veins only at prime intervals. The ore held numbers that could not be divided, and I kept every piece.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Platonic Realm (mine it for its drop).

In the Platonic Realm they grow wild in irregular clusters; out here they must be sieved. Each shard is sharp-edged and refuses to split.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Prime Number Ore in the Platonic Realm; dropped by the Axiom Sentinel (the Platonic Realm).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I first found these crystals scattered in the Platonic Realm's vaults and in the debris of Axiom Sentinels. Later I learned to sieve them out of a natural number lattice with a quantum processor, Eratosthenes style, discarding every multiple.

pages.title: Rational Field
pages.text: Every fraction of one integer by another, which is enough to divide by anything except zero. Between any two rationals there is another, so the field is dense everywhere, yet the square root of two is nowhere in it. It shimmers like a fine mesh that hides countless holes.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed division, so I let a Casimir plate split the integer ring into finer and finer slices, mimicking how the vacuum between plates is divided into modes. Every ratio appeared, and with them, the unsettling gaps between them.

pages.title: Riemann Zeta Crystal
pages.text: The zeta function encodes the distribution of primes in its zeros. Riemann conjectured that every non-trivial zero has real part exactly one half; nobody has proved it. This crystal grew in a single perfectly straight line, and every zero I have checked sits on it. It is cold and perfectly balanced.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Analytically continuing the sum over primes past where it converges took a modular form, the complex plane and superfluid helium to damp the noise. The crystal that formed grew along the critical line. I keep looking for a zero off it.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Hilbert Archive chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Number Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Godel Sentence, Mathematics Singularity.

pages.title: Transcendental Crystal
pages.text: Pi, e and their relatives: numbers no polynomial with integer coefficients will ever produce. Almost every real number is transcendental, yet proving any particular one is hard. The crystal never repeats its pattern, however closely you look, and it seems to go on past its own surface.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Transcendental Ore in the Platonic Realm.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I only ever found these in the Platonic Realm, tucked in Euclid's vaults and Hilbert's archives. No machine of mine can build one from algebra alone, which is exactly what transcendental means.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Transcendental Ore$(), in veins through the Platonic Realm.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Euclids Vault, Hilbert Archive chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Platonic Realm.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Crystal of Transcendence, Fractal Core, Golden Ratio Glass, Omnipotence Dust, Pleroma Crystal, Real Continuum, Transcendent Glass.

pages.title: Transcendental Ore
pages.text: Axiom stone shot through with crystals of transcendental numbers - pi, e and their kin, which are not roots of any polynomial. The veins never repeat and never end. It is cool and faintly bright. Its sparkle never repeats.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Deep in the axiom stone I found crystals whose patterns never repeated. Testing them, I found they were transcendental. I keep a sample in my notebook as a reminder.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Platonic Realm (mine it for its drop).

Each number system is built from the one before it. Every step patches a hole: you cannot subtract 5 from 3 in the naturals, or halve 1 in the integers, or square-root 2 in the rationals. So each time, I build something bigger.

pages.title: Yellowcake
pages.text: Uranium oxide concentrate, roasted out of pitchblende: a coarse yellow-brown powder, still 99.3% uranium-238.
$(thing)Found in$(): Oklo Reactor Ruin chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Isotope Separation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Uranium Hexafluoride.

Weigh a helium nucleus and it is lighter than its two protons and two neutrons were apart, by about 0.03 atomic mass units. That missing mass is the $(thing)binding energy$(): B = Δm·c², 28.3 MeV for helium-4 - several million times what a chemical bond holds.

Binding energy per nucleon rises from hydrogen to iron and falls after it. Split a heavy nucleus or fuse two light ones, and both ways climb towards iron and release energy. Fission and fusion are where this leads.

$(item)Pitchblende Ore$() lies in stone and, more often, in deepslate. It is uranium ore, and it is radioactive: its nuclei fall apart on their own, at random, but at a fixed rate. Of N₀ nuclei, N = N₀·e^(−λt) remain - half of them after each half-life.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Deepslate Pitchblende Ore or Pitchblende Ore in the Overworld; mined from Oklo Uraninite Ore in the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor), Oklo Reactor Ruin structures in the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor); dropped by the Fission Husk (the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor)); in the caches of Fallout Shelter structures in the Overworld.

Eight $(item)Raw Pitchblende$() and a little bone meal give one $(item)Radium Salt$() by hand; the $(item)Spectrograph$() does it from four. Radium is a hundred thousand times more active than the uranium it came from.

$(thing)Radiation Sickness$(): every radioactive thing you carry adds to a dose (the item tags $(thing)radioactive$() and $(thing)strongly_radioactive$()). The dose fades slowly. Past a point it brings nausea, hunger and lower maximum health. A $(item)Prussian Blue Tablet$() flushes most of it out.

The $(item)Geiger Counter$(), held in either hand, clicks for every decay it hears and shows your dose. Pack makers can turn Radiation Sickness off in the config. With Mekanism or GregTech installed the same dose also counts in their radiation; NuclearCraft's radiation reads this mod's items too.
Radium-226 decays into $(item)Radon-222$(), a gas with a half-life of 3.8 days. The $(item)Decay Chamber$() draws it off a piece of Radium Salt - which, with a 1,600-year half-life, is never used up.

Inside the chamber radon decays on a real clock, sped up so a day passes in a minute: after 5.5 minutes half of any radon is gone, after 11 minutes three quarters. Its daughters run down to lead, and each litre that decays leaves one $(item)Radiogenic Lead$().

A long-lived parent and a short-lived daughter settle into $(thing)secular equilibrium$(): the daughter is made as fast as it decays, so N₂ = N₁·T₂/T₁. A gram of radium holds only 17 micrograms of radon at any moment.

Radon's daughters give off gamma rays, so a working chamber is a source. Wall it in: two blocks of lead stop 99.6% of them. Radiogenic Lead makes $(item)Lead Shielding Plates$() and Lead Shielding Blocks; lead from any other mod works too.

From 1.2, radiation in the mod follows the physics. Every source is an $(thing)isotope$() with its real half-life and its own kind of radiation, and what reaches you falls with the $(thing)square of the distance$(): a source two blocks away gives a quarter of the dose it gives at one.

$(thing)Alpha$() particles (uranium, radium, radon) are stopped by a few centimetres of air or by skin: they harm only what you carry. $(thing)Beta$() electrons are stopped by any solid block. $(thing)Gamma$() rays pass through walls, but each block lets through only e^(−μx) of them. $(thing)Neutrons$() pass through metal and are slowed by water and anything rich in hydrogen.

For shielding, each block counts as a 5 cm slab. Lead lets through about 6% of gamma rays, iron 11%, concrete 55%, rock 58%, water 70%, wood 87%. Neutrons are the other way round: water stops 70% of them, lead almost none. Pack makers can set any block's values in the data map $(thing)theoreticalsciences:radiation_shielding$().

Every dimension has a $(thing)background$() rate: about 0.1 µSv/h in the Overworld (the real world's average), more in the Nether, more still in the End with no air above you, and none at all in the Quantum Foam. The $(item)Geiger Counter$() shows the rate where you stand in µSv/h and its count, which saturates near ten thousand a second as a real tube does.

Your $(thing)dose$() is counted in millisieverts and fades by 1% a second as the body repairs itself. Doses here are scaled up, as everything in the game's time is: sickness begins at 100 mSv and grows worse at 400, 1,000 and 2,500.

Natural uranium is 0.72% uranium-235. A reactor needs a few per cent. Roast $(item)Raw Pitchblende$() into $(item)Yellowcake$(), combine it with $(item)Fluorspar$() (the Spectrograph finds it in calcite and in geode shells) and you have $(fluid)Uranium Hexafluoride$(), a gas.

In a centrifuge spinning at hundreds of metres a second, the heavier U-238 crowds to the wall: the separation factor is α = e^(Δm v²/2RT). One stage barely helps. The $(item)Gas Centrifuge Cascade$() is a tower, one layer per stage: build the stage layer once, or stack it up to fourteen high, and every stage multiplies the ratio again.

The $(thing)cut$() is the share of each stage's feed passed upward: small cuts enrich more, large ones run faster. Spin the rotors faster for more separation, but carbon fibre bursts above about 1,500 MPa, and there is a flexural resonance near 450 m/s. Enrichment stops at 20%: reactor fuel, never more.
In a $(item)Molten Salt Reactor$() the fuel is liquid: uranium fluoride dissolved in a lithium salt, pumped through a core of graphite. Graphite slows the neutrons; the salt carries the heat out.

A chain reaction holds steady when each fission leads to exactly one more: k = η f p ε, less what leaks out and what the boron $(thing)control rods$() absorb. Too little uranium and it will not go critical at all; too much and the rods must hold it back.

Salt expands as it warms, so k falls with temperature: the reactor finds its own temperature, where k is exactly one. Keep that between 732 K, where the salt freezes, and 980 K, where the vessel creeps. More fuel or fewer rods: hotter. More flow: more power at the same temperature.

The spent salt still holds most of its uranium, plutonium bred from uranium-238, and fission products. The cascade takes it apart by fluoride volatility: back to hexafluoride, plutonium and $(item)Fission Fragment Mix$(). Plutonium makes mixed-oxide fuel salt.

Electrolysing water leaves the heavy molecules behind: a thousand millibuckets of $(fluid)Water$() give ten of $(fluid)Heavy Water$(), and electrolysing that gives $(fluid)Deuterium$(). $(item)Lithium$() is won from Deep Brine; the Gas Centrifuge Cascade enriches it to $(item)Lithium-6$().

In the $(item)Irradiation Chamber$() - a neutron source in one slot, never used up - lithium-6 catches a neutron and splits into helium and $(fluid)Tritium$(). Uranium-235 fissions into $(item)Technetium-99m$() and a spent fuel rod; plutonium fed neutrons for long enough climbs to $(item)Californium-252$(), and californium's flux turns uranium-238 into plutonium-239.

The $(item)Decontamination Scrubber$() melts fission products and spent salt into $(item)Nuclear Waste Glass$(), and takes the uranium back out of spent fuel rods. Radium decays, in the Decay Chamber, to $(item)Polonium-210$(); monazite sand gives $(item)Thorium-232$().

Hafnium-178m2 holds 2.4 MeV in each nucleus, locked in by its spin, for thirty-one years: $(thing)1.3 TJ$() a kilogram. The Cyclotron makes it from rare earths (hafnium travels with them) above 6 MeV.
The $(item)Isomer Trigger$() knocks it loose with a gamma pulse from a Cobalt-57 source, and all of it comes out at once - a great deal of power, and plain hafnium dust.

Deuterium and tritium fuse into helium-4 and a neutron, giving $(thing)17.6 MeV$(). They must be hot (10-20 keV, over a hundred million kelvin), dense, and held long enough: Lawson's $(thing)nTτ ≥ 3×10²¹ keV·s/m³$().

The $(item)Tokamak$() holds the plasma in a torus of twisted field: twelve toroidal field coils, a central solenoid, a vacuum vessel. Set the density, temperature and field; confinement grows with the field squared. Keep β - plasma pressure against magnetic - under 5%, or the plasma disrupts. The coils are superconducting: below 20 K, and below 12.5 T.
A $(item)Fusion Blanket Tile$() of lithium-6 breeds more tritium than the reaction burns. Deuterium alone burns too - but needs five times the triple product.

pages.title: Tokamak
pages.text: A ring of hydrogen plasma held off its walls by a twisted magnetic field, hot enough for deuterium and tritium to fuse.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Burns Deuterium and Tritium (or Deuterium alone, far harder) for power, leaving warm helium. Set the plasma density, its temperature and the toroidal field. Ignition needs the Lawson triple product nTτ above 3×10²¹ keV·s/m³; the energy confinement time τ grows with the field. The plasma pressure must stay below 5% of the magnetic pressure (β), or it disrupts. The coils are superconducting: keep it below 20 K, and the field below 12.5 T.

pages.title: Tokamak
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (1 item and 2 fluid inputs, 1 and 2 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Magnetized Plasma, Tritium, Warm Helium.
Made in a crafting grid.

Life's first molecules polymerise (Arrhenius, Eₐ = 60 kJ/mol) while water hydrolyses them (80 kJ/mol). Copying is imperfect: Eigen's error threshold says a genome of length L survives only if L < ln σ / µ. Sparks drive chemistry but also mutate.
$(thing)Set$(): Reactor temperature, Monomer concentration, Spark & UV flux.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Temperature swings: the error rate varies by ±10%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Error catastrophe: the genome cannot persist; The crucible cannot be held colder than its coolant.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Synthesis rate follows the yield and the energy supply.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Polymerisation rate: k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT)$(br)Hydrolysis rate: k_h = A_h·e^(−E_h/RT)$(br)Polymer yield: Y = k_p c/(k_p c + k_h)$(br)Copy error µ: µ$(br)Error threshold: L_max = ln σ / µ

Gas falling onto a black hole of mass M spirals in through a disk, heating as it goes, until it reaches the innermost stable orbit and drops in. The energy it has radiated by then is η·ṁc², and η depends on the spin a: the faster the hole spins, the closer that orbit, the more comes out. But the light pushes on the gas: its luminosity cannot exceed the Eddington limit L_E = 1.26×10³¹ (M/M☉) W.
$(thing)Set$(): Hole mass, Feed rate, Spin a.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The feed is clumpy: the accretion rate varies by ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Past the Eddington luminosity: the disk's own light has blown it apart; Nothing is being fed in.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power output follows the luminosity.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Radiative efficiency η: η(a): 0.057 at a = 0, 0.32 near a = 1$(br)Luminosity: L = η·ṁ·c²$(br)Eddington luminosity: L_E = 1.26×10³¹ (M/M☉) W$(br)Eddington ratio: λ = L/L_E

A condensate of density n carries sound at c = √(gn/m). It flows at v toward a step of depth U that speeds it to √(v² + 2kU/m) and thins it, so beyond the step it outruns its own sound: a horizon. There the flow speeds up over about a healing length, giving a surface gravity κ, and phonon pairs appear across the horizon at T_H = ħκ/2πk_B. They show only against a condensate colder than that, summed over many shots.
$(thing)Set$(): Density, Upstream flow, Step depth, Shots.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Shot-to-shot atom number: the density varies by ±3%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The trap is too warm for a condensate to form.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Fewer shots are faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Sound speed before: c = √(gn/m)$(br)Flow after the step: v₂ = √(v² + 2kU/m)$(br)Sound speed after: c₂ = c·√(n₂/n)$(br)Mach number before: v/c$(br)Mach number after: v₂/c₂$(br)Hawking temperature: T_H = ħκ/2πk_B$(br)Condensate temperature: T_c

Proton-antiproton annihilation turns mass entirely into pions: about half the energy in charged pions (p ≈ 0.35 GeV/c), a third in gamma rays, the rest in neutrinos. A magnetic nozzle can catch the charged pions if their gyroradius p/(0.3B) fits the 3 m chamber; the gammas must be stopped by shielding.
$(thing)Set$(): Nozzle field, Antimatter feed, Gamma shield.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Annihilation-point jitter: capture varies by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Gamma flux through the shield is melting the structure; Interlock: magnetic nozzle not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the magnetic nozzle quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Generator output follows the captured power.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Annihilation power: P = 2ṁc²$(br)Pion gyroradius: r_g = p/(0.3B)$(br)Capture fraction: f = 1 − r_g/R$(br)Electric power: P_e = ½P·f$(br)Gamma power: P_γ = ⅓P$(br)Escaping gammas: P_γ·e^(−x/20 cm)$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)

A specimen copies itself at a rate β; the ward clears it at its natural rate γ = 0.4 per day plus the quarantine field's own rate q. Each anomalous unit then makes R = β/(γ + q) more before it is cleared. Below 1 the specimen is contained and can be studied; the faster it grows the more there is to study - but at R above 1 it spreads through the containment. Clamp the field too hard and the specimen goes dormant and there is nothing to learn.
$(thing)Set$(): Growth rate β, Quarantine rate q.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The specimen's growth rate wanders by ±10%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): R above 1: the anomaly is spreading through the containment; The quarantine is so strong the specimen has gone dormant: nothing to study; The quarantine field is overheating the ward.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A faster-growing specimen held just below R = 1 gives the most to study.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective growth rate: β_eff = β·(1 + 0.1·d)$(br)Reproduction number R: R = β/(γ + q)$(br)Observable activity: A = β·R

The anomaly is dosed in n fractions of D. Each fraction kills a fraction exp(−αD − βD²) of its 10⁹ clonogenic cells (α = 0.3 Gy⁻¹, β = 0.03 Gy⁻²); it is resolved when none survives, with probability TCP = exp(−N₀·e^{−n(αD + βD²)}). The normal tissue around it repairs between fractions, but its damage grows as BED = nD(1 + D/3): small fractions spare it, large ones do not.
$(thing)Set$(): Dose per fraction D, Fractions n.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The anomaly's sensitivity α wanders by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The anomaly survives: too many of its clonogens are left; The dose is destroying the normal tissue around the anomaly; The resolution fields are overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The surer the resolution, the faster the work goes.

A breach is a bubble of different vacuum (Coleman-De Luccia). A wall of tension σ around a region whose energy is lower by Δε has critical radius R = 3σ/Δε, and the nucleation rate goes as exp(−B), B = 27π²σ⁴/(2Δε³). Too fast, and the bubble swallows everything.
$(thing)Set$(): Wall tension σ, Energy difference Δε, Barrier field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Vacuum energy noise: Δε·(1 ± 0.2%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Bubbles everywhere: the breach spreads beyond the chamber; Barrier not shaped: the wall cannot form; Interlock: barrier-shaping coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the barrier-shaping coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The breach runs at a fixed pace.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Critical radius: R_c = 3σ/Δε$(br)Bounce action B: B = 27π²σ⁴/(2Δε³)$(br)Bubbles per second: N = Δε·e^(−B)·V·t$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)

A grain of radius r in water is struck by molecules from every side and wanders: its mean square displacement grows as ⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt, with D = kT/(6πηr) (Einstein). Measure D and you have Boltzmann's constant, and from it Avogadro's number. The water's viscosity η falls steeply as it warms. n tracks measure ⟨x²⟩ to √(2/n); each position is found to about a tenth of the objective's resolution, 0.61λ/NA, and that error adds to the wandering.
$(thing)Set$(): Frame interval t, Tracks followed, Numerical aperture.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Convection in the cell: the drift biases the tracks by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The water in the cell has frozen; The water in the cell is boiling.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Fewer tracks and shorter intervals are faster.

Gamma-ray bursts come from anywhere in the sky, about once a day bright enough to catch. A lower trigger threshold Eth catches fainter ones (rate ∝ e^(−Eth/50 keV)) - and more noise. Over a watch of t hours the chance of catching at least one is 1 − e^(−N), N the bursts expected; the false triggers grow as t·e^(−Eth/8 keV).
$(thing)Set$(): Trigger threshold, Watch.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Background: the noise rate varies by ±20%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): .$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter watches report sooner.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Burst rate: R ∝ e^(−Eth/50)$(br)Detection chance: 1 − e^(−N)$(br)False triggers: FA ∝ t·e^(−Eth/8)

Take one mouth of a wormhole on a fast round trip: it ages less (twin paradox). Once its time lag exceeds the light-travel time between the mouths, the pair is a time machine - a closed timelike curve. Near that threshold, vacuum fluctuations pile up (Hawking's chronology protection).
$(thing)Set$(): Mouth speed, Trip duration, Mouth separation, Steering field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Mouth trajectory error: the trip speed is v·(1 ± 0.01%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): No closed timelike curve yet: the lag is shorter than the light time; Chronology protection: vacuum polarisation diverges at the Cauchy horizon; Close to the chronology horizon: the structure strains; Steering field too weak for that turnaround; Interlock: mouth-steering coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the mouth-steering coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Loops run at a fixed pace.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Lorentz factor: γ = 1/√(1 − v²)$(br)Time lag: Δt = T(1 − 1/γ)$(br)Light time: t_L = L/c$(br)Loop length: Δt − L/c$(br)Lag / light time: Δt/(L/c)$(br)Turnaround acceleration: a = γvc/(T/2)$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)

The $(item)Chronal Accelerator$() wraps a cube of space in a closed timelike shell and lets time inside run faster - x2 up to x256. Every machine, furnace, block entity of any mod, and every growing thing (crops, saplings, ores of the Bulk) inside the cube runs that many times faster.
$(thing)Right-click$() to change the speed, $(thing)sneak-right-click$() to change the size of the field (3x3x3 up to 9x9x9). A redstone signal stops it. It glows while it is working.

It is ruinous to run. Every extra tick it gives one block entity costs $(thing)65,536 FE$(); every extra random tick to a growing block 16,384 FE; and every eight extra ticks one mB of $(item)Chronon Gas$(). A single machine at x256 eats about 16.7 million FE and 32 mB of gas per tick. When it runs short it simply does nothing that tick.

Feed it energy and Chronon Gas from any side. Pack makers: the costs, the top speed and the largest field are in the common config; the block tag theoreticalsciences:not_accelerated lists blocks it will never touch. It never accelerates another accelerator, and the $(item)Chronal Field Projector$() (which only sets the rate of time for this mod's recipes) is a different thing.

Carbon dioxide absorbs the infrared the ground gives off: more of it, more heat kept, by a radiative forcing ΔF = 5.35 ln(C/C₀) W/m² (C₀ = 280 ppm). Aerosols reflect sunlight back out, about −20 W/m² per unit of optical depth. The world's temperature follows, ΔT = λΔF, with a climate sensitivity λ near 0.8 K per W/m².
$(thing)Set$(): Carbon dioxide, Aerosol optical depth.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Feedbacks: the sensitivity varies by ±10%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Runaway warming: the engine's own feedbacks are tearing it apart.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Small changes settle faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Radiative forcing: ΔF = 5.35 ln(C/C₀) − 20τ$(br)Warming: ΔT = λΔF

Shannon's source coding theorem: a source of entropy H bits per symbol can be compressed to any rate R above H - and to none below. At finite block length n, the error falls as exp(−n(R−H)²/2V). Every concept has its own entropy.
$(thing)Set$(): Code rate R, Block length n, Store field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Source drift: the concept's entropy fluctuates by ±1%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Rate below the entropy: information is destroyed; Store field too weak for that rate; Interlock: holographic-store coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the holographic-store coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter blocks compress faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Entropy H: H = −q log q − (1−q) log(1−q)$(br)Dispersion V: V = q(1−q)·log²((1−q)/q)$(br)Rate margin R − H: R − H$(br)Error probability: P_e ≈ exp(−n(R−H)²/2V)$(br)Compression ratio: 1/R$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)

Every multiblock has a $(thing)coolant loop$(): pipe a coolant into it (or click its tank with a filled container). The coolant holds the cold mass near its own temperature; whatever heat the machine makes raises it by heat/κ.

Coolants: Water and Ionic Liquid (300 K), Superfluid Helium and Liquid Antihelium (2 K), Neutrino Flux (10 K), Metallic Hydrogen and Antihydrogen (20 K), Dark Matter and Liquid Spacetime (3 K), and a Bose-Einstein Condensate at 10 mK that carries almost no heat.

Superfluid Helium comes back out as $(fluid)Warm Helium$() in the spent tank: send it to a Condensing Chamber and back. If the spent tank fills, the loop stops - and without coolant a machine only sheds heat slowly to the air.

Coils are superconductors with a critical temperature and field: Nb-Ti (tier 1) 9.2 K and 14.5 T, Nb₃Sn 18.3 K and 30 T, REBCO 92 K and 120 T, neutronium hydride 290 K and 400 T, transfinite lattice 4000 K. The usable field falls as B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²): the colder, the stronger.

Run a magnet above its critical field and it $(thing)quenches$(). Above 95% of T_c the interlock will not even let it start. So heat is not just a cost: every kilowatt raises the temperature, and with it lowers the field you can use.

A seed touches the melt and is drawn up at speed v: the melt freezes onto it, releasing its latent heat into the crystal. The heater's superheat sets the temperature gradient G at the growth front, and v/G decides what the crystal keeps - too fast, and it traps vacancies; too slow, interstitials; near the critical ratio, neither (Voronkov). An impurity is taken in only k_eff as readily as it sits in the melt; pulling slowly and stirring hard brings k_eff down to its equilibrium value (Burton-Prim-Slichter).
$(thing)Set$(): Heater temperature, Pull rate v, Rotation ω.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Convection in the melt: the superheat varies by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The melt has frozen: the heaters are below its melting point; The melt is so hot it attacks the crucible and boils off; The iridium crucible softens above 2,800 K.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The faster it is pulled, the sooner the boule is done.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Superheat: ΔT = T − T_m$(br)Gradient at the front: G ≈ G₀ + ΔT/L$(br)Voronkov ratio v/G: ξ = v/G$(br)Boundary layer: δ ∝ ω^(−1/2)$(br)Effective segregation k_eff: k_eff = k₀/(k₀ + (1 − k₀)e^(−vδ/D))$(br)Crystal purity: purity = 1 − k_eff·c₀

A proton in a field B circles at f = qB/2πm, whatever its speed - so an RF voltage at that frequency kicks it across the dees' gap at every half turn. Each turn adds energy and radius; at the edge, R, it has E = (qBR)²/2m. But its mass grows with energy (γ = 1 + E/mc²), its frequency falls, and over its turns it slips out of phase with the RF. Past about 90° the gap decelerates it.
$(thing)Set$(): Magnetic field B, RF frequency, Beam current.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Field ripple: B varies by ±0.05%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The beam has slipped out of phase with the RF; The iron yoke is saturating; The target is melting under the beam.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More current makes the isotope faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective field: B·(1 + δ)$(br)Cyclotron frequency: f = qB/2πm$(br)Beam energy: E = (qBR)²/2m$(br)Turns: N = E/2qV$(br)Phase slip: Δφ = 360°·N·|f_RF·γ/f_c − 1|$(br)Beam power: P = E·I

Two plates a hair apart exclude vacuum modes from the gap: a Casimir pressure P = π²ħc/(240a⁴) pushes them together, and the vacuum between them holds negative energy. At about 30 µm that energy density equals the dark energy of the universe.
$(thing)Set$(): Plate gap a, Plate area, Cycle rate, Plate stiffness.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Plate parallelism error: the effective gap is a·(1 + 0.5%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Casimir pull-in: the plates snap together; Thermal photons swamp the vacuum signal: cool the plates; The plate stack is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Plate area swept per second.

Dark matter streams through at ~230 km/s. A WIMP of mass m_χ hitting a nucleus of mass m_N can give it at most 2µ²v²/m_N of recoil - so match the target to the WIMP. Bolometers resolve ΔE ∝ T^(5/2): light dark matter needs millikelvin.
$(thing)Set$(): Target mass number, Recoil threshold, Detector mass, Shield field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Neutron background varies by ±30%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Threshold above the maximum recoil: nothing can be seen; Threshold inside the thermal noise; Interlock: veto-shield magnet not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the veto-shield magnet quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Collection follows the detection significance.

Rock warms by about 25 K for every kilometre down, and the water in its pores is under pressure. The mud in the well must press back harder than that pore pressure, or the well kicks; but not so hard that it fractures the rock. Between the two, weight and speed on the bit decide how fast it cuts.
$(thing)Set$(): Bit depth, Weight on bit, Rotary speed, Mud density.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Overpressured pockets: the pore pressure varies by ±3%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Kick: formation fluid is flowing into the well; Lost circulation: the mud is fracturing the rock; The diamond cutters are burning (above 700 K); The drill string is buckling under the weight.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The faster it cuts, the faster cores come up.

Collectors around a star reach the temperature where they radiate what they absorb: 394 K/√(r/AU) for a flat absorber. They run heat engines into your coolant, so Carnot sets the efficiency: closer is hotter and better, until the collectors melt.
$(thing)Set$(): Orbit radius, Pointing duty.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Stellar flare activity: collector temperature varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Collectors melting; Heat sink as hot as the collectors: no engine can run.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Generator output follows the useful flux.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Collector temperature: T = (L/(4πr²σ))^(1/4)$(br)Stellar flux: F = L/(4πr²)$(br)Carnot efficiency: η = 1 − T_cold/T_hot$(br)Useful flux: F·duty·η

Matter is run forward through the eras of an expanding universe until it reaches the temperature of its own horizon. The horizon of a de Sitter universe of Hubble rate H glows at T = ħH/(2πk_B); everything left inside cools towards it, and the work goes as fast as the entropy still left to produce. Squeeze the horizon too small and it is hot enough to boil the containment.
$(thing)Set$(): Horizon Hubble rate H, Simulated age.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The expansion rate wanders by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Too young: the stars are still burning and the protons have not decayed; The horizon is too small and too hot: the containment is boiling; The horizon casing is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The further towards maximum entropy, the faster the ember and the haze come off.

Entangled pairs are made in the middle and their halves sent to the two mouths, a distance L apart. Their fidelity falls as e^(−L/50 km) and with the weaver's temperature, (1 − T/1000 K) - and each pair a second warms it.
$(thing)Set$(): Pair rate, Mouth separation.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Path noise: the coherence length varies by ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): .$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More pairs, faster weaving.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Fidelity: F = e^(−L/ℓ)(1 − T/1000 K)

Information takes room. Bekenstein's bound says an object of radius R and energy E holds at most S = 2πRE/(ħc·ln 2) bits - so the densest things need the most energy in the least space. But squeeze energy E inside its Schwarzschild radius 2GE/c⁴ and it becomes a black hole. The richest forgings sit just outside that edge.
$(thing)Set$(): Field energy (log₁₀ J), Forging radius (log₁₀ m).$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The vacuum fluctuates: the energy actually held varies by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The forging volume is collapsing behind its own horizon; The Foundry is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The more room the bound leaves above what the forging needs, the faster it goes.

Many fluids boiled together separate only if the column is hot enough for the heaviest and the reflux high enough to keep them apart: the separation is S = R/(R+1)·exp(−|T_c − T_b|/300). The column must stay below the coils' limit.
$(thing)Set$(): Column temperature, Reflux ratio.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The mixture's boiling point wanders by ±15%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Reflux above 25: the column floods; The fluids do not separate (S below 0.2): bring the column to their boiling point; The coils are overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The cleaner the separation, the faster the Essence comes off.

Population genetics, run fast. A beneficial mutation fixes with Kimura's probability (1 − e^(−2s))/(1 − e^(−4Ns)). Too small a population and drift beats selection; too high a mutation rate and the genome melts (error catastrophe).
$(thing)Set$(): Population size, Selection coefficient, Mutation rate.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Mutagen drift: µ·(1 ± 20%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Drift dominates: selection is blind at this population size; Error catastrophe: mutations outpace selection; The culture is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Evolution proceeds as fast as adaptations fix.

A simulated Kerr-Newman black hole: mass, spin and charge, nothing else (the no-hair theorem). Its horizons, temperature and innermost stable orbit follow exactly. Cosmic censorship forbids a²+Q² > M².
$(thing)Set$(): Spin a/M, Charge Q/M, Confinement field, Mass.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Frame-dragging noise: the effective spin is a + 0.002·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): a² + Q² > M²: naked singularity - cosmic censorship violated; Charge not held: field too weak; Interlock: charge-confinement coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the charge-confinement coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Simulations run at a fixed pace.

Parts are held in optical and magnetic traps of stiffness κ. Equipartition sets the jitter: σ = √(kT/κ). To place parts to a picometre you need a stiff trap and a cold one - but light heats the trap and ultraviolet damages the parts.
$(thing)Set$(): Trap laser power, Wavelength, Tweezer field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Laser pointing noise: stiffness varies by ±3%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Photodamage: the light is breaking the parts; Interlock: magnetic-tweezer coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the magnetic-tweezer coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A stiffer trap settles faster.

A 40-tray distillation column. Fenske gives the fewest trays at total reflux, Underwood the least reflux at infinite trays, and Gilliland what lies between. The condenser must be colder than the light fraction boils.
$(thing)Set$(): Reflux ratio R, Reboiler duty, Product purity.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Feed composition drift: x_F·(1 ± 5%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Reflux below the Underwood minimum: the column pinches; Not enough trays for that purity at this reflux; Condenser too warm: the light fraction will not condense.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Product drawn off per second.

In a spinning rotor the heavier molecule crowds to the wall: the separation factor is α = e^(Δm v²/2RT). A stage passes on a fraction θ (the cut) of its feed, enriched by β = 1 + (α − 1)(1 − θ); n stages multiply the isotope ratio by βⁿ. Every layer of the tower is a stage.
$(thing)Set$(): Rotor peripheral speed, Cut θ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Rotor imbalance: the speed wanders by ±1%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Rotor stress above what carbon fibre safely holds; The rotors are sitting on a flexural resonance; Safeguards interlock: product above 20% U-235; Uranium hexafluoride freezing onto the rotor walls.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A bigger cut, and a taller tower, pass more product.

A current I flows up one rail, through the armature and back down the other. The rails' field pushes the armature with F = ½L′I² (L′ = 0.5 µH/m) along their 10 m; it leaves at v = √(2FL/m). Hitting the target it drives a shock of pressure P ≈ ½ρv². Shock synthesis needs the right pressure: too low and nothing changes, too high and the target vaporises.
$(thing)Set$(): Current, Armature mass.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Rail contact: the force varies by ±3%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The rails are eroding under the arc.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Smaller currents recharge faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Rail force: F = ½L′I²$(br)Muzzle speed: v = √(2FL/m)$(br)Impact pressure: P ≈ ½ρv²

A scalar field φ with potential V = ½m²φ² inflates while it rolls slowly: the slow-roll parameter ε = 2/φ² (in reduced Planck units) must stay below 1, and the number of e-folds N = (φ₀² − 2)/4 must reach about 60 to make a smooth, flat universe. Start too high, though, and quantum jumps of the field outrun its classical roll - inflation becomes eternal and the bubble never reheats.
$(thing)Set$(): Initial field φ₀, Reheating coupling Γ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Quantum fluctuations kick the starting field by ±3%·d.

Focus enough light into a small enough spot and it collapses into a black hole (the hoop conjecture). Then the hard part: a micro black hole evaporates faster the smaller it is, so it must be fed exactly as fast as it radiates - an unstable balance.

$(thing)Limits$(): Hoop conjecture not met: the pulse is not focused inside its own Schwarzschild radius.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The chamber works at a fixed pace once the hole is in range.

A gravitational wave of strain h changes the arms' lengths by ±hL/2, and the light returning to the beam splitter interferes a little differently. Four noises hide it. Shot noise - the graininess of light - falls as 1/(F√P) with the arms' finesse F and the laser power P; radiation-pressure noise - the photons' kicks on the mirrors - rises as F√P: where they are equal is the standard quantum limit. Each isolation stage cuts the ground's shaking tenfold; the thermal jiggling of the mirrors falls as √T.
$(thing)Set$(): Laser power P, Arm finesse F, Isolation stages.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Microseism: the ground shakes by ±50%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The ground shakes too hard: the arms cannot hold lock.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A clearer detection is faster; every isolation stage makes locking slower.

A mass M at distance D_l bends the light of a star behind it (at 8 kpc) into a ring of angular radius θ_E = √(4GM/c² · D_ls/D_lD_s). A star a distance u Einstein radii off the line is magnified A = (u² + 2)/(u√(u² + 4)). The aim jitters by 0.3 milliarcseconds, so a small, distant lens - a small θ_E - cannot be aimed closely. Starlight only: at night, under open sky.

The feed hops A → B with chance p each step, B → C with q, C → A with r. However it starts, it settles into the chain's steady state: the share of time in each vat is proportional to 1/(its chance of leaving), π = (1/p, 1/q, 1/r)/Σ. How fast it settles is set by the slowest hop.
$(thing)Set$(): A → B chance, B → C chance, C → A chance.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Valve wear: the A → B chance varies by ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): .$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The slowest hop sets how fast it mixes.

Nested shells around a star, each running on the waste heat of the one inside. Computation is limited by Landauer: erasing a bit costs kT·ln2, so the cold outer shell sets the price - and the coolant sets how cold it can be.
$(thing)Set$(): Inner shell radius, Number of shells, Duty.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Stellar luminosity variation: the inner shell runs at T·(1 ± 1%·d).
$(thing)Limits$(): The inner shell is melting; The core is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Computation rate follows the usable power.

A fluid of conductivity σ crossing a field B at speed u sees an electric field uB. The load takes a fraction k of it; the current density j = σuB(1 − k) flows to the electrodes, and the power per volume is p = σu²B²k(1 − k).
$(thing)Set$(): Magnetic field B, Flow speed u, Load factor k.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Magnet supply ripple: the field varies by ±1%·d.

A black hole of mass M radiates as a black body at the Hawking temperature T = ħc³/(8πGMk) - 1.2×10¹⁴ K for 10⁹ kg - and its power grows as 1/M², 356 TW at 10⁹ kg. Fed exactly what it loses, it holds its mass; fed less, it shrinks, burns hotter, and runs away.
$(thing)Set$(): Hole mass, Feed balance.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The feed is uneven: by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The hole is shrinking faster than it is fed - it is running away; The hole is growing into its own feed; Its radiation is too hot for the shield.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power follows the Hawking power.

Penning traps: a solenoid field holds antiparticles radially, an electrostatic well axially. Stable only while ω_c² > 2ω_z². Antihydrogen forms by three-body recombination, ∝ n_e²·T^(−9/2) - cold positrons, dense ones; but a plasma cannot be denser than the Brillouin limit ε₀B²/2m_e.
$(thing)Set$(): Solenoid field, Trap voltage, Positron density, RF melt power.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Positron heating: the plasma runs at T·(1 + 10%·|d|).

Each fission frees neutrons; k = η f p ε of them cause the next fission, less what leaks out and what the control rods absorb. The salt expands as it warms and k falls by 4 pcm per kelvin, so the reactor settles at the temperature where k is exactly 1. Pumping the salt through the heat exchanger carries that heat to the turbine.
$(thing)Set$(): Fuel concentration, Control rod insertion, Salt flow.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Xenon and burn-up: reactivity drifts by ±0.2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The fuel salt is freezing (below 732 K): the freeze plug has drained the core; Above 980 K the Hastelloy-N vessel creeps; Prompt critical: reactivity above the delayed-neutron fraction; No salt flow: the heat has nowhere to go.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power output follows the electric power.

Draw N random samples of a quantity of spread σ and their average is off by σ/√N: four times the work halves the error. Importance sampling draws more where it matters and cuts σ - if its proposal fits the problem; a poor one makes σ worse. Each sample erases bits, and erasing a bit gives off at least kT·ln 2 (Landauer's principle): a cold engine computes for less heat.
$(thing)Set$(): Samples (log₁₀ N), Importance sampling.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Correlations in the random stream: the error grows by up to 10%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The cores are overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More samples take longer.

Randall-Sundrum: our brane sits at the end of a warped fifth dimension, and energies there are suppressed by e^(−πkr). With kr ≈ 11 the Planck scale shrinks to TeV. The brane tensions must cancel almost exactly - the cosmological-constant problem, by hand.

$(thing)Limits$(): Brane mistuned: it inflates or crunches; The rift frame is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The rift is harvested at a fixed pace.

A neutron of wavelength λ is split by the first silicon blade, its two paths enclosing an area A, and joined at the third. Tilt the plane of the paths by α and one path climbs higher than the other: gravity changes its momentum, and the phase between them shifts by Δφ = 2πm²gλA·sin α/h². The counts at an exit follow (1 + V·cos Δφ)/2; N neutrons fix the phase to 1/(V√N).
$(thing)Set$(): Tilt α, Neutron wavelength λ, Counting time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Thermal bending of the crystal: the phase drifts by ±0.05 rad·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): .$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter counts are faster.

Matter squeezed until electrons are pressed into protons: neutron-degenerate matter, held up by the Pauli principle (P = Kρ^(5/3)). The mass and pressure you choose set the density and radius; general relativity sets the limits.

Laws as dynamical systems: the logistic map x → rx(1−x) doubles its period at r = 3, 3.449, 3.544... converging (Feigenbaum, δ = 4.669) on chaos at r∞ = 3.5699. A lattice of coupled laws synchronises only if the coupling beats the chaos: ε > 1 − e^(−λ).

A lens's power comes from its two surfaces: P = (n − 1)(C₁ − C₂), with C the curvature (one over the radius) of each, positive when it bulges toward the light. Grinding sets the curvatures; polishing then wears the surface error down, roughly exponentially with time. Below a quarter of a wavelength the image is as sharp as diffraction allows (the Rayleigh criterion).
$(thing)Set$(): Front curvature C₁, Back curvature C₂, Polishing time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Temperature of the shop: the glass expands, and the power drifts by ±0.2%·d.

Drop matter into a spinning black hole's ergosphere, split it so half falls in on a negative-energy orbit, and the other half escapes with more energy than you sent. The extra comes out of the hole's spin. Feed it angular momentum to keep it spinning.

The Echo of the Transcendental is a standing wave: it rings at its own frequency f₀ and nowhere else. The Logos coils hold it in the throat with a field B; the pump drives it. A driven resonator answers with a Lorentzian, A(f) = 1/(1 + (2Q·(f − f₀)/f₀)²): only a drive tuned to within f₀/2Q is heard at all. The playback power is the pump power the echo actually absorbs.
$(thing)Set$(): Logos coil current, Drive frequency, Pump power.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The Echo drifts: its quality factor falls to Q₀/(1 + |d|) and its frequency wanders by 0.01%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Throat field too weak to hold the Echo; Field above 70 T: the throat is tearing; More than 20 GW of drive is not being absorbed: the throat overheats; The throat is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The Transcendental rebuilds as fast as the Echo absorbs power.

Light climbing a height H in gravity g loses a fraction gH/c² of its frequency. The gamma ray of iron-57 is so sharp that this shift - a few parts in 10¹⁵ - can be seen: move the source up at v = gH/c and the Doppler shift cancels it. Counting N gamma rays measures the line's centre to its width over √N. A temperature difference between source and absorber shifts it too, by 2.2×10⁻¹⁵ a kelvin.
$(thing)Set$(): Source speed v, Counting time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Vibration of the tower: the thermal shift wanders by ±10%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): .$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter counts are faster; a taller tower measures more at once.

Every multiblock is a real machine now. Its $(thing)Operation$() console (right of its screen) has three pages.$(br2)$(thing)Controls$(): the parameters you set - fields, voltages, currents, gaps. Click a value to type it, scroll to step it.

$(thing)Readout$(): everything that follows from your settings, worked out with real equations. Hover any line for its formula. Below them, the $(thing)limits$() the machine must respect and the $(thing)recipe window$() it must be run inside.
Each recipe states a window - a beam energy, a plasma temperature, a density, a significance. JEI shows it under the recipe. If the readout is outside it, the machine waits: $(thing)Out of Window$().

Limits come in four kinds. Some simply stop the machine. Some make it $(thing)strain$() - containment wears four times as fast. Some $(thing)damage$() it every second. And some $(thing)quench$(): the stored energy dumps as heat in an instant, the containment takes a hit, and the machine needs eight seconds to recover. Enough of those and containment fails.

The $(thing)disturbance$() d (Plant page) is what the machine fights: field errors, drifting phases, impurities, outgassing. It moves while the machine runs, and every model says what it does. A Field Calibrator trims it back to zero; an Autonomous Calibrator damps it.

Structures may cross chunk borders freely. Away from home, a $(thing)chunk loader$() keeps a machine running: load every chunk the structure touches. If only some are loaded, the controller keeps the state it last saw (formed, its ports) and waits - it never reaches into an unloaded chunk.

A capacitor bank dumps a current I through a coil of N turns and length L: the field is B = μ₀NI/L. The coil's resistance turns the current into heat, ΔT ∝ NI²t over the pulse t; the magnetic pressure B²/2μ₀ pushes the coil outward. Every storey of the room is another stack of plates and its cooling: more copper to soak up the heat.

$(thing)Limits$(): The coil is melting; The magnetic pressure is tearing the coil apart.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter pulses recharge faster.

A source of flux S raises the antenna temperature by T = S·A_eff/2k. The receiver hears it over the system temperature T_sys - its own noise, the Galaxy's background (strong at low frequency), rain, and the switching noise of every machine nearby. Integrating a band B for a time τ beats the noise down: SNR = T·√(Bτ)/T_sys. A spectral line narrower than the band is diluted; a pulsar's pulse is smeared by dispersion across the band, by 8.3 µs·DM·B/ν³.
$(thing)Set$(): Frequency ν, Bandwidth B, Integration τ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Receiver gain drift: ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The dish has no view of the sky.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A clearer detection is faster; very long integrations are slower.

A fault-tolerant quantum computer. Each logical qubit is a surface-code patch of 2d² physical qubits; the logical error falls as (p/p_th)^((d+1)/2) - if the physical error p is below 1%. And p depends on temperature: hf/kT must be large, or thermal excitations flip the qubits.

$(thing)Limits$(): Above the threshold: error correction makes things worse.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Logical operations per second.

A mirror of diameter D gathers light in proportion to D², so the faintest star it records - the limiting magnitude - rises by 5·log₁₀ D, and by 2.5·log₁₀ for every tenfold longer exposure. Sunlight brings about 1000 W/m² at noon, less as the Sun sinks. Concentrated C times and let through a shutter of opening g, it heats the target until it radiates away what it absorbs: αgCG = εσT⁴. The target's temperature decides what melts - and what boils off.
$(thing)Set$(): Concentration C, Shutter opening g.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Thin cloud: the sunlight varies by ±3%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The Sun is too low (or down); Something shades the mirrors; Overcast: no sunlight to concentrate; The crucible is melting (above 3,200 K).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The hotter above its melting point, the faster the charge melts.

A tokamak (R = 6.2 m, a = 2 m): a ring of plasma confined by toroidal and poloidal fields, heated until its fuel fuses. The metals are smelted in the burning plasma.

$(thing)Limits$(): β above the Troyon limit: the plasma disrupts; Above the Greenwald density: radiative collapse, disruption; Safety factor below 2: external kink, disruption; Interlock: toroidal field coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the toroidal field coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Smelting rate follows the power heating the plasma: fusion heating plus your own.

Each mineral is stable only in part of the pressure-temperature plane, and the lines between them follow the Clapeyron slope dP/dT = ΔS/ΔV. Hold the sample on the right side of the line and keep it hot enough to react: the rate follows Arrhenius, e^(−Eₐ/RT).
$(thing)Set$(): Anvil pressure P, Furnace temperature.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Gasket creep: the sample sees P·(1 ± 2%·d).
$(thing)Limits$(): Tungsten-carbide anvils deforming above 26 GPa; The press frame is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Hotter samples react faster.

The secondary - a long winding and its toroid - rings at its own frequency, 1/2π√(L₂C₂) = 159 kHz. The primary, a capacitor and a few turns, rings at 1/2π√(L₁C₁). Only when the two agree does the energy slosh across to the secondary, where it appears as a voltage higher by √(C₁/C₂). In air an arc reaches about a metre for every 700 kV.
$(thing)Set$(): Primary capacitance, Primary turns tapped, Charging voltage.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Spark-gap jitter: the primary's frequency wanders by ±0.5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Flashover down the secondary: above 5 MV it arcs along its own winding.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Longer arcs work the charge faster.

A fifth dimension curled into a circle of radius R₅ shows up as a tower of Kaluza-Klein particles of mass nħc/R₅. A 4-cube rotated against our space casts a 3-D shadow whose volume (Cauchy) is the sum of |nᵢ| over the components of its tilt.
$(thing)Set$(): Compact radius R₅, xw rotation α, yw rotation β, Stabiliser field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Rotation-stage backlash: the xw angle is α + 0.5°·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Radion not stabilised: R₅ drifts; Interlock: radion-stabiliser coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the radion-stabiliser coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Assembly runs at a fixed pace.

A core of mass M has a Schwarzschild radius r_s = 2GM/c². Held at r from it, a sample's clock runs slower than the world's by 1/√(1 − r_s/r). The work the chamber does in its own time is that many times more, measured outside.
$(thing)Set$(): Core mass, Sample distance.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The core's mass flickers by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The samples have fallen through the horizon.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More dilation, and a bigger chamber, do more.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Schwarzschild radius: r_s = 2GM/c²$(br)Time dilation: 1/√(1 − r_s/r)

Deuterium and tritium fuse when their ions are hot enough to get close: around 10-20 keV. A plasma of density n at temperature T loses its energy over a confinement time τ, which grows with the magnetic field holding it (here τ ∝ B²). It ignites when the Lawson triple product nTτ passes 3×10²¹ keV·s/m³. The plasma's pressure pushes on the field; past β = 5% of the magnetic pressure, it disrupts.
$(thing)Set$(): Plasma density, Ion temperature, Toroidal field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Edge turbulence: the confinement time varies by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The plasma has disrupted: its pressure beat the field; The superconducting coils have quenched (too much field); The superconducting coils are too warm.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power follows the triple product.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Energy confinement time: τ ∝ B²$(br)Triple product: nTτ$(br)Plasma beta: β = 2μ₀nkT/B²

Seed a universe with a slowly rolling scalar field V = m⁴φᵖ. The slow-roll parameters at the moment the largest scales leave the horizon fix the spectrum of the universe that results: tilt n_s, amplitude A_s, gravitational waves r. Ours: n_s = 0.965, A_s = 2.1×10⁻⁹.
$(thing)Set$(): Potential power p, e-folds after CMB exit, Total e-folds, Mass scale, Trap field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Inflaton coupling noise: the power p seen is p + 0.01·d.

An electron of Lorentz factor γ, bent by a field B, circles at r = γmc/eB with proper acceleration a = γ²c²/r. An accelerated observer sees the vacuum as a thermal bath at the Unruh temperature T = ħa/(2πck_B): about 214 K per thousand of γ per tesla, here. Synchrotron radiation drains the beam as γ³B; the cavities can replace up to 500 kW.
$(thing)Set$(): Lorentz factor, Bending field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Beam energy jitter: γ varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The cavities cannot replace what the beam radiates; The bending magnets are saturating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A more energetic beam works faster.

The dynamical Casimir effect: shake a cavity mirror at twice a mode frequency and real photons are pulled out of the vacuum - parametric amplification of nothing. Here the "photons" are whatever virtual particle the Foam resonates with where you stand.
$(thing)Set$(): Resonance tuning, Modulation depth ε, Cavity quality Q, Drive field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Mirror drive phase noise: the gain varies by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Parametric instability: the photon number runs away; The cavity cannot reach that Q at this temperature; Mirror drive too weak for that modulation depth; Interlock: mirror-drive coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the mirror-drive coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Harvest rate follows the quanta created per stroke.

Alcubierre's metric moves a bubble of flat space by contracting space ahead of it and expanding it behind, at any speed v. Its wall needs negative energy, growing as v²R²σ for radius R and wall sharpness σ; the tidal shear across the wall goes as vσ; a wall that is thick for its bubble (Rσ small) is not a bubble at all.
$(thing)Set$(): Bubble speed, Bubble radius, Wall sharpness σ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Casimir supply: the negative energy needed varies by ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): More negative energy than the forge can hold.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Smaller bubbles form faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Negative energy: E ∝ −v²R²σ$(br)Wall shear: ∝ vσ$(br)Wall thinness: Rσ

A white hole only emits. But it is unstable (Eardley): any matter falling toward it piles up at its horizon until it collapses into a black hole. Keep the chamber vacuum hard and the outflow strong enough to sweep it away.
$(thing)Set$(): White hole mass, Outflow rate, Chamber vacuum, Confinement field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Chamber outgassing: the residual gas pressure fluctuates by a factor 10^(0.3·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Super-Eddington outflow batters the containment; Radiation pressure exceeds the magnetic pressure: blow-out; Interlock: confinement coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the confinement coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Ejecta production follows the outflow.

A Morris-Thorne wormhole: a throat of radius b₀ held open by exotic matter of negative energy, about b₀c²/2G of it. Cargo crossing it feels tides that grow with speed - go slowly through a wide throat.

X-rays scattered by successive planes of atoms reinforce only where the extra path between planes is a whole number of wavelengths: nλ = 2d·sin θ. A copper anode gives its Kα line, λ = 1.5406 Å - but only when the tube voltage can knock out a K-shell electron, above 8.98 kV. The count rate grows with the current and steeply with the overvoltage.
$(thing)Set$(): Tube voltage V, Tube current I, Detector angle 2θ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Thermal drift of the goniometer: the angle wanders by ±0.05°·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Below copper's K-edge: no Kα line; The anode is melting (above 2.2 kW).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More X-rays, a faster exposure.

pages.title: Crystal Growth Furnace
pages.text: A seed is dipped into the melt and drawn slowly up, turning: the melt freezes onto it as one single crystal, and the impurities stay behind.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Heat the melt a little above its melting point, pull the seed and turn it. Pull rate over the thermal gradient must sit near the critical ratio for a defect-free crystal; slow pulling and stirring leave the impurities in the melt.
