$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Beam Splitter, Echelle Grating, Einstein Ring Lens, Fluorite Lens, Fused Silica Lens, Laser Rod, Moissanite Lens, Perfect Crystal Interferometer, Photonic Lens, Sapphire Window, Schmidt Corrector Plate, Test Mass.
Made in a crafting grid.

X-rays are about as long as the gaps between atoms. Scattered by a crystal's planes, they reinforce only where the extra path between neighbouring planes is a whole number of wavelengths: $(thing)nλ = 2d·sin θ$().

The $(item)X-ray Diffractometer$() has a copper tube: above 8.98 kV it gives copper's Kα line, λ = 1.5406 Å. Set the detector angle 2θ so that θ satisfies Bragg's law for the crystal's spacing - corundum 2.551 Å, fluorite 3.155, garnet 2.584, moissanite 2.513, quartz 3.343, calcite 3.035 - and the reflection appears.

The sample comes back, with a $(item)Laue Pattern$(): the crystal's orientation, which every cut along its lattice needs. Every study gives $(thing)Insight$(). The anode melts above 2.2 kW: more current, but not too much.

In the $(item)Crystal Growth Furnace$() a seed crystal is dipped into the melt and drawn slowly up, turning - the Czochralski method. The melt freezes onto it as one crystal. Its $(item)Iridium Crucible$() is made of Iron-Nickel: a planet's core, and the iron meteorites, hoard the iridium the crust lacks.

Hold the melt a little above its melting point: the superheat sets how steeply the temperature falls at the growth front, G. Then pull at v so that $(thing)v/G$() sits near 3 - Voronkov's critical ratio: faster and the crystal traps vacancies, slower and it traps interstitials.

An impurity enters the crystal only k_eff as readily as it sits in the melt. Pull slowly and turn fast, and k_eff falls to its lowest: the impurities stay in the crucible. Optical boules must be 99.75-99.85% pure: close to the limit k₀ sets.
Sapphire from corundum (best from a whole $(item)Corundum Crystal Mass$()), fluorite from fluorspar, and garnet from garnet with a rare earth - the dopant that makes garnet a laser crystal.

Every lens is made the same way: study the crystal, grow it pure, cut it true. Three machines do it - the $(item)X-ray Diffractometer$(), the $(item)Crystal Growth Furnace$() and the $(item)Optical Workshop$() - and what they make goes into the telescopes and more.

The crystals come from everywhere: quartz and calcite from the Overworld, fluorspar from calcite and geodes, and from the Planetary Interior corundum, garnet and moissanite. Glass - fused silica - has no crystal lattice at all, so it needs no study before it is cut.

The $(item)Optical Workshop$() turns blanks into optics. A lens's power is set by its two surfaces: $(thing)P = (n − 1)(C₁ − C₂)$(), with C the curvature of each - one over its radius. A 1-dioptre lens focuses at a metre.

Polishing wears the surface error down. Below a quarter of a wavelength the image is as sharp as diffraction allows; a Schmidt corrector needs an eighth, a grating a sixteenth. Longer polishing is truer, and slower.

Fused silica becomes lenses, $(item)Schmidt Corrector Plates$() and $(item)Echelle Gratings$(). Crystals need a Laue Pattern: fluorite lenses, moissanite lenses (its index, 2.65, makes a strong lens thin) and $(item)Sapphire Windows$(), four from a boule. Fluorite between two silica lenses is an $(item)Apochromatic Objective$().
Lithography lenses are really fluorite and fused silica: the workshop makes a $(item)Photonic Lens$() from them too.

An excited atom struck by a photon of just the right energy gives off a second, identical photon: $(thing)stimulated emission$(). Fill a crystal with excited atoms, put it between two mirrors, and the light builds on itself.

A garnet boule grown with a rare earth is the crystal: neodymium in garnet lases at 1064 nm, in the infrared. Cut it along its lattice into $(item)Laser Rods$(); with mirrors, silica lenses and a flash to pump it, it becomes a $(item)Laser Head$().
Behind it sits a $(item)Faraday Isolator$(): garnet in a strong magnetic field turns polarised light the same way going and coming, so its own reflection cannot get back into the laser and upset it.

Set the tube voltage above copper's K-edge (8.98 kV) so it gives its Kα line (λ = 1.5406 Å), then the detector angle 2θ so that nλ = 2d·sin θ for the crystal's lattice spacing d. The sample comes back with a $(item)Laue Pattern$() and Insight. Keep the anode under 2.2 kW.

Hold the cell's temperature with the coolant (water stays liquid between 273 and 370 K; its viscosity falls steeply as it warms). Choose how long between frames and how many tracks to follow: the error in Avogadro's number falls as √(2/n), and the objective's resolution must be fine against how far a grain wanders in that time.

pages.title: Markov Chain Refinery
pages.text: Three vats in a ring, the feed hopping between them by tuned chances. Where it spends its time - the chain's steady state - decides what it becomes.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 4$() machine.
This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

Set the three transition chances: A to B, B to C, C to A. In a ring, the feed spends time in each vat in proportion to 1/(its chance of leaving): π ∝ (1/p, 1/q, 1/r). Each product needs its vat to hold at least three fifths of the time; thermal equilibrium needs all three nearly equal. The slowest transition sets how fast the chain mixes.

Chance has laws. Repeat an experiment n times, each a success with probability p, and exactly k successes happen with probability C(n,k)·p^k·(1 − p)^(n−k). Three heads in ten tosses: 11.7%.
Roll the $(item)Dice Set$() and add them: seven comes up a sixth of the time, two and twelve one time in thirty-six each.

$(thing)Combinatorics$() counts without listing. There are n! ways to order n things, and for large n, ln n! ≈ n ln n − n. The $(item)Quantum Random Number Chip$() draws its bits from single photons at a half-silvered mirror - the only randomness nothing can predict.
A curve made of many small chances is the $(thing)normal distribution$(): f(x) = e^(−(x−μ)²/2σ²)/(σ√2π). 68% of it lies within one width of its centre, 95% within two.

Bayes' rule turns a belief into a better one: P(H|E) = P(E|H)·P(H)/P(E). A check that is 99% reliable, for something one person in a hundred has, is right only one time in six when it says yes - because most yeses are false alarms among the many who do not have it.

The $(item)Bayesian Analyzer$() combines a $(item)Prior Tablet$() with evidence into a $(item)Posterior Tablet$(). Carry Posterior Tablets while solving research derivations: each one pays for a hint instead of Insight.

Drop a ball through rows of pegs. At each it goes left or right with even odds, so after n rows it has gone right k times with probability C(n,k)/2ⁿ. Pile up enough balls and the binomial heap becomes a bell curve: $(thing)the central limit theorem$().

The $(item)Galton Board$() sorts raw ore into ingots by where each piece lands after 12 rows: within one of the middle, one ingot (61%); two or three away, two (35%); four or more, three (4%). On average 1.43 ingots a piece.

Grains of clay in water never keep still: molecules too small to see strike them from every side, unevenly, and they wander. Einstein worked out how far: the mean square displacement grows as $(thing)⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt$(), with D = kT/(6πηr).

Measure D and you have Boltzmann's constant - and so how many molecules make a mole. The $(item)Brownian Microscope$() follows the grains in a $(item)Colloid Cell$(). The coolant sets the water's temperature, and with it the viscosity: water is three times thinner near boiling than near freezing. Keep it liquid.

Two errors. Averaging n tracks scatters by √(2/n): follow more grains. Each position is found to about a tenth of the objective's resolution, 0.61λ/NA, and that inflates ⟨x²⟩: open the aperture, or wait longer between frames so they wander further. Get Avogadro's number within 3% for an $(item)Avogadro Record$() - and the displacements, a perfect bell curve, give a Normal Distribution Crystal.

Some sums are too hard to work out. Throw dice instead: average N random samples and the answer is off by only $(thing)σ/√N$(). To halve the error, sample four times as much. The $(item)Monte Carlo Engine$() draws up to a trillion samples a run.
$(thing)Importance sampling$() draws more samples where they matter. Set near the problem's own optimum it cuts σ several times; set wrong, it makes σ worse than plain sampling.

Every sample erases bits, and $(thing)Landauer's principle$() says erasing a bit gives off at least kT·ln 2: the engine's heat is proportional to its own temperature. Cool the cores and a trillion samples cost far less.

Sums of random numbers fall on a bell curve - the central limit theorem - so the engine grows Normal Distribution Crystals; and its Markov chains sample a posterior without ever computing it, turning two Prior Tablets into four Posteriors.

At night, in the open, something drifts that has no will of its own: a cloud of particles taking an honest random walk. Near prey its steps lean toward it - a drift on top of the diffusion, the way a charged grain wanders in a field.
Its touch brings $(thing)Variance$(): luck evens out, and every good effect on you runs out twice as fast. Killed, it may leave a Normal Distribution Crystal: where it wandered, summed up.

And Maxwell's demon must forget what it sorted. Stand by a running $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$() and its erasures spill into you: $(thing)Information Loss$() - the things you hold forget their places.

The largest of n draws from a bell curve is about $(thing)√(2 ln n)$() standard deviations: five for a million draws. Rare events are rarer than average ones - but not as rare as a bell curve alone says. A Galton Board now and then sorts an Entropy Die into a $(item)Large Deviation Shard$(); the Monte Carlo Engine, tilting its samples toward the tail and weighing them back, makes one every time - slowly. A $(item)Black Swan Feather$() - proof the improbable happens - is a shortcut: with it the Pulsed Magnet Lab finds a monopole every time, and an Ergodic Mixer Core becomes a Boltzmann Brain in a tenth of the time.
The $(thing)Black Swan$() itself comes to the Overworld only after a long time - three days or more - in which nothing improbable has happened to you.

A fluctuation that costs entropy ΔS happens with odds $(thing)e^(−ΔS/k)$(). A lone brain that only thinks it remembers a world is far cheaper than a whole low-entropy universe - so in an eternal universe, which observers are likely? That is the measure problem.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Boltzmann Brain (the Accretion Frontier (Asteroid Belt, Molecular Cloud Nebula, Lensing Void)).
Boltzmann Brains fluctuate into the Accretion Frontier by chance. The sure way: an Ergodic Mixer Core and eight Entropy Dice, run for a long time through the Monte Carlo Engine.

Three vats in a ring, A → B → C → A, the feed hopping on by chances p, q and r. However it starts, it settles into the steady state: time in each vat ∝ $(thing)1/(its chance of leaving)$(). Give a vat three fifths of the time and monazite sand comes out as that vat's product: rare earths, thorium, or phosphate. Make all three equal and warm helium thermalises into $(fluid)Maxwell-Boltzmann Gas$(). The slowest hop sets how fast it mixes.
An $(item)Ergodic Mixer Core$() visits every state there is: its time average is its average over all of them (Kac: a set of measure μ is revisited every t/μ on average).

A state of energy E is found $(thing)e^(−E/kT)$() times as often as one of zero: the Boltzmann factor. Summed over every state, the factors make the partition function, and everything else - energy, entropy, pressure - is a derivative of it. The Monte Carlo Engine samples one into a $(item)Partition Function Matrix$(); a billion sorted samples make a $(item)Monte Carlo Sample Pack$().

A drunkard's walk of N steps of length l ends about $(thing)l√N$() from where it began - the reason Brownian grains wander as they do. A $(item)Markov Chain Link$() remembers only the one before it; a $(item)Poisson Clock$() ticks at random, each tick a decay in its radium. Clay stirred into water makes a $(fluid)Brownian Suspension$().
The $(item)Confidence Interval Gauge$() shows a range and how sure it is: carried in the off hand, it cancels Variance.

pages.title: Bose-Einstein Condenser
pages.text: Day 22. Cooled atoms to nanokelvin until they shared a single quantum state - a Bose-Einstein condensate, predicted in 1925, first made in 1995.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

What happens: near absolute zero each atom's wavelength grows until neighbours overlap, and bosons pile into the lowest state together, acting as one giant matter wave. The $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() does it to order.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (4 item and 2 fluid inputs, 1 and 1 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Bose-Einstein Condensate, Cryocooler Unit, False Vacuum, Metallic Hydrogen Ingot, Nanite Slurry, Psionic Ether, Quantum-Dot Photoresist, Superconducting Solder, Superfluid Helium, Synaptic Fluid, Warm Helium.

pages.title: Casimir Vacuum Press
pages.text: The $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$() squeezes matter between plates so close that the vacuum itself pushes back.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

The physics is real. Between two plates only certain vacuum fluctuations fit, so there are fewer inside than out, and the plates are pressed together. Casimir predicted it in 1948; it was measured in 1997. I find that both reassuring and unsettling.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (4 item and 1 fluid inputs, 1 and 0 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Casimir Plate, Degenerate Armour Plate, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Hawking Absorber Plate, Lattice Seed Crystal, Metamaterial Substrate, Neutronium Plate, Quadrupole Pole Tip, Quantum Dot, Solar Statite.
Made in a crafting grid.
Third dive. The Quantum Foam has a floor and a ceiling I cannot pass. Below lies $(item)Schrödinger's Limit$(), where every possibility is still undecided.

Above lies $(item)Relativity Breakdown$(), where spacetime stops being smooth - the scale where general relativity and quantum mechanics both fail at once.$(br2)Both are liquids that will not flow and cannot be crossed. Fill a cell from either and it is still there - they regenerate at once.

Schrödinger's Limit becomes the concepts of quantum mechanics in the $(item)Analytic Continuator$(): $(item)Wavefunctions$(), the $(item)Hamiltonian$(), $(item)Eigenstates$(), the $(item)Path Integral$().

Relativity Breakdown becomes $(item)Geodesics$(), $(item)Christoffel Symbols$() and the $(item)Stress-Energy Tensor$() in the $(item)Chrono Loom$(). The two great theories of the last century, bottled separately. Someday I must make them agree.

The Foam is alive:$(li)$(thing)Virtual Pairs$() drift harmlessly.$(li)$(thing)Vacuum Drifters$() only fight back; their sting is $(thing)Vacuum Decay$(): no healing.$(li)$(thing)Planck Mites$() hunt in packs; their bite $(thing)decoheres$() you.
Made in a crafting grid.
Everything a particle could be, written down at once.$(br2)Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().
Every way of getting from here to there, added up.$(br2)Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().
How the coordinates twist from one point to the next.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chrono Loom$().
Matter tells spacetime how to curve. This is what it says.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chrono Loom$().
Made in a crafting grid.

pages.title: Metamaterial Weaver
pages.text: Sketchbook. The $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$() lays down sub-wavelength lattices that bend light (and gravity) the wrong way.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

Day 37. In real metamaterials, structure smaller than a wavelength can give a negative refractive index: light bends to the wrong side of the normal. That is the trick behind laboratory invisibility cloaks. This machine weaves such lattices - and, it seems, for gravity as well.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (5 item and 2 fluid inputs, 1 and 0 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Dark Matter Lens, Dipole Winding, Dyson Shell Segment, Dyson Swarm Satellite, Gravitic Lens Element, Metamaterial Sheet, Möbius Strip, Photonic Circuit Board, Photonic Processor, Superconducting Coil.

pages.title: Bose-Einstein Condensate
pages.text: Thousands of atoms behaving as one. Chilled to within a whisper of absolute zero, they share a single wavefunction and slide as a single wave, rippling with interference fringes. It looks like a faint mist that refuses to scatter.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Seeding superfluid helium with quantum dots in the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I watched the atoms' wave packets swell until they overlapped and fused into one. Matter forgot it was many particles.

Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Calabi-Yau Manifold, Complex Plane, Differential Manifold, Hawking Correlation Record, Higgs Catalyst, Higgs Field Capacitor, Holographic Matrix, Massless Alloy and more.

pages.title: Cryocooler Unit
pages.text: A closed-cycle superfluid refrigerator. It pumps heat out of a superconducting magnet and keeps it below its critical temperature, without which the superconductor would stop superconducting. It frosts over in seconds and makes a soft, steady sigh.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)My magnets kept quenching. In the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I built a cycle where superfluid helium flowed between Casimir Plates, carrying heat out without friction. I later found a few in derelict stations.

Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block, Cryogenic Cooling Jacket, Plasma Injection Nozzle, Spacetime Alloy Coil Block.

pages.title: Cryogenic Cooling Jacket
pages.text: A jacket of containment field glass around a cryocooler, built to keep superconducting parts close to absolute zero. Frost forms on its outer face within seconds. Breath fogs in front of it, and the metal near it creaks quietly as it contracts in the cold.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Superconductors fail if they warm up. I wrapped a cryocooler unit in containment glass over spacetime casing and the parts inside stayed cold indefinitely.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.

pages.title: Crystalline Matrix Ingot
pages.text: A superposition crystal locked inside a Cherenkov lattice and fixed there by the light of a nether star. The ingot is glassy but metal-heavy, and its interior shows several overlapping lattices at once, none of them willing to collapse into the others.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Superposition crystals collapse when observed, so I sealed one inside a Cherenkov lattice and bathed it in the light of a dead star on the Extreme Assembly Table. The lattices froze mid-superposition.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst, Omnium Ingot, Transfinite Weave.

pages.title: Dimensional Residue
pages.text: The leftovers of hyperdimensional work. It is a murky, shifting fluid that contains traces of everything that passed through four dimensions. It is warm and faintly luminous, and it separates into useful fractions if distilled.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Assembling tesseracts with dark matter lenses and exotic matter, I found a residue left behind that contained fragments of everything. Distilled in the Fractionation Spire, it yielded useful matter again.

Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Geometric Topology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronon Gas, Dark Matter, Dimensional Singularity, Exotic Matter, Inflaton Field, Spacetime Slag.

pages.title: Eigenstate Lattice
pages.text: The particular states in which a measurement gives a definite value. Measure the energy, and the system will be found in one of these, no matter what it was before. The lattice is regular and seems quieter than its surroundings.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Applying the Hamiltonian to spinors and virtual photons, I searched for states it left unchanged except for a number. The Analytic Continuator arranged them into a lattice.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Quantum Singularity, Unified Notes I.

pages.title: Entangled Photon Pair
pages.text: Two photons born together and described by a single shared quantum state, so that measuring the polarisation of one fixes the other no matter how far apart they are. No signal travels between them; the correlation was there from the start. In the hand the pair is a soft double glint that never quite lines up with itself.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding Virtual Photons from the quantum foam into the Quantum Entangler, I noticed some were promoted to real light in pairs. Every pair I measured was perfectly anticorrelated. Bell would have enjoyed the tally sheets.

Made in $(item)Quantum Entangler$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Observatory Ruin chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antimatter Pellet, Coherence Stabiliser, Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor, ER Bridge Thread, Entangled Relay, Entanglement Node, Entanglement Tuner, Gauge Boson Cluster and more.

pages.title: False Vacuum Membrane
pages.text: A thin, shivering film that seems to hold two different kinds of emptiness apart. One side is our vacuum, the other a lower-energy one that would rather replace it. It is cold and faintly elastic, and I handle it the way one handles a soap bubble that could end the universe if it popped wrong.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Vacuum Drifter (the Quantum Foam).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Vacuum Drifters glide without quite touching our space. When I finally brought one down, its body collapsed and left only this skin behind - the domain wall it had been carrying around between its own vacuum and ours.
Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Vacuum Drifter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): False Vacuum.

pages.title: Foam Cache
pages.text: Held together by a bubble of stable vacuum. Spacetime at the Planck scale may seethe with fluctuations; inside, it has been made to keep still.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.

pages.title: Foam Substrate
pages.text: Spongy, effervescent matter scooped from below the Planck length. Bubbles of spacetime swell and vanish inside it so fast the block seems to fizz without making a sound. It is light, cool, and never quite the same shape twice.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Planck Mite (the Quantum Foam).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Planck Mites shed it as they scuttle through the foam. Wheeler predicted spacetime would turn frothy at the smallest scales; holding a handful of it, I can feel the froth flickering in and out of existence.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Planck Mite.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Foam Cache, Superposition Crystal, Wavefunction, Xenoplasm.

pages.title: Hall Bar Chip
pages.text: A strip of two-dimensional electrons at a kelvin and ten tesla. Its Hall resistance sits on plateaus at exactly h/(νe²): a resistance standard set by nature.
Made in $(item)Laser Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Hall Effect.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Boundary CFT Chip, Unruh Detector, Unruh Thermometer.

pages.title: Hamiltonian Operator
pages.text: The operator that answers how a quantum system evolves by telling you its energy. Schrodinger's equation is just the statement that the Hamiltonian drives time evolution. It is calm and steady, ticking quietly.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Differentiating a wavefunction with respect to time, I found the rate of change was proportional to energy. The Analytic Continuator packaged that rule into an operator.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Eigenstate Lattice, Path Integral.

pages.title: Klein Bottle
pages.text: A bottle whose neck passes through its own side to join the base from inside, so that inside and outside are the same surface. In three dimensions it must cross itself; in four it does not. This one was built in four, so its glass never touches itself and nothing can be poured into it.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Gluing two Mobius strips edge to edge needed a fourth dimension to avoid self-intersection. The Tesseract Assembler supplied it, with exotic matter to hold the surface open while I joined them.
Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Geometric Topology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Mathematics Singularity, Topos.

pages.title: Metamaterial Sheet
pages.text: A material whose properties come from its structure rather than its chemistry: a lattice of resonators smaller than a wavelength, arranged to give it a negative refractive index. Light entering it bends the wrong way, and objects behind it look subtly turned inside out. The surface is iridescent and feels like fine woven fabric.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Metamaterial Weaver let me knot quantum dots and quartz into a neutronium plate at sub-wavelength spacing, with a condensate to keep everything in phase. The first sheet bent my lamp beam backwards and I spent an hour checking it was real.

Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Metamaterials.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Analytic Continuator, Antimatter Penning Trap, Assembly Matrix, CPT Mirror, D-Brane Sheet, Dark Matter Halo Collector, Dark Matter Lens, Dipole Winding and more.

pages.title: Möbius Strip
pages.text: Take a strip, give it a half-twist and join the ends: it now has only one side and one edge. Trace the middle with a finger and you return to where you started, but on what was the other face. Cut it down the centre and it stays in one piece.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Metamaterial Weaver let me twist a sheet so its surface conducted like a topological insulator along a single path. A function graph guided the half-twist; when the ends met, both faces had become one.
Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Klein Bottle, Temporal Knot.

pages.title: Containment Cache
pages.text: A locker held in stasis by superconducting coils. Whoever sealed it meant the contents to be found exactly as they were left.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antiverse Cache, Bulk Cache, Ejecta Cache, Euclid Reliquary, Foam Cache, Hilbert Locker, Horizon Cache, Hyperreal Cache and more.

pages.title: Path Integral
pages.text: Feynman's insight: a particle takes every possible path at once, and the probabilities add up with phases. Most paths cancel; the classical one survives. The integral shimmers with countless faint trails, all overlapping.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Summing virtual quark trajectories weighted by the Hamiltonian, I found that the straight paths dominated while the rest cancelled. The Analytic Continuator kept them all.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Theory of Everything.

pages.title: Planck Mite
pages.text: $(thing)Planck Mite$(). Lives in: Quantum Foam.$(br)Drops: Foam Substrate, Virtual Monopole.

pages.title: Qubit
pages.text: A two-level quantum system held in superposition: zero and one at once, weighted by complex amplitudes, until a measurement forces it to choose. Carrying it is an exercise in restraint, because looking too closely collapses it. It feels slightly cold, and its faint glow flickers between two colours without ever settling.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Entangler I trapped one half of an Entangled Photon Pair inside a Quantum Dot. The dot's two energy levels held the photon's state cleanly, and I had my first stable qubit: a bit that refused to be either value.

Made in $(item)Quantum Entangler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antimatter Penning Trap, Axiom Schema, Chronon Capacitor, Chronon Field Inverter, Chronon Gas, Error-Correction Lattice, Femtoscale Transistor, Formal Proof Assistant and more.

pages.title: Relativity Breakdown
pages.text: The place where general relativity fails. Curvature becomes infinite and the equations stop giving answers. The fluid is cold and black, and space around it is torn. Rulers placed in it disagree with themselves, and clocks show no time at all.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)At the heart of a singularity, relativity predicts its own failure. I found a fluid where that failure was made manifest, a pool of broken spacetime.
Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Christoffel Symbol, Einstein-Rosen Core, Geodesic Thread, Stress-Energy Tensor.

pages.title: Schrödinger's Limit
pages.text: The boundary where quantum mechanics stops behaving. It is a still, cold fluid in which superpositions persist indefinitely, never collapsing. Looking at it, I see both outcomes at once. Measurements dipped into it return every answer at once.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing quantum systems to their edge, I found a limit beyond which they never collapsed. Schrodinger's cat would live and die forever here.
Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Eigenstate Lattice, Hamiltonian Operator, Path Integral, Wavefunction.

pages.title: Superconducting Coil
pages.text: A coil of wire cooled below its critical temperature, where electrical resistance drops to exactly zero. Current set running in it circulates forever, and the magnetic field it produces is steady as bedrock. It is frosted with cold and pulls gently at anything iron nearby.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Winding neutronium wire through a bath of Superfluid Helium in the Metamaterial Weaver, I watched the resistance fall off a cliff to zero. Weeks later the current was still running. Derelict stations kept spares, I later noticed.

Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Alcubierre Coil, Analytic Continuator, Antimatter Pellet, Antimatter Penning Trap, Antiproton Decelerator, Autonomous Extreme Assembler, Axiom Distiller, Cantor Diagonalizer and more.

pages.title: Superfluid Helium
pages.text: Helium so cold it flows without friction. It climbs the walls of its container in a thin film, leaks through gaps too small for any normal liquid and never stops swirling once set in motion. It is utterly clear and almost weightless in the pipe.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Distilling warm helium in the Fractionation Spire, the bottom tier collected a liquid that crept up the column walls by itself. Below the lambda point, helium-4 had lost all viscosity.

Made in $(item)Fractionation Spire$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Annihilation Core, Anomaly Containment Ward, Anomaly Resolution Engine, Antihelium Nucleus, Antihydrogen Crystal, Antimatter Pellet, Autonomous Calibrator and more.

pages.title: Superposition Crystal
pages.text: A crystal lattice that has not decided which arrangement of atoms it is in, so it occupies several configurations at once. Its outline shimmers slightly at the edges, and its weight seems to vary depending on how I hold it. Every facet reflects a slightly different room.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I placed a Qubit on a scrap of Foam Substrate in the Quantum Entangler, hoping to stabilise it. Instead the qubit's indecision spread into the substrate, and the whole lattice entered superposition without collapsing.

Made in $(item)Quantum Entangler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Transistor, Claytronic Catom, Crystalline Matrix Ingot, Error-Correction Lattice, General AI Core, Hyperframe Casing, Neural Synthesizer, Psionic Crystal and more.

pages.title: Topological Boule
pages.text: A boule doped with topological insulator, so its surface conducts and its interior never will. Sliced into wafers, each slice keeps the same protected edges. It is dark grey with a faint metallic sheen around its outside.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Growing a boule from a Lattice Seed Crystal with Topological Insulator and a condensate in the Lattice Growth Vat, I found the protected surface states grew with it, layer by layer.
Made in $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes II, Spacetime Slag, Topological Wafer, Warm Helium.

pages.title: Topological Die
pages.text: A die of topologically protected logic, cut from a braided wafer. Its anyon braids survive the cut because topology does not depend on where the edge is. It is grey and unremarkable to look at, which belies how hard it is to break.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Planck-Scale Cutter, I diced a Topological Logic Wafer, worried I would cut through the braids. Each die simply formed new protected edges where I had sliced.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Topological Processor.

pages.title: Topological Insulator
pages.text: An insulator in its interior but a conductor on its surface, and the surface states are protected by topology: no small defect or scratch can remove them, any more than a knot can be undone without cutting. It feels like dull grey glass, yet current skates around its skin without hesitation.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing a Metamaterial Sheet through a phase transition in the Topological Phase Transmuter, with a qubit to read the band structure, I saw the edge states appear and refuse to vanish no matter how I damaged the sample.

Made in $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Transistor, Calabi-Yau Manifold, Differential Manifold, Dimensional Stabiliser Matrix, Hawking Emitter, Hyperframe Casing, Möbius Strip, Plasma Nozzle Tip and more.

pages.title: Topological Logic Wafer
pages.text: A wafer of braided anyons: quasiparticles whose exchange paths store information in the topology of their braids. Errors cannot touch them, because no small disturbance can untie a braid. Its surface carries a faint woven pattern.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Lithographer, a Topological Wafer engraved through Quantum-Dot Photoresist produced anyons at the edges. Braiding them by moving the light, I wrote logic into their paths.
Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Topological Die, Warm Helium.

pages.title: Turbomolecular Vacuum Pump
pages.text: A pump whose rotor spins so fast that its blades knock gas molecules out of the chamber one by one. It whines at a pitch just below hearing. Ultra-high vacuum starts here. The rotor blades are angled like a jet turbine, and they spin faster than the eye can follow.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mechanical pumps stop at a rough vacuum. A turbomolecular rotor, driven by a superconducting coil on neutronium and spacetime casing, kicked out the remaining molecules.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryogenics.

pages.title: Vacuum Beam Pipe
pages.text: A pipe of containment field glass and metamaterial lined with Casimir plates, so the space inside is emptier than empty. A particle beam runs through it without touching anything at all. Peering inside shows nothing, not even a reflection.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Particle beams scatter off any gas. I lined containment glass with Casimir plates, which push out even virtual particles, and wrapped it in metamaterial. The beam stopped scattering.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Metamaterials.

pages.title: Vacuum Drifter
pages.text: $(thing)Vacuum Drifter$(). Lives in: Quantum Foam.$(br)Drops: False Vacuum Membrane, Virtual Graviton.

pages.title: Virtual Graviton
pages.text: A quantum of gravity that has not decided to exist yet, flickering between being and not being. It pulls faintly on everything near it, and then on nothing. Nobody has ever detected a real graviton; this one is not quite real.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Ephemeral Graviton Ore in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Vacuum Drifter (the Quantum Foam).
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Vacuum Drifters in the Quantum Foam dropped these when killed. The Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester let me catch more from between Casimir plates, cooled with superfluid helium.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Ephemeral Graviton Ore$(), in veins through the Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Vacuum Drifter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Graviton Crystal, Miniature Black Hole, Miniature Wormhole.

pages.title: Virtual Monopole
pages.text: A magnet with only one pole, borrowed from the vacuum and destined to return. Real monopoles have never been found, though grand unified theories predict them. This one pushes one end of a compass needle away and never pulls the other.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Ephemeral Monopole Ore in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Planck Mite (the Quantum Foam).
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Planck Mites in the Quantum Foam dropped these. Harvesting more from between Casimir plates, I found they only lasted as long as the superfluid helium kept them cold.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Ephemeral Monopole Ore$(), in veins through the Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Planck Mite.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Magnetic Monopole, Penteract Display, Tesseract Display.

pages.title: Virtual Pair
pages.text: $(thing)Virtual Pair$(). Lives in: Quantum Foam.$(br)Drops: Virtual Photon, Virtual Quark.

pages.title: Virtual Photon
pages.text: Light that was never emitted and will never be absorbed, existing only between two charges as the carrier of their force. It glows faintly from no direction in particular and vanishes from view when looked at directly.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Ephemeral Photon Ore in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Virtual Pair (the Quantum Foam).
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Virtual Pairs left these behind in the Quantum Foam. Later I harvested them from between Casimir plates, where they press the plates together in the Casimir effect.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Ephemeral Photon Ore$(), in veins through the Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Virtual Pair.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dyson Sphere Model, Eigenstate Lattice, Entangled Photon Pair, Galaxy in a Box, Miniature Pulsar, Miniature White Hole, Pocket Universe Display.

pages.title: Virtual Quark
pages.text: A quark borrowed from the vacuum, existing only on credit granted by the uncertainty principle. The more energy it has, the sooner it must be returned. It tugs constantly at the hand, trying to fall back into nothing.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Ephemeral Quark Ore in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Virtual Pair (the Quantum Foam).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Virtual Pairs in the Quantum Foam dropped these when they split. Later, the Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester let me pull them from between Casimir plates and keep them cold enough to stay.

Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Ephemeral Quark Ore$(), in veins through the Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Virtual Pair.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antiproton Bundle, Miniature Quasar, Path Integral, Strange & Charm Quarks, Unified Notes III, Up & Down Quarks.

pages.title: Wavefunction
pages.text: Everything a particle could be, written as one complex-valued function. Its square gives the probability of finding the particle anywhere. The function hovers above the palm as a faint, shifting haze that never settles into one shape.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a qubit with the complex plane on a foam substrate, and adding Schrodinger's Limit, I described a particle's state completely. The Analytic Continuator called it a wavefunction.
Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Quantum Foam.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Feynman Diagram, Hamiltonian Operator, Quantum Singularity.

pages.title: Weaver Casing
pages.text: Casing for a machine that stitches with entanglement. Two particles that share one state stay linked, however far apart the weave carries them.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Entanglement.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): ER=EPR Weaver.

pages.title: Quantum Entangler
pages.text: The $(item)Quantum Entangler$(): spontaneous parametric down-conversion splits photons into entangled pairs, then binds them into qubits.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

How it works for real: a pump photon enters a nonlinear crystal and splits into two lower-energy photons with correlated polarisations. Measure one and you know the other, however far away. No signal travels - Einstein's 'spooky action', but no message.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.
$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (4 item and 1 fluid inputs, 2 and 0 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Entangled Photon Pair, Qubit, Superposition Crystal.
Made in a crafting grid.
First dive. Below the Planck length, spacetime is not smooth. The $(item)Planck Diver$() takes me there.

Wheeler called it quantum foam. Inside: membranes of $(item)Foam Substrate$() between bubbles of nothing, where false-vacuum bubbles swell and pop. A false vacuum is a state that looks stable but is not the lowest - I try not to stand near them.

Matter here is borrowed. $(item)Ephemeral Ores$() condense out of the foam and vanish again a few minutes later, and anything dropped dissolves back into the vacuum within half a minute. Mine fast. (Virtual particles live on borrowed energy too: the bigger the loan, the sooner it is repaid.)

Every virtual particle has a $(thing)resonance$() that changes smoothly from place to place. The $(item)Resonance Probe$() reads all four where you stand; the strongest field decides which ore grows there.

The $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$() catches whichever particle its dial is tuned closest to - so the same harvester makes quarks in one place and gravitons fifty blocks away. Read the probe, then tune. It took me a whole afternoon of unwanted gravitons to learn that.
Shrinks you past the Planck length into the Quantum Foam. Use again to come back.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Reads the four virtual-particle resonances where you stand in the Quantum Foam.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made in $(item)Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Quantum Foam; dropped by the Planck Mite (the Quantum Foam).
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Foam Substrate$(): Foam Cache, Superposition Crystal, Wavefunction, Xenoplasm

$(thing)Dimension data: The Quantum Foam$()$(br2)$(thing)Nature$(): Gravity 1 g, 3 spatial dimensions, time x1, false vacuum vacuum.$(br2)$(thing)Carry$(): $(item)Coherence Stabiliser$() - with it, you blink a few blocks now and then.

$(thing)Ores$(): False Vacuum Bubble.$(br2)$(thing)Natives$(): Planck Mite, Vacuum Drifter, Virtual Pair.$(br2)$(thing)Landmarks$(): Anomaly Vault Quantum Foam, Ore Virtual Quark, Ore Virtual Graviton, Ore Virtual Photon, Ore Virtual Monopole.

pages.title: Topological Phase Transmuter
pages.text: The $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$() changes a material's topology without changing its chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Topology is about what survives smooth deformation: a mug and a doughnut are the same shape, one hole each. In topological materials the same atoms can sit in phases that differ only in such global properties. Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz shared the 2016 Nobel for it.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (5 item and 2 fluid inputs, 2 and 0 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Calabi-Yau Manifold, Higgs Field Capacitor, Topological Circuit Board, Topological Insulator.
Made in a crafting grid.
Final pages. Every computation the universe will ever perform, converging on a single point at the end of time: the $(item)Omega Point$(). It is the last thing you can make.

Frank Tipler's 1994 idea: a collapsing universe in which computation speeds up without limit, so infinite thought fits before the end. Cosmology has since argued against it. Mine exists anyway - and a Zero-Point Extractor will happily run on it for ten hours.
The final state of all computation. It already knows how this ends.$(br2)Made in $(item)Omnilex Engine$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Omega Point$(): Identity Kernel, Omega Simulator, Omnilex Engine, Omniscience Catalyst, Omnium Energy Cell and more

pages.title: Reality Compiler
pages.text: Bostrom asked whether we live in a simulation. The $(item)Reality Compiler$() takes it literally: if the universe is a simulation, this decompiles it.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 6$() machine.
This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

The final machine. Decompile reality into $(item)Source Code Fragments$(), forge $(item)Reality Anchors$(), and finally compile the $(item)Omega Point$() - which a Zero-Point Extractor can burn for 10 hours.$(br2)If I am wrong about the simulation, the error messages will be very interesting.

pages.title: Eye of the Event Horizon
pages.text: Final entry in this series. A captive black hole wrapped in anchors, lenses and stabilisers - used as a computer. It simulates stars, galaxies, universes, and keeps what falls out.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 7$() machine.
Note to self: this controller is too complex for a crafting grid. It has to be built on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts before ordering anything.

Why a black hole? By the $(thing)Bekenstein bound$(), a horizon holds the most information any region of space can. Bekenstein and Hawking showed its entropy scales with horizon area, not volume. If anything can hold a universe in memory, it is this.

Three simulations, each gated by coil tier:$(li)a $(thing)stellar life cycle$() (tier 4)$(li)a $(thing)galaxy$() (tier 5)$(li)a whole $(thing)cosmology$() (tier 5)$(br2)Each run returns a huge spread of materials - and $(item)Horizon Shards$().
Last note on throughput: field emitter tiers multiply its parallels, just like every other multiblock. I keep looking into the lens and feeling it look back.

pages.title: Kugelblitz Chamber
pages.text: Day 1 of the singularity work. The $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$() focuses so much light into one point that it collapses into a black hole.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

A $(thing)kugelblitz$() (German: 'ball lightning') is a real prediction of general relativity: energy curves spacetime just as mass does, so enough light in a small enough volume forms a horizon. Nobody has made one. The required intensity is absurd. Apparently, not here.

Lesson learned the hard way: while running, the singularity at its heart bends light around it ($(thing)gravitational lensing$()) and pulls in loose items and creatures. My spare tools are gone. Keep your distance.

pages.title: Kugelblitz Chamber
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Gravitational Wave Crystal, Hawking Radiation, Horizon Glass, Infall Rock, Kugelblitz Seed, Last Flash of a Black Hole, Micro Singularity, Tidal Alloy Scrap.
Made in a crafting grid.
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$(): Conceptual Singularity Compressor, Entropy Horizon, Eye of the Event Horizon

Observation log. A running singularity bends light around its horizon: the room behind it is smeared into an $(thing)Einstein ring$(), with a bright $(thing)photon ring$() at the edge of the shadow.$(br2)White holes do the opposite.

The physics: mass curves spacetime and light follows the curve. A source directly behind the hole reaches me from every side - the ring. At 1.5 Schwarzschild radii photons can orbit; that is the photon ring, the same feature the Event Horizon Telescope imaged in M87*.
Practical note: if this conflicts with a shader pack, it can be disabled in the client config ($(thing)gravitationalLensing$()). The universe will still be curved; you just won't see it.

pages.title: Biosphere Compendium
pages.text: Beef, pork, chicken, mutton, rabbit and cod, every edible animal pressed into one dense block. It smells of a farmyard, a kitchen and a fishing dock all at once. It is technically food, and absolutely not for eating.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Building the catalyst meant compressing every field of knowledge, including biology. On the Extreme Assembly Table I pressed one of each edible creature together into a single record of the food chain.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

pages.title: Burst Observatory Casing
pages.text: The shell of an observatory that waits for bursts lasting milliseconds that never repeat. It is built to sit very still for a very long time.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Burst Observatory.

pages.title: Convergence Altar
pages.text: A focus for the pedestals around it, which give up what they hold to a single point, as rays meet at the focus of a lens.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Convergence Engine.

pages.title: Block of Cosmic Neutronium
pages.text: Nine ingots of cosmic neutronium fused into a block denser than the inside of a neutron star. It is hard to pick up and harder to put down gently. It casts a faint, cold shadow even in full light. A few faint points of light swim deep inside it.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cosmic neutronium was too precious to leave loose. Pressing it into a block was easy; moving the block afterwards was not, but the supply is safe.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Singularity Energy Cell, Transcendent Cache.

pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Ingot
pages.text: Neutronium compressed together with dark matter in the heart of a star. Starlight drifts through its interior, slowly, as though it were a tiny galaxy. It is the heaviest thing I own and gives off a faint, cold glow.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Breaking a Block of Cosmic Neutronium apart by hand, I found each ingot still held its own drifting starlight. It is the strongest material I have ever worked.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Pedestal, Biosphere Compendium, Block of Cosmic Neutronium, Cantor Diagonalizer, Cosmic Flux Coupler, Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block, Dimensional Residue, Hyperdimensional Pearl and more.

pages.title: Cosmic Record Fragment
pages.text: A sliver of a disc that recorded the Big Bang, cut from Cherenkov quartz and neutronium. Play it and you hear the cosmic microwave background, a faint hiss left from the first moments of everything. It is cool and heavy, and vibrates faintly.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cherenkov quartz responds to fast particles; neutronium records pressure. Pressing them together on the Extreme Assembly Table, I found the fragment picked up the oldest signal in the universe.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

pages.title: Cosmic String Segment
pages.text: A one-dimensional defect in spacetime left over from a phase transition in the early universe: a line of trapped false vacuum, thinner than a proton but immensely heavy. Space around it is cut and rejoined with a missing wedge, so objects beside it appear doubled. It hums when it moves.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)When a White Hole Fragment emitted through a Hawking Emitter, its outflow cooled too quickly and froze into defects. In the White Hole Emitter I caught one: a filament of the early universe. A bulk monolith also held one, coiled up.

Made in $(item)White Hole Emitter$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Bulk Monolith chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): White Holes.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Circuit Board, Cosmic String Lens, Cosmic String Segment, Dark Energy, Dimensional Residue, Exotic Matter, Exotic Matter Crystal, Exotic Matter Singularity and more.

pages.title: Dense Mass Core
pages.text: A mass packed so tightly that time itself runs slow around it. Clocks set nearby lose seconds to the rest of the world, and never get them back.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Time Dilation Chamber.

pages.title: Dimensional Stabiliser
pages.text: A stabiliser that holds the number of dimensions in a region fixed while machines nearby try to change it. A dimensional stabiliser matrix sets the count, and a field emitter enforces it. Near it, corners look properly square.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hyperdimensional machines kept bleeding extra dimensions into the lab. I built a stabiliser around a dimensional stabiliser matrix with a field emitter and hyperframe casing, and the room stayed three-dimensional.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.

pages.title: Last Flash of a Black Hole
pages.text: The final second of an evaporating black hole: hotter and brighter the smaller it gets, until nothing is left but the light.
Made in $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Black Hole Era.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dark Era Haze, Heat Death Ember.

pages.title: Event Horizon Casing
pages.text: A casing with a dark metamaterial skin over spacetime casing and neutronium plate: whatever reaches it from inside does not come back out. It is utterly black and seems to absorb the edges of nearby objects.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Machines handling black holes needed housings that behaved like horizons. A metamaterial sheet that bends light around itself, over neutronium plate and spacetime casing, made a one-way wall.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dark Energy Siphon, Dark Matter Halo Collector, Entropy Horizon, Fractionation Casing, Graviton Lens Array, Kugelblitz Chamber, Mirror Matter Foundry, Nucleosynthesis Chamber and more.

pages.title: Exotic Matter
pages.text: Matter with negative energy density, the stuff wormholes and warp drives require. It pushes against gravity, bends light the wrong way, and sits in its flask like a pool of shadow that is somehow lighter than air.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Separating dimensional residue in the Fractionation Spire, one fraction refused to sink or rise in the usual way. It had negative energy density. The exotic matter of Morris and Thorne, distilled from leftovers.

Made in $(item)Fractionation Spire$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): White Holes.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Alcubierre Coil, Cherenkov Quartz, Compactified Circle, Cosmic String Lens, D-Brane Sheet, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dilithium Crystal, Dimensional Residue and more.

pages.title: Field Emitter
pages.text: A compact emitter of neutronium plate, Cherenkov quartz and a quantum dot that projects a field shaped by the dot's quantum state. Change the state, change the field. It sits warm and quiet, faintly buzzing.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Multiblocks kept needing local fields of different shapes. A quantum dot can hold a programmed state, and Cherenkov quartz can turn that state into a field. I have also found ready-made emitters in anomaly vaults.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronal Field Projector, Dark Energy Siphon, Dark Matter Halo Collector, Dimensional Lift Projector, Dimensional Stabiliser, Graviton Field Emitter, Graviton Field Projector, Hawking Radiation Collector and more.

pages.title: Gravitic Lens Element
pages.text: A dark-matter lens trimmed so its Einstein ring falls exactly where it is needed. Gravitational lensing bends light from distant objects into rings and arcs; this one is tuned to focus gravity on a chosen point. It looks like a faint distortion in empty air.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Metamaterial Weaver I trimmed a Dark Matter Lens with Metamaterial Sheet and Entangled Photon Pairs to measure the focus. Adjusting the Dark Matter, the Einstein ring settled exactly where I wanted it.

Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomaly Resolution Engine, Empirical Notes III, Graviton Field Emitter, Graviton Lens Array.

pages.title: Graviton Lens Array
pages.text: An array of gravitic lens elements that bend spacetime to focus gravitational waves, the way a glass lens bends light. Inside, the space seems to pinch toward the centre. Straight edges seen through its centre appear to bow outward, as if viewed through a thick drop of water.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Gravitational lensing is real: massive objects bend light. I set gravitic lens elements into event horizon casing over a hyperframe, and the array focused gravitational waves to a point.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Eye of the Event Horizon, Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester.

pages.title: Harmonic Pedestal
pages.text: A pedestal tuned to resonance. What is set on it rings at whole-number multiples of one frequency, as the harmonics of a single string do.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Pedestal.

pages.title: Hawking Absorber Plate
pages.text: Metamaterial tuned to soak up the thermal glow of an evaporating black hole. Hawking radiation has a characteristic spectrum, and this plate absorbs it perfectly. It is warm on its front face, cool on the back, and very black.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hawking radiation was leaking away from my experiments. In the Casimir Vacuum Press I bonded a Metamaterial Sheet to Neutronium Plate, tuning the metamaterial to the black hole spectrum.

Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Entangled Bus Bar, Entropy Horizon, Hawking Radiation, Hawking Radiation Collector, Horizon Diver, Last Flash of a Black Hole.

pages.title: Hawking Emitter
pages.text: A device that channels Hawking radiation, the faint thermal glow every black hole gives off as quantum fields near its horizon split into escaping and falling particles. It feels like holding a warm coal that slowly loses mass. The colder its source, the hotter it shines.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hawking radiation leaks in every direction, so I needed a waveguide that did not care which way it came in. A Topological Insulator does just that, and wrapping it around the glow in the Chronon Field Inverter let me point it.
Made in $(item)Chronon Field Inverter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bekenstein Crystal, Cosmic String Segment, Exotic Matter.

pages.title: Hawking Radiation
pages.text: The faint glow of a black hole evaporating. Pairs of particles at the horizon are split, one falls in and the other escapes, carrying away a sliver of the black hole's mass. It is thermal, dim and cold, and in it the hole slowly dies.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hawking showed black holes are not quite black. Feeding a Kugelblitz Seed through the Penrose Ergosphere Generator, my detectors picked up a thermal glow leaking from the horizon itself.

Made in $(item)Micro Black Hole Evaporator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bekenstein Crystal, Cosmic String Segment, Exotic Matter, Gravitational Wave Crystal, Graviton Crystal, Hawking Emitter, Residual Starlight, Spacetime Singularity and more.

pages.title: Hawking Radiation Collector
pages.text: A collector of Hawking absorber plates and entangled photons that catches the faint radiation evaporating black holes give off. It is warm, and the warmth comes from somewhere it should not. It glitters faintly with stray photons.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Black holes radiate, very faintly, as Hawking predicted. I combined absorber plates with entangled photons to catch the partners of the emitted particles and mounted them on a field emitter.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Eye of the Event Horizon.

pages.title: Horizon Shard
pages.text: A sliver of event horizon, carried out of a black hole simulating a universe of its own. By the holographic principle the horizon area stores everything that ever fell inward, so this shard is less a surface than an archive. It is black from every angle and slightly cold, as Hawking radiation would predict.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Eye of the Event Horizon computes a whole universe on a black hole's surface. Seeding a fresh simulation with a universe seed, liquid spacetime and an existing shard, I found a new sliver of horizon peeled off as the simulated cosmos ended.

pages.title: Hyperframe Casing
pages.text: A casing laced with topological insulator and superposition crystal, so that its interior exists in several overlapping configurations at once. It looks solid but sounds slightly hollow, as though echoing in a direction I cannot see.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hyperdimensional machines needed a frame that could be in more than one shape. Topological insulators conduct only on the surface and superposition crystals hold several states, and together over spacetime casing they gave the frame its depth.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronoplastic Casing, Compactification Lathe, Containment Cache, Dimensional Stabiliser, Graviton Condenser, Graviton Lens Array, Higgs Field Modulator, Hyperlattice Frame and more.

pages.title: Kugelblitz Seed
pages.text: Enough energy concentrated in one place that it collapses into a black hole under its own gravity. Energy curves spacetime just as mass does, so even pure light, focused tightly enough, falls inward. The seed hums with heat, and I never point it toward anything I value.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Kugelblitz Chamber I annihilated antimatter against strange matter inside a shell of dark matter, so none of the energy escaped. Focused enough, it stopped being light and became a horizon waiting to form.
Made in $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes I, Hawking Radiation, Micro Singularity.

pages.title: Lens Pylon
pages.text: A mast that holds mass where its curvature bends passing light. A gravitational lens has no single focal point: it brings light together along a line.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Lensing Concentrator.

pages.title: Liquid Spacetime
pages.text: Spacetime itself, flowing like a liquid. Distances inside it are fluid, and it ripples with gravitational waves when disturbed. It is cold and has no colour, only the distortion of what is behind it. Poured, it bends the light of the room around the stream.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Some theories describe spacetime as an emergent fluid. Feeding a Cosmic String Segment and raw star matter into the Eye of the Event Horizon, the simulation melted spacetime into a liquid.

Made in $(item)Eye of the Event Horizon$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmological Constant, False Vacuum, Graviton Crystal, Heat Death Remnant, Horizon Shard, Inflaton Field, Omnium Ingot, Pocket Universe and more.

pages.title: Magnetic Confinement Casing
pages.text: A casing that holds plasma away from its own walls with superconducting magnetic fields, tuned by dilithium. It works on the same principle as a tokamak. It hums, and the hum gets louder when plasma is near.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Plasma at stellar temperatures melts anything it touches. I wound superconducting coil around spacetime casing and tuned it with dilithium so the field keeps the plasma floating in the middle and away from the walls.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor, Mirror Matter Foundry, Neutron Star Forge, Nucleosynthesis Chamber, Nuclide Forge, Plasma Crucible Casing, Plasma Injection Nozzle, Stellar Containment Plate and more.

pages.title: Metric Tensor
pages.text: The object that tells you how to measure distance and time in curved spacetime: feed it two directions and it returns a number. In flat space it is simple; around stars and black holes it varies from point to point. The tensor is smooth and slightly warped when held.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Flat Minkowski geometry was not enough near massive things. I differentiated the lattice and weighted it with a neutronium plate, and the Tensor Calculus Engine returned the curved metric that described it.

Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Singularity Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Alcubierre Coil, Brane Tether, Causal Set Seed, Riemann Curvature Tensor, Spacetime Singularity, Spin Foam Lattice, Spin Network Loom, Spin Network Node and more.

pages.title: Neutronium Ingot
pages.text: One step past degenerate electrons: here the electrons have been pressed into the protons and only neutrons remain, packed shoulder to shoulder as in a neutron star. Something keeps it from springing back to ordinary matter, and I am grateful.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I first found bars of it stacked in an anomaly vault, already stabilised by someone who came before me. Working out how they held it together became the backbone of everything I built afterwards, and I have used it in nearly every machine since.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault, Crashed Satellite, Fallout Shelter Stores, Observatory Ruin chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes II, Block of Neutronium, Bose-Einstein Condenser, Brane Shifter, Casimir Vacuum Press, Chronosteel Ingot, Coherent Wiring Harness, Computronium Ingot and more.

pages.title: Neutronium Plate
pages.text: A sheet of neutron-degenerate matter rolled down to a thickness of a few femtometres, a handful of nucleons across. It is strong enough to hold back vacuum pressure and thin enough that light should barely notice it, yet it blocks everything. Bending it feels like trying to fold a mountain into a letter.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ordinary rollers simply sank into neutronium ingots. The Casimir Vacuum Press solved it: by letting the vacuum itself push from both sides, I could squeeze the ingot evenly until it spread into a plate thinner than an atomic nucleus.

Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Analytic Continuator, Bioreactor, Brane Tether, CPT Mirror, Casimir Plate, Chemical Reactor, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dipole Bending Magnet and more.

pages.title: Plasma Injection Nozzle
pages.text: A nozzle that fires plasma into a confinement chamber at a precisely controlled rate. Magnetic confinement steers it, a cryocooler keeps the coils cold, and the tip glows white when in use. The air around the tip crackles.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding plasma into a nucleosynthesis chamber needs precision. I fitted a plasma nozzle tip into magnetic confinement casing with a superconducting coil block and a cryocooler, and the plasma went exactly where I aimed.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Nucleosynthesis Chamber.

pages.title: Precision Assembly Casing
pages.text: A casing of neutronium plate around a photonic processor and a femtoscale inductor, built so that nothing inside it vibrates by more than a fraction of a proton. It is dead silent and dead still. Even the dust on it seems to settle more carefully.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Femtoscale assembly is ruined by the slightest tremor. I combined photonic processors for control with femtoscale inductors to cancel vibration, and the casing held parts steady enough to join.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Femtoscale Assembly Line, Gene Sequencer, Research Nexus.

pages.title: Primordial Harvest
pages.text: Wheat, carrot, potato, beetroot, melon and pumpkin, every staple crop combined into a single seed. It is warm and slightly damp and seems ready to sprout into all of them at once. Planting it would probably be unwise.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Agriculture belonged in the catalyst too, so I pressed every crop I could grow into one seed on the Extreme Assembly Table. It holds the genome of a whole harvest.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

pages.title: Quadrupole Focusing Magnet
pages.text: A quadrupole magnet with four pole tips that squeeze a particle beam in one direction while stretching it in the other. Pairs of them focus a beam the way lenses focus light. Its four poles alternate north and south around the bore, and the field between them is zero at the very centre.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A beam spreads as it travels. Quadrupoles focus it like lenses. I fitted quadrupole pole tips to a superconducting coil on spacetime casing and the beam stayed tight.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperion Synchrotron.

pages.title: Raw Star Matter
pages.text: The matter of a star, as simulated inside a black hole. It behaves exactly as stellar material should, because the horizon simulates it perfectly. It glows with the light of a star that does not exist.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding a Stellar Core and dark matter into the Eye of the Event Horizon, the black hole simulated a star, and the simulation left matter behind. Raw star matter, from computation.

Made in $(item)Eye of the Event Horizon$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic String Segment, Dark Energy, Exotic Matter, Exotic Matter Crystal, Horizon Shard, Liquid Spacetime, Micro Singularity, Multiverse Shard and more.

pages.title: Singularity Energy Cell
pages.text: At the centre of this cell sits a tiny singularity, wrapped in cosmic neutronium. Energy falls into it and is held behind the horizon until it is needed. The casing never warms, though it carries more than any star.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A black hole is the densest possible store of energy. Wrapping a Micro Singularity in cosmic neutronium around a vacuum cell gave me a battery whose capacity is limited only by its horizon.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnium Energy Cell.

pages.title: Solar Statite
pages.text: A light sail balanced exactly between a star's gravity and its radiation pressure, so it hovers in place without orbiting. It is mostly metamaterial, thin as a breath and much larger than it looks when folded. Unfolded indoors, it drifts toward the nearest lamp.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A Dyson swarm needs collectors that can stay put. In the Casimir Vacuum Press I backed a Metamaterial Sheet with a sliver of neutronium so the light pushing it outward balanced the pull of the star.
Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Engineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dyson Swarm Satellite.

pages.title: Stellar Containment Plate
pages.text: A plate of degenerate armour and spacetime alloy over magnetic confinement casing, built to hold back the pressure and heat of a star. It is impossibly heavy and faintly warm. Heat haze clings to its face even when the machine it guards is cold and silent.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stellar machines needed walls that would not buckle. I combined degenerate armour plate with spacetime alloy and magnetic confinement, and the plate held a star's pressure.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.

pages.title: Stellar Frame Casing
pages.text: A casing of neutronium plate over event horizon casing with a Higgs field capacitor to steady its mass. It is built to hold the weight and heat of a star, and it glows faintly gold at the seams. Standing beside it feels like standing near a hearth.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stellar machines put their housings under both gravity and heat. Event horizon casing kept the energy in, neutronium plate kept the shape, and a Higgs capacitor let me adjust the mass of the casing itself.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Stellar Lamp.

pages.title: Stellar Lamp
pages.text: A stellar frame casing with glowstone at its heart, so it shines with a warm, golden light like a small star seen through a window. It is warm to stand next to. The colour is the warm yellow of a midday sun, steady and comforting, and the seams of the casing glow brightest of all.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stellar frame casing glowed at its seams already. Adding glowstone dust turned it into a lamp that gives off starlight. It is my favourite light.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Focus Receiver.

pages.title: Superconducting Coil Block
pages.text: A drum of superconducting coil wound around spacetime casing. Current, once started, circulates in it forever with no loss at all. The field it makes tugs gently at anything metal nearby. Frost gathers along the windings, a reminder of how cold the wire must stay.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Large machines needed strong, steady fields. Winding superconducting coil around spacetime casing gave me a coil that carries current indefinitely without heating, and a magnetic field that never flags.

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronosteel Coil Block, Dipole Bending Magnet, Femtoscale Assembly Line, Neutrino Condenser, Plasma Crucible Casing, Plasma Injection Nozzle, Quark-Gluon Collider.

pages.title: Tokamak Casing

pages.title: Unruh Ring Casing

Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.

pages.title: Vacuum State Projector
pages.text: A projector that changes what empty space is. Exotic matter in its core shifts the vacuum energy of the region it covers, so the field inside is a slightly different universe. The edge of the effect shimmers.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The vacuum is not unique; there are many possible ground states. Feeding Exotic Matter Crystal into the projector stack let me nudge a region into a neighbouring one, briefly and safely.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Horizon Simulation.

pages.title: White Hole Fragment
pages.text: A shard of a white hole, the time-reverse of a black hole: a horizon nothing can enter, from which matter and light only ever pour out. General relativity allows them, though nature seems shy. It feels like holding a pressure that pushes my fingers apart.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The White Hole Emitter took Ejecta Rock and Primordial Ejecta from the far side of a horizon and pushed Hawking radiation through them in reverse. What crystallised could not be entered: a white hole in miniature.

Made in $(item)White Hole Emitter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): White Holes.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes I, Closed Timelike Curve, Cosmic String Segment, Dimensional Residue, Ejecta Rock, Exotic Matter, Miniature White Hole, Planck Shard and more.

pages.title: Penrose Ergosphere Generator
pages.text: Extracts the rotational energy of a spinning black hole via the $(thing)Penrose process$(). My first real power from a singularity.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Penrose, 1969: around a rotating hole lies the $(thing)ergosphere$(), where spacetime itself is dragged so hard nothing can stand still. Split a particle there, drop one half onto a negative-energy orbit, and the other escapes with more energy than you sent in. The hole spins down to pay for it.
Running figures: a $(item)Micro Singularity$() burns for twenty minutes at 65,536 FE/t. Energy leaves through the controller and any $(item)Interface Port$().

pages.title: White Hole Emitter
pages.text: A black hole, run backwards in time. Nothing can enter; everything comes out. The $(item)White Hole Emitter$() should not work. It does.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Theory check: the equations of general relativity are time-symmetric, so every black hole solution has a reversed twin - a $(thing)white hole$(), a horizon that can only be left, never crossed inward. None has ever been observed. Its lensing ring, I note, behaves the opposite way to a black hole's.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

pages.title: Analog Black Hole
pages.text: A condensate flowing faster than its own speed of sound: a horizon that sound cannot cross back over - and, at it, Hawking radiation of phonons.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.
