Carry a Geiger Counter.$(li)$(fluid)Basaltic Magma$(), the Interior's sea, does 10 damage a hit and Fire Resistance does not help. $(fluid)Deep Brine$() sets you alight like lava.
The floor is the $(item)Inner Core Boundary$(): solid iron under 330 GPa, which no tool yet made can break. The roof is bedrock, which the Core Drill cuts again from below.

Others have been down here before. In the Crustal Caverns stand $(thing)Deep Boreholes$(): drill holes cased in steel and abandoned two dozen blocks down, a broken drill floor at the top and a cache at the bottom of the hole.

In the Natural Reactor, lead-walled $(thing)Oklo Reactor Ruins$() are dug round the reactor seam itself - fission fragments and uraninite in the floor. Bring a Geiger Counter and radiation-plated armour; their caches hold fuel, graphite and control rods.

pages.title: Answer Pedestal
pages.text: A plinth that waits for a conclusion. When the right answer is placed on it, the surrounding proof settles into consistency and the room grows quiet. A wrong answer sits there and does nothing at all.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)At the heart of each proof chamber stood this pedestal. I understood it once I realised the whole chamber was a theorem waiting for its final line.

pages.title: Anticarbon Ore
pages.text: $(item)Anticarbon Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Anti-Gold Ore
pages.text: $(item)Anti-Gold Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Antihydrogen Ice
pages.text: $(item)Antihydrogen Ice$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Anti-Iron Ore
pages.text: $(item)Anti-Iron Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Antisilicon Ore
pages.text: $(item)Antisilicon Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Antisoil
pages.text: Soil of the Antiverse, made of antiprotons, antineutrons and positrons. It is stable only because everything around it is antimatter too; brought into contact with ordinary matter, a gram of it would release about 180 TJ.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Antiverse.

pages.title: Arbor Planks
pages.text: Planks cut from the Arbor, pale and fine-grained, with faint branching lines running along their length. The wood smells of rain and seems to grow warmer when people walk across it. Nails go in easily and never split it.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I split Arbor heartwood into planks for building. The grain branched instead of running straight, and every board I cut was slightly different.
$(thing)Used in$(): Arbor Planks Slab, Arbor Planks Stairs.

pages.title: Axiom Lamp
pages.text: A lamp that shines when its axiom is in force. Its light is steady and colourless, and when the axiom is withdrawn it simply goes dark. Rows of them read like a truth table drawn in light. Watching them, I finally understood how much of mathematics is a matter of choice.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)These lit and darkened as I flipped axiom toggles inside the proof. They showed me which postulates I had accepted, and which I had not.

pages.title: Axiom Toggle
pages.text: A switch that adopts or rejects an axiom. Flip it and the local truths rearrange; some things become provable, others not. It moves with a satisfying click, like choosing between Euclidean and hyperbolic geometry.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Inside the proof I found switches wired to the axiom lamps. Each one admitted or denied a single postulate. Solving the room meant choosing a consistent set.

pages.title: The Binary
pages.text: Two bodies coiled round each other in a tightening spiral, shedding gravitational waves. Each turn is faster than the last, until the chirp ends in a merger.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Chirp Signal Record, Merger Remnant.

pages.title: Brane Tension Fiber
pages.text: A thread pulled from a brane, the membrane on which strings end. It is strong beyond any material, because its tension is a property of spacetime rather than chemistry. It hums faintly and pulls back toward the surface it came from.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Brane Strider (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef)).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Brane Striders walk on membranes in the Bulk, and when they fell they left these threads behind. I found more in derelict stations, still taut as if attached to something invisible.
Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Brane Strider.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): D-Brane Sheet.

pages.title: Bridgmanite Ore
pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 4 and 70. Gives Bridgmanite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Bulk Cache
pages.text: Bigger on the inside: it borrows a little room from a fifth dimension. In brane cosmology our whole universe floats in such a bulk.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Transcendent Cache.

pages.title: Bulk Crystal
pages.text: A translucent crystal from the Bulk whose facets seem to point in directions I cannot quite name. Light passing through comes out a little out of phase with itself, as if it had taken a short detour through another axis.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found these growing in the Bulk where the extra dimensions are most tightly curled. Looking through one, I saw my own hand from an angle I should not have been able to see it from.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Tension Fiber, Bulk Cache, Graviton Wisp Core, Silicon Life Spore, String Coupling Crystal.

pages.title: Bulk Stone
pages.text: The bedrock of the higher-dimensional Bulk: a grey stone that seems to have more surfaces than it shows. Edges blur where the extra dimensions curl back in. It is cool and unremarkable to the touch, which is somehow worse.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Everything in the Bulk rests on this stone, and I first broke some off to see if the extra dimensions would follow it home. They did, a little - enough to make it useful in crafting.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dilaton Crystal, Hyperdimensional Pearl, Kaluza-Klein Shard, Moduli Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.

pages.title: Cardinal Ore
pages.text: Rather than order, this ore measures size. Its crystals pair up perfectly with one another, unless they come from a larger infinity, in which case some are always left over. It is heavier than it looks, and denser in every sense.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Next to ordinal veins I found a second kind of ore that refused to be sorted, only compared. Diagonal arguments on the samples always left a remainder, the clear mark of a larger cardinal.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Time Dilation Chamber Casing
pages.text: The shell of a chamber where time runs at another rate. Even on Earth, a clock a kilometre higher gains about one part in 10¹³.
Made in a crafting grid.

pages.title: Chance Tiles
pages.text: Tiles laid in no repeating order, each pattern drawn at random. Any stretch that looks designed is a coincidence the dice were always going to throw.

pages.title: Cherenkov Bricks
pages.text: Cherenkov quartz cut into small bricks, each one glowing softly blue along its edges. A wall of them looks like a shallow pool at night. They are smooth and slightly cool to the touch. Every joint carries its own thin line of blue light, so the whole wall seems sketched in glow.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I cut Cherenkov quartz into bricks to make glowing walls with more texture than plain blocks. The light catches along every seam.
$(thing)Used in$(): Cherenkov Bricks Slab, Cherenkov Bricks Stairs, Cherenkov Bricks Wall.

pages.title: Cherenkov Pillar
pages.text: A column of Cherenkov quartz that glows along its length with an even blue. Placed at a doorway it reads like a beam of light holding up the lintel. It is cool and faintly humming. Rows of them along a corridor make it feel like walking beneath a reactor pool.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pillars of Cherenkov quartz gave the labs a sense of structure and a little light. They were easy to cut and look better than they have any right to.

pages.title: Chondrite
pages.text: A stony meteorite: rock that has not melted since the planets formed. Found in craters out in open country.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Chronosteel Hazard Panel
pages.text: A chronosteel panel painted with warning stripes, used to mark doorways, machine edges and anything I do not want to walk into. The stripes look very slightly out of step with each other. Yellow and black on dull metal - a language every lab in every universe seems to share.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)After walking into a running time field once, I started marking hazards. Chronosteel panels with stripes were the clearest way to say keep out.

pages.title: Chronosteel Pillar
pages.text: A column of chronosteel, banded and fluted, that carries a load without complaint. It reflects light in a slightly delayed blur and gives a doorway the feel of an engine room. Its bands are spaced at regular intervals, like the ticks on a clock face.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Chronosteel pillars were stronger than I needed and looked better than stone. I used them to frame machine halls. They also make a reliable time reference.

pages.title: Chronosteel Plating
pages.text: Chronosteel rolled into plates and fixed to a block face. Its sheen is cool and slightly blurred, as if the surface had moved a moment before it was seen. It gives a wall a clean, mechanical look. Rivets mark each corner, set in perfectly even rows.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had spare chronosteel, so I plated walls with it. The blurred reflections are a side effect of the metal's own clock and I have grown fond of them.
$(thing)Used in$(): Chronosteel Plating Slab, Chronosteel Plating Stairs.

pages.title: Chronosteel Vent
pages.text: A chronosteel grille that lets air pass between rooms. The slats are angled to keep light out and air moving, and a faint draught always seems to be flowing through it, even when the room is still. The slats never collect dust, though I have never cleaned them.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Labs full of machines get stuffy. Chronosteel vents were the obvious fix, and they look the part. The slats were angled by trial and error until the hum of the machines dropped.

pages.title: Climate Engine Casing
pages.text: Casing for a climate engine. Earth's climate balances about 340 W/m² of incoming sunlight against heat radiated back to space.
Made in a crafting grid.

pages.title: Metamaterial Cloaking Glass
pages.text: A pane of metamaterial that bends light around itself, so the glass is nearly invisible from any angle. Only the edges betray it, as a faint distortion in the room. Walking past it, the room behind seems to shift a little too smoothly, like a painted backdrop.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Metamaterials can steer light around an object. I built them into glass to see if I could make a window that vanished, and it nearly did.

pages.title: Computronium Panel
pages.text: A panel of computronium with fine glowing traces running across its face, like a circuit board that is thinking. It is warm and faintly busy to the touch. The traces brighten when someone stands close, then fade once they walk away, as though the panel had finished noticing them.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Computronium walls were too warm as solid blocks. Thin panels gave me the look of a working computer without heating the room.

pages.title: Computronium Tiles
pages.text: Computronium cut into tiles, each one lit by faint, shifting traces. A floor of them flickers softly, as if computing something about whoever walks across it. Patterns chase each other across the joints between tiles, too fast to follow, and settle into stillness when the room empties.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I tiled a floor with computronium offcuts. It flickers gently underfoot, and I am almost sure it is only decorative. It has never miscounted anything.
$(thing)Used in$(): Computronium Tiles Slab, Computronium Tiles Stairs.

pages.title: Concentrator Mirror
pages.text: A great curved array of mirrors that gathers light from a field of heliostats onto one focus. The Odeillo furnace reaches about 3,500 °C this way.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Meteoritics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Solar Furnace.

pages.title: Core Magnetite Ore
pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 1 and 48. Gives Magnetite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Plating
pages.text: Cosmic neutronium rolled into plating, dark as space with faint pinpricks of light. A wall of it looks like a window onto the night sky that happens to be load-bearing. Running a hand over it feels like touching cold glass, and the lights inside never quite stay still.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Plating walls with cosmic neutronium was extravagant, but the effect was worth it. It is the closest thing to a sky I have indoors.

pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Tiles
pages.text: Cosmic neutronium cut into dark tiles that seem to have tiny points of light deep inside them, like stars seen through a deep well. The floor they make feels impossibly solid. The tiny lights drift very slowly if I watch them long enough, like stars wheeling over a night.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had offcuts of cosmic neutronium and laid them as tiles. The faint lights inside them were a surprise, and I left them as they were.
$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Tiles Slab, Cosmic Neutronium Tiles Stairs.

pages.title: Cyclotron Yoke
pages.text: The iron return path of a cyclotron magnet. It carries the flux back from pole to pole, so the field across the gap stays strong and even.
Made in a crafting grid.

pages.title: Deepslate Pitchblende Ore
pages.text: Found in the Overworld, between Y -64 and 0. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Overworld's deepslate (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Degenerate Matter Ore
pages.text: End stone cracked around knots of matter so compressed that its electrons are packed into the lowest states quantum mechanics permits. Pauli exclusion holds it up, not chemistry. The block is far heavier than it looks, and the pick rings against it.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the End, where dead stars seem to have been scattered, a pickaxe bounced off a seam of end stone that was much too heavy. Under the crust was matter pressed into degeneracy, like a fragment of a white dwarf.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the End (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Derrick Frame
pages.text: The tall frame over a well that carries the crown block and the whole string of pipe. The word comes from Derrick, a seventeenth-century Tyburn hangman.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Deep Borehole Surface chests.

pages.title: Dilaton Crystal
pages.text: In string theory, the dilaton is a field whose value sets the string coupling: how readily strings split and join. This crystal froze one value of it. Hold it up to the light and everything behind it looks slightly more or less substantial.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilaton Ore in the Bulk (Graviton Reef).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found these growing on the Graviton Reefs of the Bulk and inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Their facets responded to string interactions, and I realised they had frozen the dilaton field in place.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Dilaton Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, String Coupling Crystal.

pages.title: Dilaton Ore
pages.text: Pale, oddly variable mineral whose hardness seems to drift as I handle it. The dilaton is the scalar field in string theory that sets the coupling strength of strings; here it is pinned into crystal, and wherever it sits the rules of interaction loosen or tighten slightly.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the bulk stone a seam kept changing how hard my tools struck it. Plotting the variance against depth, I realised the local string coupling was shifting, a frozen dilaton field showing through the rock.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Ejecta Ore
pages.text: Scorched nuggets blown out of a white hole. They are rich in elements that should not exist together, flung up from a region that admits no entry. The surfaces are glassy from the violence of their exit.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The ejecta rock is peppered with dense, blistered lumps. I first took them for meteorites until I traced their trajectories back to a point nothing can enter.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the white hole interior (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Ex Nihilo Engine
pages.text: Creation from nothing, made a machine. It does not convert energy - it simply has it: it gives unlimited FE to every block beside it, and charges the items of every player within 16 blocks.

pages.title: Exhaust Stack
pages.text: A tall brick chimney. The hot gas inside is lighter than the air outside, so the taller the stack, the harder it draws.
Made in a crafting grid.

pages.title: Fission Fragment Seam
pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 36 and 126. Gives Fission Fragment Mix when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: False Vacuum Bubble
pages.text: A pocket of space sitting in a higher-energy vacuum than its surroundings, metastable and patient. If it tunnels down to the true vacuum it will expand at nearly light speed and rewrite everything it touches. The surface ripples softly, waiting for an excuse.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Quantum Foam.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Drifting through the quantum foam, I noticed bubbles whose interior energy did not match the vacuum outside. Coleman's false vacuum, right there. I have learned to give them a very wide berth.

pages.title: Frozen Light Ore
pages.text: Photons that fell toward a horizon and appear to have stopped. To any outside observer, their final moments are stretched forever, so the ore glows a deep, slow red that never fades. It is not hot, merely luminous and patient.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Seen from far away, anything falling into a black hole freezes at the horizon. In infall rock I found veins of that frozen light, caught at the instant it crossed and preserved there indefinitely.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the black hole interior (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Goniometer
pages.text: A precision turntable that sets sample and detector at exact angles. The detector swings twice as far as the crystal, keeping θ and 2θ in step.
Made in a crafting grid.

pages.title: Graviton Wisp Core
pages.text: The heart of a Graviton Wisp: a closed loop of string vibrating in the mode that makes a graviton. Even out of the Wisp, it pulls gently on everything nearby. It is light, but holding it gives a faint sensation of falling toward it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Graviton Wisp (the Bulk (Graviton Reef)).
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Graviton Wisps drift through the Bulk, and when one dissipated it left this behind. I found more in the Calabi-Yau Knot, still faintly attracting dust.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Graviton Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Graviton Crystal.

pages.title: Hawking Imp
pages.text: A small creature forever evaporating. Like a black hole, the smaller it gets the hotter it glows and the faster it radiates itself away.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Hawking Quanta.

pages.title: Heliostat
pages.text: A mirror that tracks the Sun on two axes. At Odeillo, sixty-three of them feed one parabolic concentrator whose focus passes 3,000 °C.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Meteoritics.

pages.title: Hexagonal Field Glass
pages.text: Glass held together by a hexagonal force field, like a honeycomb of light. Each cell glows faintly at its edges. It is strong and very slightly warm to the touch. Tapping it makes each hexagon ring separately, a soft chiming that dies away quickly.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted a stronger glass for labs. A hexagonal field pattern spread stress evenly across every cell, and the honeycomb glow came free.

pages.title: Hyperdimensional Pearl
pages.text: An ender pearl wrapped in bulk stone and cosmic neutronium and charged by a nether star. Thrown, an ordinary pearl takes you somewhere; this one would take you everywhere. It shimmers and is never quite in the place it appears to be.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ender pearls teleport through some hidden dimension. Wrapping one in bulk stone gave it access to all of them, and a nether star kept it from scattering on the Extreme Assembly Table.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

pages.title: Hyperspherical Ore
pages.text: Spheres in four dimensions leave odd traces when they intersect our three. This ore shows them as nested balls that swell and shrink as I turn the lump. It has no corners anywhere and rolls slightly uphill.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Slicing a 4-sphere with a 3-dimensional plane gives a growing then shrinking ball. In the ordinal stone I found ore whose cross-sections did exactly that as I rotated it. Something four-dimensional was buried here.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Impact Breccia
pages.text: Rock shattered and welded back together in the instant of an impact. It lines a meteorite crater's bowl and rim.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.

pages.title: Inner Core Boundary
pages.text: The floor of the Planetary Interior: the edge of the solid inner core, 5,150 km down. Iron here is crystallised under 330 GPa and about 5,400 C - as hot as the Sun's surface, yet solid because the pressure will not let it melt. No tool breaks it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Planetary Interior.

pages.title: Iridium Crucible
pages.text: A crucible of iridium, which melts at 2,446 °C and shrugs off most molten oxides. Laser crystals such as YAG are pulled from melts held in one.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Meteoritics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Crystal Growth Furnace.

pages.title: Iron Meteorite
pages.text: The iron-nickel mass of a meteorite, half buried where it struck. Found in craters out in open country.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Kaluza-Klein Shard
pages.text: Kaluza and Klein noticed that general relativity in five dimensions, with one dimension curled up small, produces electromagnetism for free. Momentum around that hidden circle appears as electric charge. The shard has a faint static charge and seems to hum slightly when spun.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Kaluza-Klein Ore in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef); dropped by the Brane Strider (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef)).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I first found these in the Bulk, among Brane Strider remains and derelict stations. Running bulk stone through Maxwell's Demon Sorter with helium, I could separate grains with momentum in the fifth dimension.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Kaluza-Klein Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Brane Strider.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Compactification Lathe, Compactified Circle, Dimensional Singularity.

pages.title: Lead Bricks
pages.text: Bricks of lead shielding. Lead is dense and has many electrons, so it stops gamma rays well - about half of them every 1.3 cm - but it does little against neutrons. Shields as well as the Lead Shielding Block.

pages.title: Lead Hazard Panel
pages.text: Lead shielding striped yellow and black to mark a radiation area. It shields as well as the Lead Shielding Block.

pages.title: Lens Phantom
pages.text: Nearly invisible: it is seen only by how it bends the light behind it into arcs and rings, the way unseen dark matter betrays itself to telescopes.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Einstein Ring Lens.

pages.title: Magnetite Bricks
pages.text: Bricks of magnetite (Fe3O4), the most magnetic mineral in nature. Iron oxide is dense, so it also shields: it stops gamma rays about two thirds as well as lead, and neutrons three times better.

pages.title: Mantle Breach
pages.text: A hole bored through bedrock by the Core Drill. Step into it and you fall to the Planetary Interior; on arrival a second breach opens in the floor beside you, and stepping into that one brings you back up. It cannot be broken or moved.

pages.title: Moduli Crawler
pages.text: $(thing)Moduli Crawler$(). Lives in: Moduli Wastes, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Moduli Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.

pages.title: Moduli Crystal
pages.text: The extra dimensions of string theory have shapes and sizes set by fields called moduli. This crystal is those parameters frozen solid: a record of exactly how the hidden dimensions are curled. It changes shape slightly depending on the angle you view it from.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Moduli Ore in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes); dropped by the Moduli Crawler (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes)).

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Moduli Crawlers in the Moduli Wastes of the Bulk dropped these, and more lay inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Measuring their facets, I found they recorded the shape and size of the compact dimensions.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Moduli Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Moduli Crawler.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, G₂ Manifold.

pages.title: Moduli Ore
pages.text: Each crystal here is a snapshot of one possible shape for the hidden dimensions. Moduli are the dials that describe the size and shape of compactified space, and this ore holds those dials fixed in mineral form. Different veins, different geometries, all perfectly valid.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)String theory admits an enormous landscape of vacua, each set by its moduli. Mining the bulk, I noticed no two lumps of this ore refract light the same way. Each one has settled into a different vacuum.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Neutronium Plating
pages.text: Neutronium rolled into flat plates and riveted onto a block face. It is grey, dense and almost reflective, with seams that look as though they were drawn with a ruler. It gives a lab the look of a reactor vault.
Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Block of Neutronium, Neutronium Plating Slab, Neutronium Plating Stairs, Neutronium Plating Wall.

pages.title: Oklo Rock
pages.text: Host rock of the Natural Reactor, modelled on Oklo in Gabon, where two billion years ago groundwater slowed neutrons enough for uranium ore to run as a fission reactor for hundreds of thousands of years. It is still slightly radioactive.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor), Oklo Reactor Ruin structures in the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor).

pages.title: Oklo Uraninite Ore
pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 36 and 126. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Ordinal Ore
pages.text: Ore whose crystals arrive in sequence: each one has a definite successor, and even infinite chains of them have a limit crystal waiting beyond. Breaking a lump never disturbs the order of what remains.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the ordinal stone I found a vein where crystals grew in strict succession, with a larger one capping every infinite run. Von Neumann's construction of the ordinals, rendered in mineral.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Pitchblende Ore
pages.text: Found in the Overworld, between Y 0 and 48. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Overworld (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Pulsar Wisp
pages.text: A spinning wisp that flashes on a perfect beat, like the lighthouse beam of a pulsar. Millisecond pulsars keep time nearly as well as atomic clocks.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Pulsar Timing Crystal, Cosmic Ray Shard.

pages.title: Retrocausal Ore
pages.text: Ore that knows when it is going to be mined. The vein grows brighter before my pick arrives, and splinters along lines that only make sense once the strike has happened. Holding it feels like being remembered.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)White holes run time backwards. Mining the ejecta rock, I noticed this ore cracking a moment before I struck it. The effect preceded the cause, and the cause still happened.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the white hole interior (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Rich Copper Ore
pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 50 and 126. Gives Rich Copper Chunk when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Rich Gold Ore
pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 12 and 96. Gives Rich Gold Chunk when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Rich Iron Ore
pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 50 and 126. Gives Rich Iron Chunk when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Ringwoodite Ore
pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 4 and 84. Gives Ringwoodite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Spacetime Panel
pages.text: A panel of spacetime alloy whose surface seems to bend inward slightly, as if the wall behind it were further away than it is. It is cool, smooth and very faintly disorienting to look at for long. Its edges line up neatly in rows.
Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Block of Spacetime Alloy.

pages.title: Tidal Ore
pages.text: A seam of metal pulled thin by gravity gradients. One end of every grain feels a stronger pull than the other, and the ore is threaded with stretch marks. It flexes slightly in the hand, as if still being tugged.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Tidal forces are the difference in gravity across an object. Deep in infall rock I found metal that had been stretched rather than crushed, and recognised the signature of a nearby singularity.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the black hole interior (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Tidal Stretcher
pages.text: A creature of the tide near a compact mass, where feet are pulled harder than head. It draws everything near it out long and thin, like spaghetti.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Tidal Shear Crystal, Accretion Disk Fragment.

pages.title: Ephemeral Graviton Ore
pages.text: A vein where gravity itself fizzes. The quanta of the gravitational field appear and vanish here so densely that the ore feels slightly heavier one moment and lighter the next. Nearby dust drifts in slow, uneven arcs.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)No detector has ever caught a single graviton. Picking through foam substrate, I found a seam where my plumb line twitched in rhythm with bursts of vacuum noise. Borrowed gravitons, pinned in stone.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Ephemeral Monopole Ore
pages.text: A vein that points only one way. Each fleck carries a lone magnetic pole, north without south or the reverse, which classical electromagnetism forbids. A compass held close swings and holds, refusing to recover.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dirac showed one monopole anywhere would explain why charge is quantised. In foam substrate my compass locked onto a single seam and would not let go: monopole pairs, flickering up from the vacuum.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Ephemeral Photon Ore
pages.text: Glints of light that do not come from anywhere. Virtual photons, the messengers that carry the electromagnetic force, wink in and out of this vein, so the ore glows without a source. It is cool to the touch despite the sparkle.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Every electric force is an exchange of virtual photons. Working in foam substrate I saw a seam lit from within, though nothing nearby could be lighting it. The vacuum was lending light and briefly forgetting to take it back.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Ephemeral Quark Ore
pages.text: Quarks borrowed from the vacuum and caught before they could be returned. They glow in shifting red, green and blue, colour charge that never settles, and the vein flickers as pairs pop into being and vanish. Leave it alone and it seems to breathe.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In foam substrate I saw sparks that lasted only an instant, virtual quark pairs living on borrowed energy. One seam held them a little longer than the uncertainty principle should allow, long enough to mine.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Void Lattice Bricks
pages.text: Void lattice cut into bricks - rigid blocks of nothing stacked with careful joints. The wall looks like a pattern of very clean holes in the world. Each brick has crisp, flawless edges, and the joints between them are the only part that looks like ordinary matter. Torchlight seems to fall into them.
Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Void Lattice Block, Void Lattice Bricks Slab, Void Lattice Bricks Stairs, Void Lattice Bricks Wall.

pages.title: Void Lattice Ore
pages.text: Bulk stone holding pockets of a crystal made of nothing - a lattice of empty sites that remains rigid even though there is nothing in them. It looks like a gap in the rock that has decided to be solid.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mining in the Bulk, I hit a patch of rock that the pick went through as though it were air but that still dropped something. The lattice was a crystal of vacancies, ordered without anything to order.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).
Survey notes. $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() grows deep in the deepslate layer. $(item)Degenerate Matter$() is found in End stone; smelt or blast it into $(item)Neutronium$().

$(item)Void Lattice$() only forms in the Bulk.$(br2)Names explained: Cherenkov light is the blue glow of particles outrunning light in a medium. Degenerate matter is what remains when atoms are crushed until only quantum exclusion holds them up, as in white dwarfs and neutron stars.
Glows with the blue light of particles outrunning light in a medium.$(br2)Made in $(item)Galton Board$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Deepslate Cherenkov Quartz Ore in the Overworld.
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(): Atomic Clock, Block of Cherenkov Quartz, Casimir Plate, Casimir Vacuum Press, Chemical Reactor and more

Out past the edge of the sky, round a black hole feeding on a disk of its own fire, islands of rock and ice drift in the dark. The $(thing)Accretion Frontier$() is reached with a $(item)Light Sail$() (research $(thing)Galactic Dynamics$()): climb to y 200 or higher, stand under open sky, and unfurl it. Unfurled again in the Frontier, it brings you home and slows your fall.

It has five regions. The $(thing)Molecular Cloud Nebula$(), cold ice and dust where stars are born: you cannot see far. The $(thing)Asteroid Belt$(), where you weigh almost nothing - and $(thing)micrometeorites$() strike anyone not wearing a $(item)Whipple Shield$() (a quarter stopped per piece; a full set stops all).

The $(thing)Pulsar Field$(): crust of neutron-star iron, and a pulse of radiation every five seconds, on the beat, for anyone under open sky. Gravity is high and time runs slow (Time Dilation). The $(thing)Accretion Rim$(): slag lakes of disk plasma; it is hot enough to burn, and the disk's tidal pull stretches you. The $(thing)Lensing Void$(): black glass, sight lines bent, and frame-dragging currents that push you sideways.

Its ores: $(item)Interstellar Dust$() in the nebula's ice, $(item)Exoplanet Core Samples$() and $(item)Brown Dwarf Cores$() in the asteroids, $(item)Magnetar Crust$(), $(item)Pulsar Timing Crystals$() and $(item)Cosmic Ray Shards$() in the pulsar crust, $(item)Accretion Disk Fragments$() in the slag, and $(item)Einstein Ring Lenses$() in the void glass. Derelict Stations drift between the islands; Pulsar Beacons stand on the field.

Each of the Frontier's creatures acts out its physics. The $(thing)Nebuloid$() is a drifting knot of gas and dust; inside it you are blind. The $(thing)Pulsar Wisp$() pulses on an exact beat, once every one and a half seconds, and its pulse hurts and irradiates anyone it can see within ten blocks - dodge behind something between pulses.

The $(thing)Tidal Stretcher$() pulls you in harder the closer you are (a tidal force grows as 1/r³) and stretches what it grabs. The $(thing)Lens Phantom$() is never where it appears: its light reaches you bent round the void's mass, so its image stands a block or two from its body. Aim beside it.

The $(thing)Hawking Imp$() is a tiny black hole. It evaporates, and the smaller it gets the hotter and faster it burns (T ∝ 1/M) - until it pops. The $(thing)Boltzmann Brain$() fluctuates out of nothing, mutters, and is gone within half a minute unless caught.

$(thing)The Binary$(): play a Binary Black Hole Merger record - or a Gravitational Wave Echo - in the Frontier and two compact stars spiral out of the dark. Their gravitational waves carry off their orbit: they close in (da/dt ∝ −1/a³) and circle ever faster. Kill both before they meet - if they merge, the shockwave hits everything nearby, and nothing is left to loot.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Accretion Disk Fragment when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Accretion Rim's slag.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Accretion Disk Fragments.

$(item)Asteroid Rock$(). The rubble of planetesimals that never became planets. Its chondrules are frozen droplets from the Solar System's first few million years.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Asteroid Belt).
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The Spectrograph sorts four into two Meteoric Iron and a Chondrite Fragment.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Brown Dwarf Core when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt's rock.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Brown Dwarf Cores (also made in the Tectonic Press, from dust and cloud gas).
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Cosmic Ray Shard when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Cosmic Ray Shards (also made by the Interstellar Scoop, from glass left high up).
$(item)Dust Cloud$(). A cloud of dust grains, too thin to stand on. Now and then, broken, it leaves Interstellar Dust.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Breaks into Interstellar Dust, sometimes.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Interstellar Dust when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Nebula's ice.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Interstellar Dust.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Einstein Ring Lens when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Lensing Void's glass.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Einstein Ring Lenses.

$(item)Frontier Regolith$(). Rock ground to dust by billions of years of micrometeorites. Assayed in bulk it gives back its interstellar dust and a little rare earth.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The top of every island of the Accretion Frontier (except the Lensing Void).$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The Spectrograph assays eight into four Interstellar Dust and a Rare Earth Oxide.
$(item)Hydrogen Cloud$(). Ionised hydrogen glowing red at 656 nm, the H-alpha line. You can walk straight through it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Light: it glows. Its gases will be gathered in a later expansion.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Magnetar Crust Fragment when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Magnetar Crust Fragments.

$(item)Nebular Ice$(). Water, carbon monoxide and ammonia frozen together on dust grains at about fifteen kelvin. Starlight slowly builds larger molecules within it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Molecular Cloud Nebula).
$(thing)Found$(): Patches in the Molecular Cloud Nebula, among its clouds.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Two sublimate into 250 mB of Molecular Cloud in the Electrolytic Cell.
$(item)Oxygen Cloud$(). Doubly ionised oxygen glowing green-blue at 501 nm. You can walk straight through it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Light: it glows. Its gases will be gathered in a later expansion.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Exoplanet Core Sample when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt's rock.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Exoplanet Core Samples (also made in the Hypervelocity Impact Forge).
$(item)Protostar Fragment$(). Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Protostellar Ember when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): Inside the Nebula's ice.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives a Protostellar Ember: thermoelectric fuel that burns for a long time, or feed for the Accretion Disk Reactor.

$(item)Pulsar Crust$(). Iron from a neutron star's crust: a lattice of nuclei in a sea of electrons, held under a field of some hundred million tesla.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field).
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Two with two Iron-Nickel become a Magnetar Crust Fragment in the Pulsed Magnet Lab, at 80 T.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Pulsar Timing Crystal when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Pulsar Timing Crystals.

$(item)Rim Slag$(). Cinder flung from the inner edge of an accretion disk, where gas spirals in at a fair fraction of light speed and is heated to millions of degrees.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Accretion Rim).
$(thing)Found$(): The Accretion Rim, round its plasma lakes.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Quenched with Accretion Disk Plasma in the Tectonic Press: Accretion Disk Fragments.
$(item)Station Hull$(). Aluminium skin and stringers from a spacecraft, thin enough to dent by hand. In vacuum, a few millimetres of it is all that separates air from nothing.
$(thing)Found$(): Derelict Stations drifting in the Frontier; or crafted from iron.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The body of the Whipple Shield and the Frontier Suit.

$(item)Void Glass$(). Glass as dark as the space it came from. Gravity bends light as a lens does, and a well-aligned mass draws a background source into a full Einstein ring.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Lensing Void).
$(thing)Found$(): The Lensing Void.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Four with Fused Silica make an Einstein Ring Lens in the Optical Workshop.
Every region of the Accretion Frontier has its hazard, and each has an answer.

$(li)$(thing)Nebula$() - blinding dust: the $(item)Adaptive Optics Visor$().$(li)$(thing)Asteroid Belt$() - micrometeorites: the $(item)Whipple Shield$() (a quarter per piece); low gravity: $(item)Gravity Compensators$().$(li)$(thing)Pulsar Field$() - its radiation pulse: $(item)Radiation Plating$() on your armour; high gravity: Gravity Compensators; Time Dilation: an $(item)Atomic Clock$() in the off hand.

$(li)$(thing)Accretion Rim$() - heat: the $(item)Thermal Shroud$() (or a full Refractory Suit); its tidal pull: the $(item)Tidal Brace$() (or a Precision Gyroscope in the off hand).$(li)$(thing)Lensing Void$() - frame dragging: a $(item)Precision Gyroscope$() in the off hand; warped sight: the Adaptive Optics Visor.

The four pieces of the $(item)Frontier Suit$() are made of Station Hull, each round a piece of the region it answers: an Einstein Ring Lens, an Accretion Disk Fragment, a Tidal Shear Crystal and a Planetary Core Sample (the reference mass the boots weigh gravity against).

Found a crashed research observatory, its containment dome cracked, a supply cache still inside. They dot the Overworld. Who built them, I don't yet know.$(br2)A good source of early Cherenkov Quartz and Neutronium - worth a detour before I can make either myself.

A cache the Transcendental keeps for itself - and the one you can build: 243 kinds of item, and up to $(thing)2,147,483,647$() of each. Whatever you put in joins the pile of the same item. Scroll to move through its 27 rows; a click or shift-click takes one normal stack at a time.
Pipes put into it and take out of it (one stack at a time). Broken, it keeps everything inside. It is made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

block:abiogenesis_crucible#lore.text: A crucible of primordial soup under lightning and ultraviolet light, held where chemistry tips over into life.

block:absolute_frame_casing#lore.text: A frame that keeps its shape whatever the laws around it do: the one fixed reference in a place where every other measure has come loose.

block:absolute_pedestal#lore.text: A pedestal of the highest grade, made to hold an offering at the very centre of a ritual. Nothing set on it is ever quite where it was before.

block:acceleration_cavity#lore.text: A copper RF cavity ringing at its resonant frequency. Its field points forward each time a bunch arrives, so particles gain energy on every pass.

block:accretion_casing#lore.text: Casing built to sit beside an accretion disk, where infalling gas heats to millions of degrees and shines in X-rays before it crosses the horizon.

block:accretion_disk_plasma#lore.text: Accretion Disk Plasma, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:accretion_disk_reactor#lore.text: Feeds matter onto a captive black hole: falling in, it gives up to a third of its rest energy as light. Too much at once, and its own light blows the disk away.

block:accretion_fragment_ore#lore.text: Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Accretion Disk Fragment when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:aerosol_sprayer#lore.text: Breaks liquid into droplets fine enough to hang in the air for days. The same kind of haze turns Titan orange and hides its surface from view.

block:aleph_glass#lore.text: Glass whose clarity has a cardinality. It holds countably many points of light in a perfectly ordered grid, yet every sliver of it still contains as many points as the whole.

block:alt_az_mount#lore.text: A mount that turns a dish on two simple axes, altitude and azimuth, while a computer works out how to follow the sky. Nearly every large modern telescope sits on one.

block:analog_black_hole#lore.text: A condensate flowing faster than its own speed of sound: a horizon that sound cannot cross back over - and, at it, Hawking radiation of phonons.

block:analytic_continuator#lore.text: Calculus in a box: limits, derivatives, integrals, series and the analytic continuation of functions into the complex plane.

block:annihilation_reactor#lore.text: Converts mass entirely into energy, E = mc^2, regulated by dilithium crystals.

block:anomaly_containment_ward#lore.text: A quarantine cell of chronoplastic walls, causal shielding and windows of containment glass, with dimensional stabilisers at every corner. It lets what it holds grow - just slower than its field can clear it.

block:anomaly_resolution_engine#lore.text: A tower of reality-lattice casing around a column of lensed, error-corrected fields. It doses an anomaly fraction by fraction until not one of its cells is left, and writes what it learned back into the laws.

block:answer_pedestal#lore.text: A plinth that waits for a conclusion. When the right answer is placed on it, the surrounding proof settles into consistency and the room grows quiet. A wrong answer sits there and does nothing at all.

block:anticarbon_ore#lore.text: Found in the Antiverse, between Y -60 and 20. Gives Anticarbon Crystal when mined with diamond pickaxe or better.

block:antigold_ore#lore.text: Found in the Antiverse, between Y -48 and 60. Gives Raw Anti-Gold when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:antihydrogen_ice#lore.text: Found in the Antiverse, between Y 20 and 160. Gives Antihydrogen Crystal when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:antiiron_ore#lore.text: Found in the Antiverse, between Y -48 and 120. Gives Raw Anti-Iron when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:antimatter_penning_trap#lore.text: Pair-produces antimatter from gamma photons and holds it in a magnetic bottle.

block:antiproton_decelerator#lore.text: A ring that catches antiprotons from collisions at nearly light speed and brakes them, lap after lap, until they can be trapped.

block:antisilicon_ore#lore.text: Found in the Antiverse, between Y -20 and 100. Gives Antisilicon Shard when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:antisoil#lore.text: Soil of the Antiverse, made of antiprotons, antineutrons and positrons.

block:antistone#lore.text: Stone made of antimatter, the mirror image of ordinary rock. It looks exactly the same; only meeting matter would tell the difference, and then not for long.

block:antistone_bricks#lore.text: Antistone dressed into bricks. Among antimatter it is as sound as any masonry; a single ordinary atom touching it would annihilate with it.

block:antiverse_cache#lore.text: A locker for matter of the wrong sign. It holds its contents by fields alone, since a single touch of the walls would annihilate both.

block:antiwater#lore.text: Antiwater, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:aquifer_pump#lore.text: Draws water from the rock it stands on - and, in the Planetary Interior, brine and hotter things.

block:arbor_heartwood#lore.text: The innermost wood of the Arbor, dense and pale, with rings that record not years but the branching of possibilities. Run a finger along the grain and it follows a different branch each time.

block:arbor_planks#lore.text: Planks cut from the Arbor, pale and fine-grained, with faint branching lines running along their length. The wood smells of rain and seems to grow warmer when people walk across it.

block:arbor_planks_slab#lore.text: A slab of Arbor Planks, for building with.

block:arbor_planks_stairs#lore.text: Stairs of Arbor Planks, for building with.

block:armature_breech#lore.text: The loading end of a railgun, where the conducting armature sits across the rails. A megaamp pulse closes the circuit and the Lorentz force flings it down the bore.

block:asteroid_rock#lore.text: The rubble of planetesimals that never became planets. Its chondrules are frozen droplets from the Solar System's first few million years.

block:atomic_clock#lore.text: Counts the oscillations of a caesium atom. The deeper it stands in a gravity well, the slower it ticks.

block:autocatalytic_broth#lore.text: Autocatalytic Broth, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:autonomous_extreme_assembler#lore.text: An Extreme Assembly Table that crafts on its own: give it a pattern, feed it, power it.

block:axiom_distiller#lore.text: Boils reality down past its source code to the axioms underneath, and condenses them into fragments.

block:axiom_lamp#lore.text: A lamp that shines when its axiom is in force. Its light is steady and colourless, and when the axiom is withdrawn it simply goes dark. Rows of them read like a truth table drawn in light.

block:axiom_stone#lore.text: Pale, smooth stone that seems to be made of definitions. Each block holds its shape because it has been told to. It is cool and faintly humming, like a theorem being proved.

block:axiom_toggle#lore.text: A switch that adopts or rejects an axiom. Flip it and the local truths rearrange; some things become provable, others not.

block:axiomatic_breach_engine#lore.text: Breaks every law of physics and mathematics at once. While it runs, step into its heart to fall out of reality.

block:axiomatic_field_emitter#lore.text: A field emitter that projects not forces but rules - a small region where a chosen axiom holds or does not.

block:basalt_column#lore.text: Lava that cooled slowly and shrank as it set, cracking into columns, most often six-sided, as at the Giant's Causeway.

block:basaltic_magma#lore.text: Basaltic Magma, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:bayesian_analyzer#lore.text: Weighs a prior against a piece of evidence and writes down the updated belief.

block:bec_trap#lore.text: A magnetic bottle for atoms cooled to billionths of a degree, where thousands of them fall into one quantum state and move as a single wave.

block:bending_magnet#lore.text: A dipole magnet that curves a beam of charged particles along an arc. The faster the beam or the tighter the turn, the stronger the field it needs.

block:bioreactor#lore.text: A sterile, stirred, temperature-held vat where cells grow and do the chemistry for you.

block:bitter_plate_stack#lore.text: Perforated copper discs stacked in a helix, as Francis Bitter designed in the 1930s. Water rushes through the holes to carry off the heat of tens of kiloamps.

block:bose_einstein_condensate#lore.text: Bose-Einstein Condensate, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:bose_einstein_condenser#lore.text: Cools atoms to nanokelvin until they share a single quantum state.

block:breached_anomaly_engine#lore.text: Ruins of a machine that pulled creatures out of nothing. Built anew at the Convergence Altar, it grows any creature whose genome it is shown.

block:bridgmanite_ore#lore.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 4 and 70. Gives Bridgmanite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:brown_dwarf_ore#lore.text: Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Brown Dwarf Core when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:brownian_microscope#lore.text: A microscope over a drop of water with clay in it. The grains never stop jittering - molecules strike them from every side - and how far they wander weighs the molecules.

block:brownian_suspension#lore.text: Brownian Suspension, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:bubble_pedestal#lore.text: The cradle on which a warp bubble is shaped. In Alcubierre's metric space contracts ahead and expands behind, while the bubble's own interior stays flat and calm.

block:bubble_universe#lore.text: A sphere of an entirely separate universe, nucleated out of the inflating vacuum and sealed off from ours. Inside it, the constants are slightly different.

block:bulk_cache#lore.text: Bigger on the inside: it borrows a little room from a fifth dimension. In brane cosmology our whole universe floats in such a bulk.

block:bulk_crystal#lore.text: A translucent crystal from the Bulk whose facets seem to point in directions I cannot quite name.

block:bulk_stone#lore.text: The bedrock of the higher-dimensional Bulk: a grey stone that seems to have more surfaces than it shows. Edges blur where the extra dimensions curl back in.

block:burst_casing#lore.text: The shell of an observatory that waits for bursts lasting milliseconds that never repeat. It is built to sit very still for a very long time.

block:burst_observatory#lore.text: Twelve scintillators facing every way at once, waiting for the brightest explosions in the Universe.

block:calorimeter_detector_array#lore.text: An array of scintillator crystals and pixel trackers that records where a particle went and how much energy it carried. A quantum processor reads the flashes. The crystals glow faintly when hit.

block:cantor_diagonalizer#lore.text: Lists every number, then builds one that is on no list. Manufactures infinities - and then bigger ones.

block:capacitor_bank#lore.text: Rows of capacitors charged slowly and emptied all at once: energy gathered over seconds, released in microseconds as a single heavy pulse.

block:carborane_superacid#lore.text: Carborane Superacid, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:cardinal_ore#lore.text: Found in the Transfinite Hierarchy, between Y 0 and 256. Gives Cardinal Shard when mined with diamond pickaxe or better.

block:cascade_casing#lore.text: Shielded housing for a centrifuge cascade. Each stage enriches uranium only slightly, so stages are piped in series by the dozen and machines run by the thousand.

block:casimir_energy_cell#lore.text: An energy store built around the force between two plates in a vacuum.

block:casimir_press#lore.text: Presses matter between plates so close the vacuum itself pushes back.

block:causal_shielding_plate#lore.text: A plate of chronosteel and causal shield lattice that keeps cause and effect in the right order on either side. It feels slightly ahead of the moment, as though it knew I was going to touch it.

block:causal_solder#lore.text: Causal Solder, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:causality_loop_engine#lore.text: Sends objects back along a closed timelike curve so they exist twice. The universe is not amused.

block:central_solenoid#lore.text: The tall coil at a tokamak's core. Ramping its current induces the plasma current, so the plasma itself is the secondary winding of a giant transformer.

block:centrifuge_rotor#lore.text: A thin-walled cylinder spun so fast its rim outruns sound. Heavier molecules crowd towards the wall and lighter ones drift to the axis.

block:chamber_casing#lore.text: The shell of a chamber where time runs at another rate. Even on Earth, a clock a kilometre higher gains about one part in 10¹³.

block:chance_tiles#lore.text: Tiles laid in no repeating order, each pattern drawn at random. Any stretch that looks designed is a coincidence the dice were always going to throw.

block:chemical_reactor#lore.text: A pressure vessel with a catalyst bed, a heater and a stirrer. Most of chemistry is getting the right molecules to meet at the right energy.

block:cherenkov_bricks#lore.text: Cherenkov quartz cut into small bricks, each one glowing softly blue along its edges. A wall of them looks like a shallow pool at night. They are smooth and slightly cool to the touch.

block:cherenkov_bricks_slab#lore.text: A slab of Cherenkov Bricks, for building with.

block:cherenkov_bricks_stairs#lore.text: Stairs of Cherenkov Bricks, for building with.

block:cherenkov_bricks_wall#lore.text: A wall of Cherenkov Bricks, for building with.

block:cherenkov_lamp#lore.text: A lamp of Cherenkov quartz with glowstone at its heart, so the blue Cherenkov glow is amplified into a strong, clean light. It is the colour of a reactor pool, and as calming.

block:cherenkov_pillar#lore.text: A column of Cherenkov quartz that glows along its length with an even blue. Placed at a doorway it reads like a beam of light holding up the lintel. It is cool and faintly humming.

block:cherenkov_quartz_block#lore.text: Forty pieces of Cherenkov quartz fused into a single block that glows the soft blue of particles outrunning light in a medium.

block:chondrite#lore.text: A stony meteorite: rock that has not melted since the planets formed. Found in craters out in open country. Gives Chondrite Fragment when mined. Needs a stone pickaxe or better.

block:chronal_accelerator#lore.text: Time runs faster for everything in its field, and the universe sends the bill. Each borrowed tick must be paid for, in energy and in Chronon Gas.

block:chronal_field_projector#lore.text: A projector that stretches time in its field. A temporal knot sits in the emitter stack, so clocks inside run faster or slower depending on its setting.

block:chrono_loom#lore.text: Weaves worldlines. Reverses the arrow of time, ties temporal knots and enforces self-consistency on time loops.

block:chronon_field_inverter#lore.text: Inverts the local arrow of time to harvest chronons.

block:chronoplastic_casing#lore.text: A casing laced with tachyon crystal and a chronon capacitor, so that time inside flows at a rate I can adjust.

block:chronosteel_block#lore.text: Forty chronosteel ingots fused into one block around an empty set: a metal whose atoms keep slightly different time from their surroundings.

block:chronosteel_coil_block#lore.text: A superconducting coil wrapped in chronosteel, so that current inside it runs on its own clock. The field it makes is steadier than any ordinary coil, as though the coil had more time to think.

block:chronosteel_hazard_panel#lore.text: A chronosteel panel painted with warning stripes, used to mark doorways, machine edges and anything I do not want to walk into. The stripes look very slightly out of step with each other.

block:chronosteel_pillar#lore.text: A column of chronosteel, banded and fluted, that carries a load without complaint. It reflects light in a slightly delayed blur and gives a doorway the feel of an engine room.

block:chronosteel_plating#lore.text: Chronosteel rolled into plates and fixed to a block face. Its sheen is cool and slightly blurred, as if the surface had moved a moment before it was seen. It gives a wall a clean, mechanical look.

block:chronosteel_plating_slab#lore.text: A slab of Chronosteel Plating, for building with.

block:chronosteel_plating_stairs#lore.text: Stairs of Chronosteel Plating, for building with.

block:chronosteel_vent#lore.text: A chronosteel grille that lets air pass between rooms. The slats are angled to keep light out and air moving, and a faint draught always seems to be flowing through it, even when the room is still.

block:climate_casing#lore.text: Casing for a climate engine. Earth's climate balances about 340 W/m² of incoming sunlight against heat radiated back to space.

block:climate_engine#lore.text: Changes the air's carbon dioxide and aerosols, and with them how much heat the world keeps: enough to bring rain, clear the sky, or grow ice.

block:cloaking_glass#lore.text: A pane of metamaterial that bends light around itself, so the glass is nearly invisible from any angle. Only the edges betray it, as a faint distortion in the room.

block:cloud_seeder_stack#lore.text: A stack that releases ice nuclei into supercooled cloud. Silver iodide, the usual agent, has a lattice so like ice that droplets freeze onto it and fall.

block:colloid_cell#lore.text: A thin glass cell of fine grains in water. Unseen molecules jostle them endlessly; in 1908 Perrin watched that jitter and counted the atoms in a mole.

block:compactification_lathe#lore.text: Rolls extra dimensions up small: Kaluza-Klein circles, Calabi-Yau and G₂ spaces, D-branes and finally M-theory itself.

block:computronium_block#lore.text: A block of matter arranged so that every atom is part of a computation. It is warm to the touch and very slightly noisy, as though it is always working.

block:computronium_lamp#lore.text: A computronium block lit from within by glowstone, its traces brightened into a steady, warm glow. It looks like a terminal screen turned into a lamp.

block:computronium_panel#lore.text: A panel of computronium with fine glowing traces running across its face, like a circuit board that is thinking. It is warm and faintly busy to the touch.

block:computronium_tiles#lore.text: Computronium cut into tiles, each one lit by faint, shifting traces. A floor of them flickers softly, as if computing something about whoever walks across it.

block:computronium_tiles_slab#lore.text: A slab of Computronium Tiles, for building with.

block:computronium_tiles_stairs#lore.text: Stairs of Computronium Tiles, for building with.

block:concentrator_mirror#lore.text: A great curved array of mirrors that gathers light from a field of heliostats onto one focus. The Odeillo furnace reaches about 3,500 °C this way.

block:concept_compressor#lore.text: Takes whole stacks of everything a field of science has produced and compresses them into a single singularity of pure concept.

block:conceptual_casing#lore.text: Housing for things that are not physical. Its plates are woven from transfinite structure and braced with formal proofs, so that what it contains is held by consistency rather than by strength.

block:containment_field_glass#lore.text: Glass that is not really glass, but a field held between two panes with a shimmer of plasma in between.

block:control_rod_drive#lore.text: The mechanism that raises and lowers a reactor's boron rods. If power fails it simply lets go, and gravity drops the rods into the core.

block:convergence_altar#lore.text: A focus for the pedestals around it, which give up what they hold to a single point, as rays meet at the focus of a lens.

block:convergence_engine#lore.text: Does in a box what the Convergence Altar does with pedestals and patience: every ritual but the Breached Anomaly Engine, fed by pipes like any machine.

block:core_iron#lore.text: The alloy of planetary cores and iron meteorites, roughly nine parts iron to one of nickel. Etched, it shows Widmanstätten patterns grown over millions of years.

block:core_magnetite_ore#lore.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 1 and 48. Gives Magnetite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:corundum_crystal#lore.text: Aluminium oxide crystallised in bulk, second only to diamond among common minerals for hardness. A trace of chromium makes it ruby; others, sapphire.

block:cosmic_neutronium_block#lore.text: Forty ingots of cosmic neutronium fused into a block denser than the inside of a neutron star. It casts a faint, cold shadow even in full light.

block:cosmic_neutronium_coil_block#lore.text: A coil of cosmic neutronium over spacetime alloy, cooled cryogenically and threaded with pentaquark shards. It runs hotter than anything below it and seems to pull faintly on the room.

block:cosmic_plating#lore.text: Cosmic neutronium rolled into plating, dark as space with faint pinpricks of light. A wall of it looks like a window onto the night sky that happens to be load-bearing.

block:cosmic_ray_ore#lore.text: Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Cosmic Ray Shard when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:cosmic_tiles#lore.text: Cosmic neutronium cut into dark tiles that seem to have tiny points of light deep inside them, like stars seen through a deep well. The floor they make feels impossibly solid.

block:cosmic_tiles_slab#lore.text: A slab of Cosmic Neutronium Tiles, for building with.

block:cosmic_tiles_stairs#lore.text: Stairs of Cosmic Neutronium Tiles, for building with.

block:cosmogenic_casing#lore.text: A casing built to contain the birth of a universe: spin foam lattice and multiverse shards folded around a rift frame casing.

block:crustal_rock#lore.text: Silicate rock of a planet's crust, the thin cool skin over the mantle: on Earth about 7 km thick beneath the oceans and 35 km under the continents.

block:cryogenic_cooling_jacket#lore.text: A jacket of containment field glass around a cryocooler, built to keep superconducting parts close to absolute zero. Frost forms on its outer face within seconds.

block:crystal_growth_furnace#lore.text: A seed is dipped into the melt and drawn slowly up, turning: the melt freezes onto it as one single crystal, and the impurities stay behind.

block:crystal_interferometer_mount#lore.text: A rigid, damped cradle for an interferometer cut from one perfect silicon crystal. A neutron splits inside it, and a shake of an atom's width spoils the fringes.

block:cyclotron#lore.text: Protons spiralling outward between two copper dees, kicked across the gap twice a turn by a radio-frequency voltage that must keep exact step with them.

block:cyclotron_dee#lore.text: One of a cyclotron's two hollow D-shaped electrodes. The RF voltage across the gap between them kicks each particle every half turn, so it spirals outward ever faster.

block:cyclotron_yoke#lore.text: The iron return path of a cyclotron magnet. It carries the flux back from pole to pole, so the field across the gap stays strong and even.

block:dark_energy_siphon#lore.text: Taps the energy of empty space that drives the expansion of the universe.

block:dark_matter_collector#lore.text: Gravitationally focuses the invisible halo surrounding every galaxy.

block:decay_chamber#lore.text: A sealed, shielded vessel where short-lived isotopes live out their half-lives. Radon in its tanks decays on a real clock - a day in a minute - into lead.

block:decontamination_scrubber#lore.text: Melts radioactive waste into glass, and takes the uranium back out of spent fuel.

block:decorative_telescope#lore.text: A small reflecting telescope on its stand, still pointed at whatever its last observer wanted to see.

block:deep_brine#lore.text: Deep Brine, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:deep_drilling_rig#lore.text: A derrick and a string of drill pipe kilometres long. The deeper the bit, the hotter the rock, the higher the pressure in it - and the older and stranger the core it brings up.

block:deepslate_cherenkov_quartz_ore#lor.text: Found in the Overworld, between Y -64 and 0. Gives Cherenkov Quartz when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:deepslate_pitchblende_ore#lore.text: Found in the Overworld, between Y -64 and 0. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:degenerate_matter_ore#lore.text: Found in the End, between Y 10 and 80. Gives Degenerate Matter Chunk when mined with diamond pickaxe or better.

block:dense_mass_core#lore.text: A mass packed so tightly that time itself runs slow around it. Clocks set nearby lose seconds to the rest of the world, and never get them back.

block:derrick_frame#lore.text: The tall frame over a well that carries the crown block and the whole string of pipe. The word comes from Derrick, a seventeenth-century Tyburn hangman.

block:dilaton_ore#lore.text: Found in the Bulk, between Y 0 and 160. Gives Dilaton Crystal when mined with diamond pickaxe or better.

block:dilithium_block#lore.text: Dilithium crystals fused into one solid block that rings when struck and glows a soft violet. The resonance carries through the floor, and anything metal nearby picks up a faint hum.

block:dilithium_lamp#lore.text: A dilithium block with glowstone at its centre, so the violet crystal shines with a soft, even light. It hums a single note when lit.

block:dilithium_ore#lore.text: Found in the Nether, between Y 10 and 110. Gives Dilithium Crystal when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:dimensional_lift_projector#lore.text: A lift that pushes along an extra dimension. With a tesseract core set inside the emitter stack, it can nudge anything in its field slightly outside ordinary space, where weight no longer applies.

block:dimensional_residue#lore.text: Dimensional Residue, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:dimensional_stabiliser#lore.text: A stabiliser that holds the number of dimensions in a region fixed while machines nearby try to change it. A dimensional stabiliser matrix sets the count, and a field emitter enforces it.

block:dipole_bending_magnet#lore.text: A superconducting dipole magnet on a neutronium frame that bends a charged particle beam into a circle. Its field is perfectly uniform across the gap. Metal tools drift toward it.

block:dish_truss#lore.text: The steel frame behind a radio dish. It must hold the surface true to a fraction of a wavelength while the whole dish tilts and sags under its own weight.

block:disk_confinement_ring#lore.text: A ring of magnets that shapes the field around an accretion disk. In real disks, tangled fields drive the turbulence that lets gas shed its spin and fall inward.

block:display_black_hole#lore.text: A real one, very small, held on a pedestal. It bends the light behind it.

block:display_dyson_sphere#lore.text: A star wrapped in a swarm of collectors.

block:display_galaxy#lore.text: Two hundred billion stars, more or less, in two spiral arms.

block:display_penteract#lore.text: The shadow of a five-dimensional cube. It has 32 corners and 80 edges.

block:display_pocket_universe#lore.text: A whole universe, still expanding, in a jar.

block:display_pulsar#lore.text: A neutron star spinning hundreds of times a second, sweeping its beams across the room.

block:display_quasar#lore.text: A feeding black hole outshining its host galaxy.

block:display_tesseract#lore.text: A four-dimensional cube turning through itself.

block:display_white_hole#lore.text: Nothing can enter it. Light pours out forever.

block:display_wormhole#lore.text: The other mouth is somewhere else. Do not put your hand in.

block:doppler_drive#lore.text: Moves a gamma source at speeds of a fraction of a micrometre per second, so its Doppler shift can cancel the tiny shift that gravity puts on its light.

block:drill_string#lore.text: Lengths of steel pipe screwed end to end that turn the bit and carry mud down to it. Kilometres of it wind up like a spring before the bit begins to turn.

block:dust_cloud#lore.text: A cloud of dust grains, too thin to stand on. Now and then, broken, it leaves Interstellar Dust.

block:dust_ice_ore#lore.text: Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Interstellar Dust when mined with stone pickaxe or better.

block:dyson_array#lore.text: Surrounds a captive star with a swarm, and eventually a sphere, of collectors.

block:einstein_ring_ore#lore.text: Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Einstein Ring Lens when mined with iron pickaxe or better.

block:einstein_rosen_bridge#lore.text: A wormhole made solid: one mouth here, the other somewhere far away, joined by a throat through curved spacetime. Peering into it, I see the far side foreshortened and tinted.

block:ejecta_cache#lore.text: Thrown out of a white hole with everything else. A white hole is a black hole run backwards: nothing can enter, so this has never been opened from outside.

block:ejecta_ore#lore.text: Found in the White Hole Interior, between Y 0 and 256. Gives Primordial Ejecta when mined with diamond pickaxe or better.

block:ejecta_rock#lore.text: Stone thrown outward from somewhere nothing should leave. Its grains are shocked and blistered, as if fired out of a white hole, and the strata run backwards: newest at the bottom, oldest on top.

block:electrolytic_cell#lore.text: Two electrodes in a conducting liquid: drive a current through it and it comes apart into what it was made of.

block:entangled_relay#lore.text: Two halves of a quantum pair, each locked inside a small housing. Whatever happens to one is correlated with the other, however far apart they sit.

block:entangled_transceiver#lore.text: Sends to (or receives from) every other transceiver on the same channel, at any distance. Sneak-use to switch between sending and receiving; an Entanglement Tuner sets the channel.

block:entanglement_node#lore.text: A junction that keeps entangled pairs until they are wanted. Their correlations are perfect, yet no message can ride on them: no-signalling sees to that.

block:entropy_horizon#lore.text: A ring of event-horizon casing that runs a universe forward to its end: stars burn out, protons decay, black holes evaporate, and the horizon glows at its own faint temperature over what is left.

block:entropy_sink#lore.text: A copper heat sink for computation. By Landauer's principle every bit erased gives off at least kT ln 2 of heat, and something has to carry it away.

block:er_epr_weaver#lore.text: Shares the halves of entangled pairs between two distant mouths - weaving, if Maldacena and Susskind are right, a wormhole between them.

block:eschaton_foundry#lore.text: A sphere of Pleroma glass on a waist of Omnipotence casing, ringed in Logos coil and watched by four towers. It packs as much as the laws allow into as little space as they allow - right up to the edge of becoming a black hole - and repeats what you once forged by hand.

block:essence_distillery#lore.text: A tower of fractionation trays wound with chronosteel coils. Pour in every fluid one mod has and it boils them together, tray after tray, until what is left is a single fluid that stands for all of them: that mod's Essence.

block:euclid_reliquary#lore.text: A casket laid out in Euclid's proportions. The Elements rest on five postulates, and the fifth, on parallel lines, was doubted for two thousand years.

block:evaporator_shield#lore.text: Lead-lined housing for a radioactive evaporator. The water boils away cleanly; everything dangerous it carried stays behind, and stays concentrated.

block:event_horizon_casing#lore.text: A casing with a dark metamaterial skin over spacetime casing and neutronium plate: whatever reaches it from inside does not come back out.

block:evolution_engine#lore.text: A biodome where generations of designed life live and die in seconds. Run it inside a fast chronal field and a million years pass in a minute.

block:ex_nihilo_engine#lore.text: Creation from nothing, made a machine. It does not convert energy - it simply has it.

block:exhaust_stack#lore.text: A tall brick chimney. The hot gas inside is lighter than the air outside, so the taller the stack, the harder it draws.

block:exotic_matter#lore.text: Exotic Matter, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:exotic_solder#lore.text: Exotic Solder, loose in the world. An empty Containment Cell scoops it up.

block:extreme_assembly_table#lore.text: A crafting table with a 9x9 grid, for the recipes too large for any other.

block:eye_of_the_horizon#lore.text: A captive black hole wrapped in anchors, lenses and stabilisers, used as a computer: it simulates entire stars, galaxies and universes, and keeps what falls out.
